semin-durr:31-31.t:
«تَزْدَري» is tafṭaʿil (the iftiʿāl pattern) from زرى يَزْري, i.e. "to hold in contempt"; the tāʾ of iftiʿāl was changed into a dāl after the zāy, and this is regular (muṭṭarid). One says «زَرَيْتُ عليه» when you find fault with him, and «أَزْرَيْتُ به», i.e. "I belittled him". The returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) of the relative noun is omitted, i.e. "whom your eyes تَزْدَريهم", i.e. hold in contempt and belittle. The poet said:
2656 - تَرَى الرجلَ النحيفَ فَتَزْدَريه ... وفي أثوابهِ أسدٌ هَصُورُ
(You see the slender man and hold him in contempt, while within his garments is a crushing lion.)
And he also said:
2657 - يباعِدُه الصَّديقُ وتَزْدريهِ حَلِيْلتُه ... ويَنْهرَهُ الصغيرُ
(His friend keeps away from him, his wife holds him in contempt, and the little one rebuffs him.)
The lām in «للذين» is for causation (taʿlīl), i.e. "for the sake of those who", and it cannot be the lām of conveyance (tablīgh: addressing), because if it were, the regular form would have been «لن يؤتيكم» in the second person.
His words: {وَلاَ أَعْلَمُ الغيب}: the apparent view is that this clause has no grammatical position, being conjoined to his words {وَلاَ أَقُولُ لَكُمْ}, as though he were informing about himself with these [three clauses]. It has already been stated in al-Anʿām [that this is the preferred view], and that al-Zamakhsharī said: "His words, the Exalted, {وَلاَ أَعْلَمُ الغيب} are conjoined to «عندي خزائن», i.e. I do not say: I have the treasuries of Allah, nor do I say: I know the unseen."

semin-durr:32-32.t:
His words, the Exalted: {جِدَالَنَا}: Ibn ʿAbbās read «جَدَلنا», as in His words {أَكْثَرَ شَيْءٍ جَدَلاً} [al-Kahf: 54]. Abū al-Baqāʾ reported that it was read «جَدَلْتَنا فأَكْثرت جَدَلَنَا» without an alif in both; he said: "and it means: you have overcome us in disputation."
His words: {بِمَا تَعِدُنَآ}: «ما» may mean "that which", in which case the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. تَعِدَناه ("which you promise us"). It may also be maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), i.e. "your promise to us". As for his words «إنْ كنت», its apodosis (jawāb) is either omitted or placed before it, namely «فَأْتِنا».

semin-durr:34-34.t:
His words, the Exalted: {إِنْ أَرَدْتُّ أَنْ أَنصَحَ لَكُمْ إِن كَانَ}: The ruling on two consecutive conditions has already been given: that the second of them is a restriction (qayd) on the first, and that it must occur before the first. Al-Zamakhsharī said here: "«إن كان اللَّه»: its apodosis (jazāʾ) is what is indicated by his words «لا ينفعكم نُصْحي», and this indicator is in the same status as what it indicates, so it was joined to a condition, just as the apodosis is joined to the condition in the saying «إنْ أَحْسَنْتَ إليَّ أحسنتُ إليك إنْ أمكنني» (If you do good to me, I will do good to you, if I am able)."
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The rule when a condition enters upon a condition is that the second condition together with the apodosis is the apodosis of the first condition, as in «إنْ أَتَيْتني إنْ كلَّمتني أَكْرَمْتك» (If you come to me, if you speak to me, I will honour you): your saying «إنْ كَلَّمْتني أكرمتُك», the whole of what follows, is the apodosis of «إن أتيتني». That being so, the first condition, while mentioned first, becomes later in meaning, so that if he came to him and then spoke to him, honouring would not be required; but if he spoke to him and then came to him, honouring would be required. The reason for this is that the apodosis has become held back by the second condition. An instance of this occurs in the Qurʾān: {إِن وَهَبَتْ نَفْسَهَا لِلنَّبِيِّ إِنْ أَرَادَ النبي} [al-Aḥzāb: 50]."
I say: as for his words «إنْ وَهَبَتْ ... أن أراد», its apparent sense, and the apparent sense of the narrated story, indicate that it is not a condition that the second condition precede the first. That is because his (upon him be peace) wish to marry is only consequent upon the woman's giving herself to him; and so too what happened in the story: when she gave herself, he wished to marry her; it is not narrated that he wished to marry her and then she gave herself. This needs an answer, and it will come, if Allah wills, in its place.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said here: "My counsel to you is not of benefit, nor is my wishing good for you of any avail, if Allah the Exalted wishes to lead you astray. The second condition is a parenthesis (iʿtirāḍ) within the speech, and it has eloquence in the pairing of the two wills, and in that the will of human beings is of no avail. This condition is attached to «بنصحي», and the other is attached to «لا ينفع»."
What emerges from this is that the [first] condition has its apodosis indicated by his words «ولا ينفعكم», because it follows it, and the apodosis of the second is likewise what indicated the apodosis of the first; as if the implied form were: "And if I wish to counsel you, if Allah wishes to lead you astray, my counsel will not benefit you." In terms of meaning, it is like the condition when it comes with the fāʾ, as in: "If Allah wishes to lead you astray, then if I wish to counsel you, my counsel will not benefit you."
The majority read «نُصْحي» with ḍamma on the nūn, and this admits two possibilities: first, that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), like الشُّكر and الكُفْر; second, that it is a noun, not a maṣdar. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read «نَصْحي» with fatḥa on the nūn, and this is only a maṣdar.
In the course of al-Zamakhsharī's words there is: «إذا عرف اللَّهُ» ("when Allah knows [lit. recognises]"), and this is not permissible, because this verb is not ascribed to Allah the Exalted, nor is He described by its meaning; the reason for this has been given more than once. And in the course of the words of the Shaykh [i.e. Abū Ḥayyān]: "The Muʿtazilī may say: it is not necessary that «إنْ» be conditional; rather it is negative, and the meaning is: Allah was not wishing to lead you astray." I say: I do not think anyone would accept this statement, even if it agrees with his school.

semin-durr:35-35.t:
His words, the Exalted: {فَعَلَيَّ إِجْرَامِي}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), or a verb and its fāʿil (agent). The majority read the hamza of «إجرامي» with kasra; it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of أجرم, and أجرم is the widespread form, though the triliteral جَرَمَ is also permissible; they recited:
2658 - طَريدُ عشيرةٍ ورهينُ ذَنْبٍ ... بما جَرَمت يَدي وجَنَى لساني
(An outcast of my clan and hostage to a sin, for what my hand committed and my tongue brought on.)
It was read, among the irregular (shādhdh) readings, «أجرامي» with fatḥa; al-Naḥḥās reported it and explained it as the plural of جُرْم, like قُفْل / أَقْفال, the meaning being "my sins".

semin-durr:36-36.t:
His words, the Exalted: {وَأُوحِيَ}: the majority read «أُوحي» as passive (mabnī lil-mafʿūl), and what stands in place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil) is «أنه لن يؤمن», i.e. what was revealed to him was the non-belief of some. Abū al-Barahsam read «أوحى» as active, its agent being Allah the Exalted, with «إنه» with kasra on the hamza. There are two views on it, the first of them — and it is a principle of the Basrans — being that it is by treating revelation (īḥāʾ) as equivalent to speech (qawl). [Translator's note: the second view is not stated in the source.]
His words: {فَلاَ تَبْتَئِسْ}: it is tafṭaʿil from البُؤْس, and its meaning is grief accompanied by submissiveness. One says: ابتأسَ فلانٌ, i.e. something he dislikes reached him. [The poet] said:
2659 - ما يَقْسِمِ اللَّهُ أَقْبَلْ غيرَ مُبْتَئِسٍ ... منه وأقْعُدْ كريماً ناعمَ البالِ
(Whatever Allah apportions, I accept without grieving over it, and I remain noble, with a contented mind.)
And another said:
2660 - وكم مِنْ خليلٍ أو حَميمٍ رُزِئْتُه ... فلم نَبْتَئِس والرُّزْء فيه جَليل
(How many a friend or close kinsman have I been bereaved of, yet we did not grieve, though the loss of him was great.)

semin-durr:37-37.t: His words, the Exalted: {بِأَعْيُنِنَا}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «اصنع», i.e. "protected by Our eyes"; it is a figurative expression (majāz) for Allah's addressing him with protection. It was also said: what is meant by them is the angels, likening them to the "eyes" of people, i.e. those who keep watch over news; in that case the plural is literal. Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read «بأعيُنَّا» with assimilation (idghām).

semin-durr:38-38.t: His words, the Exalted: {وَكُلَّمَا مَرَّ}: what governs «كلما» is «سَخِر», and «قال» is resumptive (mustaʾnaf), since it is the answer to an implied question. It was also said: rather, what governs «كلما» is «قال», and «سخروا» on this view is either an adjective (ṣifa) of مَلأ or a badal (substitute) from «مرَّ»; and this is very far-fetched, since «سَخِرَ» is neither a kind of passing nor the same as it, so how could it substitute for it? The clause from his words «كلما» to its end is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "he builds the ship, the situation being that whenever … passed".

semin-durr:39-39.t:
His words, the Exalted: {مَن يَأْتِيهِ}: there are two views on «مَنْ»: first, that it is a relative noun (mawṣūla); second, that it is interrogative. On both assumptions, «تعلمون» is either of the category of certainty (yaqīn), so it takes two objects, or of the category of recognition (ʿirfān), so it takes one. If it is of recognition and «مَنْ» is interrogative, then «مَنْ» with what follows it stands in place of one object; and if it takes two objects, it stands in place of both objects. If «تعلمون» takes two objects and «مَنْ» is a relative noun, it is in the position of the first object and the second is omitted. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It may be the one that takes two objects, contenting itself with one." This expression is not good, because contenting oneself (iqtiṣār) with one of the two objects in this category is not permissible, for what has been established more than once — that they are originally a mubtadaʾ and khabar. As for omission for brevity (ḥadhf al-ikhtiṣār), it is also impossible here, since there is no indicator of it. If it takes one object and «مَنْ» is a relative noun, then its case is clear.
Al-Zahrāwī reported: «ويَحُلُّ» with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ, meaning "becomes due".
«التنور» is well known [i.e. the oven]. It was also said: it is the face of the earth. Is the al in it for something known (ʿahd) or for the genus (jins)? As for the pattern of تَنُّور, it was said: it is tafʿūl from the root of النور; the first wāw was changed into a hamza because of its ḍamma, then it was dropped for lightness, then they doubled the nūn as a kind of compensation for what was dropped; this is attributed to Thaʿlab. It was also said: its pattern is faʿʿūl, and this is attributed to Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī. It was also said: it is non-Arabic (aʿjamī), and on this view it has no derivation. The well-known view is that it is among the words in which the language of the Arabs and the non-Arabs coincide, like الصابون (soap).

semin-durr:40-40.t:
His words, the Exalted: {مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ}: the generality of readers read «كل» in a genitive construct (iḍāfa) with «زوجين». Ḥafṣ read «كل» with tanwīn (nunation). As for the generality's reading, it was said: the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «احمل» is «اثنين», and {مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنٍ} is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object, because it was an adjective of the indefinite noun, and when it was placed before it, it was made accusative as a ḥāl. It was also said: rather, «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida), «كل» is the direct object, and «اثنين» is a naʿt (adjective) of «زوجين» for emphasis; but this only holds on the view of those who hold that «مِنْ» can be redundant absolutely, or in an affirmative statement. It was also said: his words «زوجين» have a general meaning, i.e. "of everything that has pairing"; this is the meaning of His words {مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنٍ}, and it is the view of al-Fārisī and others. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "If the meaning were: carry in it, of every two existing spouses, two, he would have had to carry four of every kind; and زوج in their well-known usage is for one of what has pairing."
As for Ḥafṣ's reading, its meaning is "of every animal", «زوجين» is the direct object, «اثنين» is an adjective for emphasis, and «مِنْ كلٍ» on this reading may be attached to «احمل», which is the apparent view, or attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «زوجين». This disagreement and analysis apply also in the sura {قَدْ أَفْلَحَ} [al-Muʾminūn: 27].
His words: {وَأَهْلَكَ}: conjoined (nasaq) to «اثنين» in the reading of those who put «كل» in construct with «زوجين», and to «زوجين» in the reading of those who gave «كلاً» tanwīn. His words {إِلاَّ مَن سَبَقَ} are a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil) in an affirmative statement, so it must be accusative according to the well-known view.
His words: {وَمَنْ آمَنَ}: a direct object, conjoined to the object of «احمِلْ».

semin-durr:41-41.t:
His words, the Exalted: {وَقَالَ}: the fāʿil (agent) may be the pronoun of Nūḥ, upon him be peace, or the pronoun of the Creator, the Exalted, i.e. "and Allah said to Nūḥ and those with him". «فيها» is attached to «اركبوا», and it was made transitive with «في» because it implies the meaning of «ادخلوا فيها راكبين» ("enter it riding") or «سيروا فيها» ("travel in it"). It was also said: its implied form is "ride the water in it". It was also said: «في» is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis.
His words: {بِسْمِ الله}: this preposition and its genitive noun may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «اركبوا» or from the «ها» in «فيها», and «مجراها» and «مرساها» are then agents of the notion of "being settled" (istiqrār) implied by the preposition, because it occurs as a ḥāl. It is also possible that «بسم اللَّه» is a fronted khabar (predicate) and «مَجْراها» a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), the clause likewise being a ḥāl from what preceded; on both assumptions it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara). This is how Abū al-Baqāʾ and others parsed it. Makkī, however, rejected that, because the clause lacks a pronoun returning to the one the ḥāl describes, if we parse the clause or the preposition as a ḥāl from the agent of «اركبوا». He said: "It is not good for this clause to be a ḥāl from the agent of «اركبوا», because there is no returning element in the clause referring to the pronoun in «اركبوا»; for the pronoun in «بسم اللَّه», if you make it the predicate of «مَجْراها», only refers to the subject, which is مجراها; and if you make «مجراها» nominative by the adverbial phrase, it contains no pronoun, and the hāʾ in «مجراها» only refers to the pronoun in «فيها». But if you make «مجراها» accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf), «بسم اللَّه» governs it, and the clause is a ḥāl from the agent of «اركبوا»."
It was also said: {بِسْمِ الله} is a ḥāl from the agent of «اركبوا», and مَجْراها and مُرْساها are in the position of an adverbial of place or of time, the implied form being: "ride in it, naming [Allah] at the place of its running and its anchoring", or "at the time of its running and its anchoring". The governor of these two adverbials is then the notion of "being settled" implied by «بسم اللَّه», the implied form being: "ride in it, seeking blessing by the name of Allah at these two places or times." Makkī said: "It is not permissible for what governs them to be «اركبوا», because he did not mean: ride in it at the time of running and anchoring; the meaning is only: mention the name of Allah at the time of running and anchoring."
It is also possible that «مَجْراها ومُرْساها» are maṣdars (verbal nouns) and «بسم اللَّه» a ḥāl as stated before, making these two maṣdars nominative as agents, i.e. "its being made to run and its being made to anchor are settled by the name of Allah"; in that case the preposition can only be a ḥāl from the «ها» in «فيها», because of the presence of the linking element (rābiṭ), and it cannot be a ḥāl from the agent of «اركبوا», because of the absence of the linking element.
On these parsings the speech is a single sentence. It is also possible that {بِسْمِ الله مجراها وَمُرْسَاهَا} is a resumptive (mustaʾnafa) clause with no connection to the first in terms of grammar: he commanded them in the first clause to ride, and informed them that its running and its anchoring are by the name of Allah. In the tafsīr: when he said «بسم اللَّه» it stopped, and when he said it, it ran, according to what he wished; so the two clauses are reported speech governed by «قال».
The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Ḥafṣ read «مَجْراها» with fatḥa on the mīm, and the rest with ḍamma. The Seven agreed on ḍamma on the mīm of «مُرْساها». Ibn Masʿūd, ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī, Zayd ibn ʿAlī and al-Aʿmash read «مَرْساها» with fatḥa on the mīm as well. The ḍamma in both is because they are from أَجْرى and أرسى, and the fatḥa because they are from جَرَتْ and رَسَتْ; and they are either adverbials of time or place, or maṣdars, according to the implied forms already given.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Nakhaʿī, Ibn Waththāb, Mujāhid, Abū Rajāʾ, al-Kalbī, al-Jaḥdarī and Ibn Jundab read «مُجْرِيها ومُرْسِيها» with kasra on the rāʾ followed by an explicit yāʾ; they are two active participles from أجرى and أَرْسى, and they are explained as two badals (substitutes) from the name of Allah. Ibn ʿAṭiyya, Abū al-Baqāʾ and Makkī said: they are two naʿts (adjectives) of Allah the Exalted. What they mentioned only holds on the assumption that they are definite through the annexation being pure (maḥḍa); and al-Khalīl said: "Every impure annexation may be made pure, except the annexation of the ṣifa mushabbaha (assimilated adjective), which does not become pure."
Makkī said: "If «مجراها» and «مرساها» were put in the position of an active participle, they would be an anticipated ḥāl, and that would be permissible, and you would put them in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the name of Allah the Exalted." I say: Makkī, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, spoke at length on this question, and said at its end: "Through this question one comes to understand everything like it in speech and in the Qurʾān — that is, for one who understands it as it should be understood and reflects on it as it should be reflected upon; for it is among the choicest of difficult questions."
His words: {وَهِيَ تَجْرِي}: there are three views on this clause. First, that it is resumptive: Allah the Exalted informs about the ship with this. Second, that it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in «بسم اللَّه», i.e. its running is settled by the name of Allah while it is running. Third, that it is a ḥāl from something omitted, contained in a clause indicated by the context of the speech. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: to what are His words {وَهِيَ تَجْرِي بِهِمْ} connected? I say: to something omitted, indicated by His words {اركبوا فِيهَا بِسْمِ الله}, as if it were said: so they rode in it, saying: in the name of Allah, while it ran with them."
His words: {بِهِمْ}: two views are possible: first, that it is attached to «تَجْري»; second, that it is attached to an omitted element, i.e. "it runs bearing them"; and for that reason al-Zamakhsharī explained it by saying: "i.e. it runs while they are in it."
الرُّسُوُّ is firmness and settledness; one says رَسَا يَرْسُو, and أَرْسَيْتُه (I anchored it). [The poet] said:
2661 - فَصَبَرْتُ نَفْساً عند ذلك حُرَّةً ... تَرْسُو إذا نفسُ الجبان تَطَلَّعُ
(So I held firm, at that moment, a free-born soul that stays anchored when the coward's soul leaps up.)
i.e. it stands firm and settled when the coward's soul is agitated and moves.

semin-durr:42-42.t:
His words, the Exalted: {كالجبال}: an adjective (ṣifa) of «مَوْج». His words: «نوحٌ ابنَه»: the majority read the tanwīn of «نوح» with kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Wakīʿ read it with ḍamma, following the vowel of the case-ending. Abū Ḥātim considered this reading base and said: "It is a bad dialect that is not known."
The generality read «ابنه» connecting the hāʾ of the pronoun with a wāw [in pronunciation], and this is the eloquent, widespread usage. Ibn ʿAbbās read it with sukūn on the hāʾ. Some said: "This is restricted to poetic necessity," and recited:
2662 - وأَشْربُ الماء ما بيْ نحوَه عَطَشٌ ... إلا لأنَّ عيونَهُ سيلُ واديها
(And I drink the water though I have no thirst for it, only because its springs are the torrent of her valley.)
Some do not restrict it to that. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: it is a dialect of Azd al-Sarāt, and from it is the saying:
2663 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ومِطْوايَ مُشْتاقان لَهْ أَرِقانِ
(… and my two companions long for him, sleepless.)
Some said: "It is the dialect of ʿUqayl and Banū Kilāb."
Al-Suddī read «ابناهْ» with an alif and the hāʾ of pause (hāʾ al-sakt). Ibn Jinnī said: "It is in the vocative." Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "ابناه is by way of lamenting (tarathhī) and is not nudba (the lament of the vocative), because nudba does not occur with the hamza." This statement is problematic in itself: where is the hamza here? If he meant the hamza of the vocative, we do not grant that the implied vocative particle is the hamza, because the grammarians have stated explicitly that no vocative particle is implied except «يا», since it is the mother of the category. And his word "tarathhī" is close in meaning to nudba; and they have stated explicitly that it is not permissible to omit the vocative particle from the one lamented (mandūb), and this resembles it.
ʿAlī, upon him be peace, read «ابنها», annexing it to his wife, as if he took into account His words «ليس من أهلك». And his words «ابني» and «من أهلي» are no evidence against it, since that may be out of tenderness; this is the view of al-Ḥasan and a group.
Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, ʿUrwa and al-Zubayr read «ابْنَهَ» with a hāʾ with fatḥa and no alif; it is like the preceding reading, except that he dropped the alif of «ها», making do with the fatḥa in its place, just as the yāʾ is dropped making do with the kasra. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is a dialect," and recited:
2664 - أمَا تقودُ بها شاةً فتأكلُها ... أو أنْ تبيعَهَ في بعض الأراكيبِ
(Will you not lead a sheep with it and eat it, or sell it among some of the caravans?)
He means «تبيعَها», making do with the fatḥa instead of the alif, just as another made do without it in his saying — Ibn al-Aʿrābī recited it for this point:
2665 - فلستُ براجعٍ ما فاتَ مني ... بِلَهْفَ ولا بِلَيْتَ ولا لوَاني
(I will not bring back what has escaped me by "alas!", nor by "would that", nor by "if only I had".)
He means يا لَهْفا, and dropped [the alif]. Some restrict this to poetic necessity and forbid, in free speech, يا غلامَ for يا غلاما. I say: it will come, regarding the like of «يا أبتَ» with fatḥa, whether there is an omitted alif there or not; and we have already given the disagreement about the like of يابنَ أمَّ and يابنَ عَمَّ: is there an omitted alif there, the fatḥa standing in for it, or not? This too is like that; but the apparent view is that it is not to be used as a basis for analogy.
Al-Naḥḥās held Abū Ḥātim to be wrong regarding the dropping of this alif, and this is open to consideration (fīhi naẓar).
His words: {وَكَانَ فِي مَعْزِلٍ}: a clause in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the one it describes is «ابنه»; the ḥāl may come from the one addressed in the vocative (munādā) because it is an object. المَعْزِل with kasra on the zāy is the noun of the place of isolation, and likewise the noun of time; with fatḥa it is the maṣdar. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "I do not know anyone who read it with fatḥa." I say: because the maṣdar neither contains him nor is his location, so how could it be read thus except by a far-fetched figurative usage?
Al-Bazzī, Qālūn and Khallād read the yāʾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the letter concerned is the bāʾ] of «اركب» distinctly (iẓhār) before the mīm of «معنا», with a disagreement reported from them, and the rest with assimilation (idghām). ʿĀṣim read here «يا بنيَّ» with fatḥa on the yāʾ. As for elsewhere than this sura, Ḥafṣ, from him, did that, while the rest read with kasra on the yāʾ throughout the Qurʾān, except Ibn Kathīr in the first of Luqmān, namely His words {لاَ تُشْرِكْ بالله} [Luqmān: 13], where he gave it sukūn both in continuous reading and in pause; in the second he is like the others, i.e. he gives its yāʾ kasra, while Ḥafṣ keeps to his principle of fatḥa. In the third, namely His words {يابني أَقِمِ الصلاة} [Luqmān: 17], there is disagreement from him: al-Bazzī related from him the like of Ḥafṣ, and Qunbul related from him sukūn as in the first. This is the precise record of the reading.
As for its explanation: for those who read fatḥa, it was said: its origin is يا بُنَيَّا with an alif, and the alif was dropped for lightness, making do with the fatḥa in its place; many examples of this have preceded. It was also said: rather, it was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, since the rāʾ of «اركب» comes after it; and this is a very corrupt explanation, as shown by its absence in the sura of Luqmān in three places where there are no two quiescent letters. It is as though the one giving this explanation did not know of ʿĀṣim's reading outside this sura, nor of al-Bazzī's reading of the last in Luqmān; Abū al-Baqāʾ reported it and did not object to it.
As for those who read kasra, the yāʾ was also dropped: either for lightness, which is correct, or because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, whose corruptness has already been shown. As for those who read sukūn, it is because of the heaviness they saw with any vowel at all, and there is no doubt that sukūn is lighter than the lightest of vowels. And one should not say: why then did Ibn Kathīr agree with those other than Ḥafṣ in the second of Luqmān, agree with Ḥafṣ in the last in al-Bazzī's transmission from him, and give the first sukūn? Because that combines the dialects, and the one who differentiates brings an impossibility.
The origin of this word has three yāʾs: the first is for the diminutive; the second is the final radical (lām) of the word — and whether it is a yāʾ originally or changed from a wāw is a disagreement whose verification has preceded at the beginning of this topic, on what the final radical of «ابن» is; and the third is the yāʾ of the speaker to which it is annexed, which is the one that underwent change into an alif and then dropping, or dropping while remaining a yāʾ.

semin-durr:43-43.t:
His words, the Exalted: {لاَ عَاصِمَ اليوم}: there are several views. First, that it is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ): that is, you take عاصم in its literal sense, and the one on whom He has mercy is the one protected; in «رَحِم» there is a nominative pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted, and its object is the pronoun of the relative noun «مَنْ», omitted because the conditions are fulfilled; the implied form is: "there is no protector at all today from the command of Allah; but whoever Allah has mercy on, he is protected." Second, that what is meant by «مَنْ رَحِم» is the Creator, the Exalted, as if it were said: "there is no protector today except the Merciful." Third, that عاصم means مَعْصوم (protected); the active pattern fāʿil sometimes comes in the sense of the passive mafʿūl, as in ماء دافق, i.e. مدفوق ("poured"); they recited:
2666 - بطيءُ القيامِ رخيمُ الكلا ... مِ أَمْسى فؤادي به فاتِنا
(Slow in rising, soft of speech: my heart has become captivated [lit. captivating] by her.)
i.e. مفتوناً (captivated); and «مَنْ» refers to the one protected, the implied form being: "none is protected today from the command of Allah except the one on whom Allah has mercy, for he is protected." Fourth, that «عاصم» here expresses relation (nasab), i.e. "possessing protection", as in لابن (possessor of milk) and تامر (possessor of dates); and "possessor of protection" applies both to the protector and to the protected, and what is meant here is the protected.
On these assumptions it is a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil). Al-Zamakhsharī made it connected by another route, namely the omission of a muḍāf, its implied form being: "No place of refuge — a mountain or the like — will protect you today at all except one place of refuge, namely the place of those on whom Allah has had mercy and whom He has saved," meaning in the ship.
As for the khabar (predicate) of «لا», it is best taken as omitted, because when there is an indicator of it, its omission is obligatory among Tamīm and frequent among the Ḥijāzīs; the implied form is: "there is no protector existing." Al-Ḥūfī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya permitted its predicate to be the adverbial, namely اليوم. Al-Ḥūfī said: "It is possible that «اليوم» is the predicate, so that it is attached to the notion of being settled (istiqrār), and {مِنْ أَمْرِ الله} is attached to it." Abū al-Baqāʾ rejected this and said: "As for the predicate of «لا», it cannot be «اليوم», because an adverbial of time is not a predicate about a concrete entity (juththa); rather the predicate is {مِنْ أَمْرِ الله}, and «اليوم» is governed by {مِنْ أَمْرِ الله}."
As for «اليومَ» and {مِنْ أَمْرِ الله}, it has been stated that some made one of them the predicate, the other then being attached to the notion of being settled implied by the one occurring as predicate. «اليوم» may also be attached to {مِنْ أَمْرِ الله} itself, since it has the sense of a verb. Al-Ḥūfī permitted «اليوم» to be an adjective of «عاصم», and this is corrupt for the same reason that its occurring as a predicate about concrete entities is corrupt.
It was read {إِلاَّ مَن رَّحِمَ} as passive, and this strengthens the view of those who claim that «مَنْ رَحِم» in the generality's reading means the one shown mercy, not the one showing mercy, as its interpretation has been given above. Neither «اليوم» nor {مِنْ أَمْرِ الله} may be attached to «عاصم», nor either one of them, because the noun would then be "lengthened" (muṭawwal), and whenever it is lengthened it is declinable, and whenever it is declinable it takes tanwīn; and no account is taken of al-Zajjāj's dissent, where he claimed that the noun of «لا» is declinable, its tanwīn being dropped for lightness.

semin-durr:44-44.t:
His words, the Exalted: {ابلعي}: البَلْع (swallowing) is well known. Its verb has the middle radical with kasra and with fatḥa: بَلِعَ and بَلَعَ; al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ reported both. الإِقلاع is holding back, and from it is «أَقْلَعَت الحمى» ("the fever abated"). It was also said: أقلع عن الشيء, i.e. he left it, and this is close to the first. الغَيْض is diminishing, and its verb is intransitive and transitive. Of the intransitive is His words, the Exalted: {وَمَا تَغِيضُ الأرحام} [al-Raʿd: 8], i.e. diminish — though it was also said: rather, it is transitive there too, and this will come. Of the transitive is this verse, because a verb is not made passive without the mediation of a preposition unless it is transitive by itself.
الجُودِيُّ is a particular mountain at al-Mawṣil. It was also said: rather, every mountain is called جُودي; and from this is the saying of ʿAmr ibn Nufayl:
2667 - سبحانَه ثم سُبْحاناً نعوذُ به ... وقبلَنا سَبَّح الجُودِيُّ والجُمُدُ
(Glory be to Him, and again glory — we seek refuge in Him; before us al-Jūdī and al-Jumud glorified Him.)
I do not know what in that indicates that it is general for every mountain. Al-Aʿmash and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «الجُوْدِيْ» with the [yāʾ] lightened. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "They are two dialects." The correct thing to say is: the yāʾ of relation (nisba) was lightened, even though that is not permissible in their widespread speech.
His words: {بُعْداً}: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) by an implied verb, i.e. "and it was said: perish, a perishing", so it is a maṣdar in the sense of an imprecation against them, like جَدْعاً. One says بَعِد يَبْعَد بَعَداً when one perishes. [The poet] said:
2668 - يقولون لا تَبْعَدْ وهم يَدْفِنونه ... ولا بُعْدَ إلا ما تُواري الصَّفائحُ
(They say "do not perish!" while they bury him — yet there is no perishing but what the grave-slabs conceal.)
The lām is either attached to an omitted verb, being by way of clarification (bayān), as stated before regarding the like of «سَقْياً لك ورَعْياً», or attached to قيل, i.e. "this saying was for them".
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its account came with verbs in the passive to indicate majesty and grandeur, and that those mighty matters can only come about by the act of an All-Powerful One and the bringing-into-being of an Overwhelming Bringer-into-being, and that the doer of these acts is a single doer who has no partner in His acts; so the imagination cannot go so far as to suppose that another said: O earth, swallow your water, or that anyone but He decreed that tremendous matter, or that the ship settled upon al-Jūdī and rested on it except by His settling and establishing it. Because of the meanings and subtleties we have mentioned, the scholars of rhetoric (bayān) deemed this verse supremely eloquent and swayed their heads to it — not because of the paronomasia (tajānus) of the two words, namely His words ابلعي and أقلعي; for that, even if the speech is not devoid of beauty from it, is as if unnoticed beside those beauties which are the kernel, while everything else is husks." He means that some people counted the paronomasia among the eloquence of the verse, so he said that this is of no great value in comparison with the meanings he mentioned; and by my life, he spoke the truth.
When the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] reported this splendid passage from him, his only reward for it from him was: "most of it is oratory."
Al-Zamakhsharī's saying «ورقَصوا لها رؤوسهم» ("and swayed their heads to it") may refer to what is related: that a group of the eloquent men of their time gathered in the pilgrimage season at ʿArafa and dispersed on the understanding that each of them would compose a counterpart to something of the Qurʾān, to test their powers in eloquence; they dispersed on the understanding that they would gather the following year. One of them — it was said he was Ibn al-Muqaffaʿ — opened the codex and found this verse, and shrank back before it and submitted, and said: "No one is able to produce the like of this."

semin-durr:45-45.t: His words, the Exalted: {فَقَالَ}: conjoined to «نادى». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: if the calling is His words «رَبّ», how is «فقال ربِّ» conjoined to «نادى» with the fāʾ? I say: what is meant by the calling is the intention to call; had the calling itself been meant, it would have come as it came in His words {إِذْ نادى رَبَّهُ نِدَآءً خَفِيّاً}: «قال ربِّ», without a fāʾ."

semin-durr:46-46.t:
His words, the Exalted: {عَمَلٌ غَيْرُ صَالِحٍ}: al-Kisāʾī read «عَمِل» as a past verb and «غيرَ» in the accusative; the rest read «عَمَلٌ» with fatḥa on the mīm and tanwīn, as a noun, and «غيرُ» in the nominative. In al-Kisāʾī's reading, the pronoun must refer to the son of Nūḥ; the fāʿil (agent) of «عمل» is a pronoun referring to him as well, and «غيرَ» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). It may also be a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being: "he did a deed not righteous", as in His words {واعملوا صَالِحاً} [al-Muʾminūn: 51].
As for the reading of the rest, there are several views on the pronoun. The most apparent is that it refers to the son of Nūḥ, and in predicating a maṣdar (verbal noun) of him there are the three positions [known] regarding «رجل عدل» ("a just man", lit. "a man [who is] justice"). Second, that it refers to the calling understood from his words «ونادى», i.e. "your calling and your asking"; Abū al-Baqāʾ, Makkī and al-Zamakhsharī took this view. This carries a grave danger: how can this be said of one of the prophets, let alone the first messenger sent to the people of the earth after Ādam, upon them both be peace? When Abū al-Qāsim [al-Zamakhsharī] reported it, he said: "and it is not quite so," and he was right. Those who held this view adduced that in the codex (ḥarf) of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd there is «إنه عملٌ غيرُ صالحٍ أن تسألني ما ليس لك به علمٌ», but this contradicts the standard text (al-sawād).
Third, that it refers to the son of Nūḥ's riding, indicated by his words «اركب معنا». Fourth, that it refers to his abandoning riding and being with the believers, i.e. his abandoning riding with the believers and his being with the unbelievers is a deed not righteous. On the [last] three views, predicating the maṣdar needs no interpretation, because both are abstract notions. On the fourth view it is part of the speech of Nūḥ, upon him be peace, i.e. Nūḥ said: "Your being with the unbelievers and your abandoning riding with us is not righteous" — unlike what preceded, which is the speech of Allah the Exalted only. So said Makkī, and this is open to consideration; rather, the apparent view is that all of it is the speech of Allah the Exalted. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why was it not said: it is a corrupt deed? I say: when He denied that he was of his family, He denied to him their attribute with the word of negation with which the wording of what is negated is retained, and announced thereby that He saved those He saved only because of their righteousness, not because they were your family."
His words: {فَلاَ تَسْأَلْنِي}: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read «فلا تسألَنِّ» with a doubled nūn with kasra and no yāʾ; Ibn Kathīr with it doubled and with fatḥa; Abū ʿAmr and the Kufans with a light nūn with kasra, with a yāʾ in continuous reading [for Abū ʿAmr] and without a yāʾ [in both states] for the Kufans. In al-Kahf, {فَلاَ تَسْأَلْني عَن شَيءٍ} [verse 70], Abū ʿAmr and the Kufans read as they read here, and Ibn Kathīr agreed with them in al-Kahf; Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read as they read here, and there is disagreement from Ibn Dhakwān on retaining or dropping the yāʾ. Ibn Kathīr read the one in Hūd with fatḥa, but not the one in al-Kahf, only because the yāʾ in Hūd is dropped in the script, so his reading with fatḥa on the nūn was possible, unlike al-Kahf, where the yāʾ is present in the script, so its fatḥa does not agree with it.
Ibn Dhakwān's disagreement on retaining the yāʾ in al-Kahf has already been mentioned.
Those who read the nūn light take it as the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya) alone; those who doubled it take it as the nūn of emphasis (nūn al-tawkīd). Ibn Kathīr in Hūd did not make the verb connected with the yāʾ of the speaker, while the rest did, so kasra was necessary for them. It has been stated that «سأل» takes two objects, the first being the yāʾ of the speaker and the second {مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ}.
His words: {أَن تَكُونَ}: with omission of the preposition, i.e. "from being" or "for the sake of being". As for His words {مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ}, «به» may be attached to «عِلْم». Al-Fārisī said: "It is then like the saying:
2669 - كان جَزائي بالعَصا أن أُجْلَدا
(My reward was to be flogged with the stick.)"
It may also be attached to the notion of being settled (istiqrār) to which «لك» is attached; the bāʾ then means «في», i.e. "that about which you have no knowledge". This is open to consideration.

semin-durr:47-47.t: His words, the Exalted: {وَإِلاَّ تَغْفِرْ}: «لا» did not prevent the jussive particle from governing, just as it does not prevent a preposition from governing in the like of «جِئْتُ بلا زادٍ» ("I came without provisions"). Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Because it is like a part of the verb, and it does not govern in negation, and it negates what is in the future; «ما» is not like that, for it negates what is in the present, and for that reason «إنْ» may not enter upon it."

semin-durr:48-48.t:
His words, the Exalted: {قِيلَ يانوح}: the disagreement given earlier regarding His words {وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ آمِنُواْ} [al-Baqara: 13] and the like applies here too, i.e. whether what stands in place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil) is the reported clause or the pronoun of the verb's maṣdar.
His words: {بِسَلاَمٍ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «اهبط», i.e. "accompanied by peace". «منا» is an adjective (ṣifa) of «سلام», so it is attached to an omitted element, or it is attached to سلام itself, the beginning of extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya) being figurative. Likewise «عليك» may be an adjective of بركات or attached to it.
His words: {مِّمَّن مَّعَكَ}: «مَنْ» [i.e. مِنْ] may be for the beginning of extent, i.e. "arising from those with you", namely the believing nations to the end of time; or «مِنْ» may be for explaining the genus (bayān al-jins), in which case the nations who were with him in the ship are meant, because they were groups. It was read «اهبُط» with ḍamma on the bāʾ, and this was dealt with at the beginning of al-Baqara. Al-Kisāʾī read, according to what is transmitted from him, «وبركة» in the singular.
His words: {وأُمَمٍ}: it may be a mubtadaʾ (subject), with «سنمتِّعهم» as its khabar (predicate). As for what justifies it as a subject [though indefinite], there are two views. First, an implied description, since the implied form is: "and nations of them", i.e. of those with you, as in their saying «السَّمْن مَنَوان بدرهم» ("ghee: two manns for a dirham"), where منوان is a subject described by «منه» implicitly. Second, that what justifies it is the division into parts (tafṣīl), as in: «الناسُ رجلان: رجلٌ أَهَنْتُ، وآخَرُ أكرمتُ» ("people are two men: a man I insulted and another I honoured"); and of this is the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
2670 - إذا ما بكى مِنْ خَلْفِها انحرفَتْ له ... بشقٍّ وشِقٌّ عندنا لم يُحَوَّل
(Whenever he cried behind her, she turned to him with one half, while one half with us was not turned away.)
It may also be nominative as an agent, conjoined to the latent pronoun in «اهبط», the separation making emphasis by a detached pronoun unnecessary; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. The Shaykh said: "This implied form and meaning are not sound, because those who were with Nūḥ in the ship were only believers, because of His words «ومَنْ آمنَ»; they were not unbelievers and believers, so that the unbelievers would be commanded to descend — unless it is supposed that among the believers were some who would disbelieve after the descent, and they were described by the state they would come to; then it is possible, though far-fetched." I say: it has been stated that the like of this is not permissible, regarding His words {اسكن أَنْتَ وَزَوْجُكَ} [al-Baqara: 35], for a technical reason. On this view «سنمتِّعُهم» is an adjective of «أمم», and the wāw may be for the ḥāl. Al-Akhfash said: "As you say: «كلَّمْتُ زيداً وعمروٌ جالس» (I spoke to Zayd while ʿAmr was sitting)"; and it may be simply for conjunction.

semin-durr:49-49.t: His words, the Exalted: {تِلْكَ مِنْ أَنْبَآءِ الغيب}: like His words {ذلك مِنْ أَنَبَآءِ الغيب} [verse 44] in Āl ʿImrān. His words: {مَا كُنتَ تَعْلَمُهَآ}: this clause may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the kāf in «إليك», or a ḥāl from the object in «نُوحيها», or a khabar (predicate) after a khabar.

semin-durr:50-50.t:
His words, the Exalted: {وإلى عَادٍ أَخَاهُمْ هُوداً}: these two are conjoined to His words {وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحاً إلى قَوْمِهِ} [Hūd: 25]: nominative to nominative [Translator's note: so in the source (مرفوع على مرفوع); «هوداً» and «نوحاً» are in fact accusative] and genitive to genitive, as when you say: «ضرب زيد عمراً وبكر خالداً» ("Zayd struck ʿAmr, and Bakr Khālid"). It is not of the category in which the conjunction and the conjoined are separated by a preposition and its genitive noun, as in «ضربت زيداً وفي السوق عمراً» ("I struck Zayd, and in the market ʿAmr"), so that the well-known disagreement would arise. It was also said: rather, it is by an implied verb, i.e. "and We sent Hūd", and this fits better given the length of the separation. «هوداً» is a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of «أخاهم».
Ibn Muḥayṣin read «يا قومُ» with ḍamma on the mīm; it is a dialect of the Arabs who make a noun annexed to the yāʾ indeclinable on ḍamma, as in His words, the Exalted: {قَالَ رَبِّ احكم} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 112] with ḍamma on the bāʾ. It cannot be other than annexed to the yāʾ, for a reason that will come in its place, if Allah wills.
His words: {مِّنْ إله غَيْرُهُ}: what concerns it, in reading and in parsing, has been mentioned in al-Aʿrāf.

semin-durr:51-51.t: His words, the Exalted: {فطرني}: Nāfiʿ and al-Bazzī read it with fatḥa on the yāʾ, and Abū ʿAmr and Qunbul with sukūn.

semin-durr:52-52.t:
His words, the Exalted: {مِّدْرَاراً}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). It was not made feminine, though it is from a feminine [noun], for three reasons. First, that by السماء the clouds are meant, so it was made masculine according to the meaning. Second, that the pattern mifʿāl is for intensiveness, so masculine and feminine are equal in it, like صبور, شكور and faʿīl. Third, that the hāʾ [of the feminine] was dropped from mifʿāl by way of relation (nasab); Makkī said this, and its explanation has preceded in al-Anʿām.
His words: {إلى قُوَّتِكُمْ}: it may be attached to «يَزِدْكم» by implication (taḍmīn), i.e. "He will add to your strength another strength"; or the preposition and its genitive noun may be made an adjective of «قوة», so it is attached to an omitted element — Abū al-Baqāʾ gave its implied form as «مضافةً إلى قوتكم» ("added to your strength"), but the grammarians reject this, since in such a case they only imply general being (al-kawn al-muṭlaq); or «إلى» may be taken in the sense of "with", i.e. "with your strength", as in His words, the Exalted: {إلى أَمْوَالِكُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 2].

semin-durr:53-53.t:
His words, the Exalted: {بِبَيِّنَةٍ}: the bāʾ may be for making transitive (taʿdiya), so it is attached to the verb before it, i.e. "you have never shown us a clear proof". Second, that it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial), the implied form being: "settled with" or "accompanied by a clear proof".
His words: {عَن قَوْلِكَ}: a ḥāl from the pronoun in «تاركي», i.e. "and we will not leave our gods, proceeding from your word". «عن» may also be for causation (taʿlīl), as it is in His words, the Exalted: {إِلاَّ عَن مَّوْعِدَةٍ وَعَدَهَآ إِيَّاهُ} [al-Tawba: 114], i.e. "except for the sake of a promise". The meaning here is then: "leaving our gods because of your word", so it is attached to تاركي. Ibn ʿAṭiyya alluded to causation, but the preferred view is the first, and al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing else.

semin-durr:54-54.t:
His words, the Exalted: {إِلاَّ اعتراك}: the apparent view is that what follows «إلا» is the object of the verb of saying before it, since what is meant is: "we say nothing but this utterance"; so the clause is reported speech (maḥkiyya), like your saying «ما قلت إلا زيد قائم» ("I said only: Zayd is standing"). Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The clause explains an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), the implied form being: we say nothing but a saying, namely اعتراك; and its position may be accusative, i.e. we mention nothing but this saying." This is not satisfactory, because reporting with a verb of saying is a clear meaning that needs no interpretation, nor does it need the verb of saying to be made to imply the sense of "mentioning".
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«اعتراك» is the object of «نقول», and «إلا» is void (laghw), i.e. we say nothing but our saying «اعتراك»." End of quotation. By his saying "void" he means that it is an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh); and his implied form after that is an explanation of the meaning, not of the parsing, since its apparent sense requires the clause to be accusative by an omitted maṣdar, that maṣdar being accusative by «نقول»; this is the apparent sense. One says: اعتراه بكذا يَعْتريه ("it befell him with such-and-such"); it is iftaʿala from عَراه يَعْرُوه when it strikes him. The origin is اعْتَرَوَ from العَرْو, like اغتَزَو from الغَزْو [Translator's note: the source has اغتَرَوا]; the weak letter took a vowel and the letter before it had fatḥa, so it was changed into an alif. It takes two objects, the second of them by a preposition.
His words: {أَنِّي برياء}: this may be of the category of contention for government (iʿmāl / tanāzuʿ), because «أُشْهِدُ» requires it and «اشْهدوا» requires it as well, the implied form being: "I call Allah to witness that I am free, and you too bear witness to it"; it is then a case of the second [verb] governing, because had the first governed, a pronoun would have been implied in the second. And there is nothing strange in contention between two verbs differing in transitivity and intransitivity.
As for «مِمَّا تُشْركون», «ما» may be maṣdariyya, i.e. "of your associating gods besides Him", or it may mean "that which", i.e. "of those you associate, of gods besides Him", i.e. you are the ones who make them partners.

semin-durr:55-55.t: His words, the Exalted: {جَمِيعاً}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «فكيدون». All the readers retained the yāʾ of «فكيدوني» in both states [continuous reading and pause], and they dropped it in al-Mursalāt.

semin-durr:56-56.t: الناصِيَة is the place where the hair grows at the front of the head; the hair growing there is also called «ناصِية», named after its location. نَصَوْتُ الرجل means "I seized the man by his forelock", so its final radical (lām) is a wāw. One also says ناصاة, changing its yāʾ into an alif. Seizing by the forelock is an expression for overpowering and domination, even if one is not actually seizing his forelock; for that reason, when they freed a captive as a favour, they would shear his forelock.

semin-durr:57-57.t:
His words, the Exalted: {فَإِن تَوَلَّوْاْ}: i.e. تَتَوَلَّوا, one of the two tāʾs having been dropped. It cannot be a past verb, because of his words «أَبْلَغْتكم»; nor can a shift of person (iltifāt) be claimed in it, since that would be a weakness in the construction. Ibn ʿAṭiyya permitted this, saying: "It is possible that «تولَّوا» is a past verb, and there is in the speech a return from the third person to address." I say: it may be a past verb, but by another route than iltifāt: namely, that it is with an implied verb of saying, i.e. "then say to them: I have conveyed to you." Its being a past verb is made preferable [Translator's note: so in the source; the reading cited supports an imperfect] by the reading of ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī [Translator's note: the source has «عيسى والثقفي», "ʿĪsā and al-Thaqafī"] and al-Aʿraj «فإن تُوَلُّوا» with ḍamma on the tāʾ and the lām, an imperfect of ولى with ḍamma on the tāʾ and the lām, an imperfect of وَلي; the origin is تُوَلِّيُوا, and it underwent weak-letter change.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: the conveying was before the turning away, so how did it occur as the apodosis (jazāʾ) of the condition? I say: its meaning is: if you turn away, I am not to be blamed for any shortcoming in conveying, and you are refuted by the fact that what I was sent with to you has reached you, yet you refused anything but denial."
His words: {وَيَسْتَخْلِفُ}: the generality read it in the nominative as resumptive (istiʾnāf). Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is conjoined to the apodosis with the fāʾ." ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd read it with sukūn, and there are two views on it: first, that it was given sukūn for lightness because of the succession of vowels; second, that it is jussive (majzūm), conjoined to the apodosis joined with the fāʾ, since its position is jussive; it is parallel to His words {فَلاَ هَادِيَ لَهُ وَيَذَرُهُمْ}, whose verification has preceded, except that the two readings there are among the mutawātir ones.
His words: {وَلاَ تَضُرُّونَهُ}: the generality read with the nūn, because it is nominative as stated above, and Ibn Masʿūd dropped it; this determines that the sukūn of «يستخلف» is jussive. For that reason al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing else, since he mentioned the jussive of both verbs; and since Abū al-Baqāʾ did not mention the jussive in «تَضُرُّونه», he permitted both views in «يَسْتخلف».
«شيئاً» is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "any harm".

semin-durr:59-59.t:
His words, the Exalted: {جَحَدُواْ}: a resumptive clause brought to inform about them with this; it is not a ḥāl (circumstantial) from what precedes. «جَحَد» is transitive by itself, but it was made to imply the meaning of كفر, so it is made transitive by its preposition, just as «كفر» was made to imply the meaning of «جحد» and so became transitive by itself in His words after that: {كَفَرُواْ رَبَّهُمْ} [Hūd: 60]. It was also said: «كفر» is like «شكر» in being transitive by itself at times and by a preposition at others.
The derivation of الجبَّار has preceded. العنيد is the tyrant who exceeds bounds in wrongdoing, from their saying «عَنَد يَعْنِد» when one swerves from the truth from one side to another. It was said: and from it is «عندي», which is an adverbial, because it has the meaning of "side", as in your saying: عندي كذا, i.e. "at my side". From Abū ʿUbayd: العنيد, العنود, العاند and المُعاند all mean the one who opposes by contrariness.

semin-durr:61-61.t:
His words, the Exalted: {وإلى ثَمُودَ أَخَاهُمْ}: like what precedes it. The generality read «ثمود» here as a diptote for two causes, namely proper-name status and femininity, taking it in the sense of the tribe; al-Aʿmash and Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb made it fully declinable, taking it in the sense of the clan (ḥayy). The explanation of the disagreement will come elsewhere.
His words: {مِّنَ الأرض}: [«مِن»] may be for the beginning of extent, i.e. the beginning of your being produced is from it — either the production of your origin, Ādam; or because each one was created from his own soil; or because their nourishment and the means of their life are from the earth. It was also said: «مِن» means «في», but there is no need for this.

semin-durr:62-62.t:
His words, the Exalted: {وَإِنَّنَا}: this is the original form; «وإنَّا» with a single doubled nūn is also permissible, as in the other sura. The one omitted should be the second nūn of «إنَّ», because its omission is known even without its combining with «نا», so its omission with «نا» is more fitting; and also, omitting part of nouns is not easy. Al-Farrāʾ said: "Whoever says «إننا» brings the particle out in its original form, because the [pronoun] written for the speakers is «نا», so three nūns come together; and whoever says «إنَّا» found their combination heavy, so he dropped the third and kept the first two." End of quotation. The discussion of this has preceded at the beginning of this topic.
His words: {مُرِيبٍ}: an active participle from أراب. «أراب» may be transitive, from «أرابه», i.e. "he cast him into doubt", or intransitive, from «أراب الرجلُ», i.e. "the man came to be in doubt". Doubt is described as مُريب in the two senses given, figuratively.

semin-durr:63-63.t:
His words, the Exalted: {أَرَأَيْتُمْ} to its end: its parallel has preceded. The second object here is omitted, its implied form being: "shall I disobey Him?", and «إن عصيته» indicates it. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is from seeing with the heart, and the condition after it with its apodosis stands in place of the two objects of «أرأيتم»." The Shaykh said: "What has been established is that «أرأيت» has been made to imply the meaning of "tell me"; and on the supposition that it is not made to imply it, the conditional clause with its apodosis does not stand in place of the two objects of علمت and its sisters."
His words: {غَيْرَ تَخْسِيرٍ}: the apparent view is that «غيرَ» is the second object of تَزيدونني. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The strongest view here is that «غير» is an exception in meaning, and it is the second object of «تزيدونني», i.e. you increase me in nothing but loss." «غير» may also be an adjective of an omitted object, i.e. "something other than loss", and this is good in meaning. The meaning of the pattern tafʿīl here is attribution (nisba), and the meaning is: "other than that I attribute loss to you", i.e. I ascribe you to loss; al-Zamakhsharī said this. It was also said: it is with omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "other than [what is] harmful to it, your loss" [Translator's note: the Arabic here, «غير بضارِّه تخسيركم», appears corrupt]; Ibn ʿAbbās said this.

semin-durr:64-64.t:
His words, the Exalted: {آيَةً}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) in the sense of "a sign". What makes it accusative is either the hā of alerting (hā al-tanbīh) or the demonstrative, because of the verbal meaning they imply, or an omitted verb.
His words: {لَكُمْ}: in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from «آيةٍ», because had it come after it, it would have been its naʿt (adjective); when it was placed first, it became accusative as a ḥāl. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: to what is «لكم» attached? I say: to «آية», as a ḥāl from it placed first, because had it come after, it would have been its adjective; when it came first, it became accusative as a ḥāl." The Shaykh said: "This is self-contradictory, because insofar as «لكم» is attached to «آية», it is governed by «آية», and if it is governed by it, it cannot be a ḥāl from it, because the ḥāl is attached to an omitted element." I say: how can the like of this be raised as an objection against the like of al-Zamakhsharī, after he has made clear the intended meaning, that it is attachment in meaning?
A group read «تأكلُ» in the nominative, either as resumptive or as a ḥāl.

semin-durr:65-65.t:
His words, the Exalted: {فِي دَارِكُمْ}: it was said: it is the plural of «دارَة», like ساحة / ساح / سُوح; and they recited from Umayya ibn Abī al-Ṣalt:
2671 - له داعٍ بمكةَ مُشْمَعِلٌّ ... وآخرُ فوق دارَتِه يُنادي
(He has a brisk crier at Mecca, and another calling from atop his dwelling.)
His words: {مَكْذُوبٍ}: it may be a maṣdar (verbal noun) on the pattern of the passive participle mafʿūl; a few words of this kind occur, such as المَجْلود, المَعْقول, الميسور and المفتون. It may also be a passive participle in its proper sense, and there are then two interpretations. First: "not lied about (ghayr makdhūb fīhi)"; then the preposition was dropped and the pronoun became attached, nominative and latent in the adjective; similar to it is {يَوْمٌ مَّشْهُودٌ} [Hūd: 103] and the saying:
2672 - ويومٍ شَهِدْناه سليمى وعامراً ... قليلٌ سوى الطَّعْنِ النِّهالِ نوافلُهْ
(And many a day we witnessed [lit. witnessed it] — Sulaym and ʿĀmir — whose spoils were few besides the thirsting spear-thrusts.)
Second: that it itself was made "not lied", because when it is fulfilled, it has been made true.

semin-durr:66-66.t:
His words, the Exalted: {وَمِنْ خِزْيِ يَوْمِئِذٍ}: attached to an omitted element, i.e. "and We saved them from the disgrace". Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: to what is it conjoined? I say: to «نَجَّيْنا», because its implied form is: and We saved them from the disgrace of that day, as He said: {وَنَجَّيْنَاهُمْ مِّنْ عَذَابٍ غَلِيظٍ} [Hūd: 58], i.e. and the saving was from disgrace." Others said: "It is attached to the first «نَجَّيْنا»." This is not permissible according to the Basrans other than al-Akhfash, because the redundancy of the wāw is not established.
Nāfiʿ and al-Kisāʾī read the mīm of «يومئذ» with fatḥa, it being a vowel of indeclinability (bināʾ) because it is annexed to a non-declinable word (ghayr mutamakkin), as in the saying:
2673 - على حينَ عاتَبْتُ المشيبَ على الصِّبا ... فقلت ألمَّا أَصْحُ والشيبُ وازع
(At the time when I reproached grey hair for [my] youthful passion, and said: have I not yet sobered up, when grey hair is a restrainer?)
The rest read the mīm in the genitive. The same disagreement applies in {سَأَلَ سَآئِلٌ} [al-Maʿārij: 1].
Ṭalḥa and Abān ibn Taghlib read «خزي» with tanwīn, and «يومئذ» is then accusative as an adverbial, governed by الخزي.
The Kufans and Nāfiʿ read in al-Naml {مِّن فَزَعٍ يَوْمَئِذٍ} with fatḥa as well, and the Kufans alone with tanwīn on «فزع» and «يومئذ» accusative by it.
In the reading of those who gave tanwīn to what precedes «يومئذ», the fatḥa may be a fatḥa of declension (iʿrāb) or a fatḥa of indeclinability; «إذ» is annexed to an omitted clause for which the tanwīn is a compensation, its implied form being: "when Our command came". Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is possible that the Day of Resurrection is meant, as the harsh punishment was explained as the punishment of the Hereafter." The Shaykh said: "This is not good, because there has been no previous mention of the Day of Resurrection, nor of what will happen in it, so that this tanwīn could be a compensation for the clause that would be about the Day of Resurrection." I say: indication may be verbal, and it may be in meaning; and this is of the latter kind.

semin-durr:67-67.t: His words, the Exalted: {وَأَخَذَ الذين}: the tāʾ of the feminine was omitted, either because the feminine is figurative (majāzī), or because of the separation by the object, or because الصيحة has the sense of الصياح (shouting). الصَّيْحة is faʿla, indicating a single instance of shouting, namely a violent sound: صاح يصيح صِياحاً, i.e. he cried out forcefully.

semin-durr:68-68.t:
Ḥamza and Ḥafṣ read {أَلاَ إِنَّ ثَمُودَ} here, and in al-Furqān {وَعَاداً وَثَمُودَاْ} [verse 38], and in al-ʿAnkabūt {وَعَاداً وَثَمُودَاْ وَقَد تَّبَيَّنَ لَكُم} [verse 38], and in al-Najm {وَثَمُودَ فَمَآ أبقى} [verse 51], all of these as a diptote; Abū Bakr agreed with them on the one in al-Najm.
His words: {أَلاَ بُعْداً لِّثَمُودَ}: the readers made it a diptote, except al-Kisāʾī, who made it fully declinable. It has been stated that whoever makes it a diptote takes it as the name of the tribe, and whoever makes it declinable takes it as the name of the clan (ḥayy). For the diptote, this was recited:
2674 - ونادى صالحٌ يا ربِّ أنزلْ ... بآلِ ثمودَ منك عذاباً
(And Ṣāliḥ called: O my Lord, send down upon the family of Thamūd a punishment from You.)
And for the declinable form, this was recited:
2675 - دَعَتْ أمُّ عمروٍ أمرَ شرٍّ علمتُه ... بأرضِ ثمودٍ كلِّها فأجابها
(Umm ʿAmr called for an evil matter I know of, in the whole land of Thamūd, and it answered her.)
The discussion of the derivation of this word has preceded in the sura of al-Aʿrāf.

semin-durr:69-69.t:
His words, the Exalted: {قَالُواْ سَلاَماً}: there are two views on its accusative. First, that it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); this then admits two possibilities: first, that it means they said this very utterance, which is permissible because it implies the meaning of speech; second, that it means they said the meaning of this utterance; this has been dealt with regarding the like of His words, the Exalted: {وَقُولُواْ حِطَّةٌ} [al-Baqara: 58]. The second of the two views: that it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) by an omitted verb, that verb [with its clause] being in the position of accusative by the verb of saying; its implied form is: "they said: we greet [you] with a greeting". It is of the category in which the maṣdar stands in for its governor, and [that governor] must be implied.
His words: {قَالَ سَلاَمٌ}: there are two views on its nominative. First, that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "peace be upon you". Second, that it is the predicate of an omitted subject, i.e. "my affair" or "my word is: peace". It was stated at the beginning of this topic that the nominative indicates permanence more than the accusative does. The clause as a whole — even though one of its two parts is omitted — is in the position of accusative by the verb of saying, as in the saying:
2676 - إذا ذُقْتُ فاها قلت طعمُ مُدامةٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(When I tasted her mouth, I said: the taste of wine …)
The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read «قال سِلْم» here and in the sura of al-Dhāriyāt, with kasra on the sīn and sukūn on the lām, which necessarily entails the dropping of the alif. It was said: they are two dialectal forms, like حِرْم and حَرام, and حِلّ and حَلال; and this was recited:
2677 - مَرَرْنا فقُلنا إيه سِلْمٌ فسَلَّمَتْ ... كما اكْتَلَّ بالبرق الغمامُ اللوائحُ
(We passed by and said: come, peace! — and she greeted us, as the gleaming clouds flash with lightning.)
He means سلام, as shown by «فسلَّمت». It was also said: «السِلْم» with kasra is the opposite of war; and this fits, because he found them strange and said: I am at peace with you, not at war with you.
His words: {فَمَا لَبِثَ}: three views are possible on this «ما». The most apparent is that it is negative; and there are then two views on the agent of «لَبث». First, that it is the pronoun of Ibrāhīm, upon him be peace, i.e. "Ibrāhīm did not delay"; and if it came with the dropping of the preposition, they supplied it with the bāʾ, with «عن» and with «في», i.e. "he did not delay in", or "with", or "from" [bringing]. Second, that the agent is His words «أن جاء», the implied form being: "and he did not delay", i.e. his coming with a fat calf was not slow or delayed. [Translator's note: the source has «فلما لبث» in the implied form.]
The second view: that it is maṣdariyya; the third: that it means "that which". In the last two views it is a subject, with its predicate coming with the omission of a muḍāf, its implied form being: "his delay", or "that which he delayed, was the measure of his coming".
الحَنيذ is what is roasted on heated stones in a trench. حَنَذْتُ الشاةَ أَحْنِذُها حَنْذاً [Translator's note: the source has حَنْزاً], so it is حَنيذ, i.e. مَحنوذة. It was also said: حنيذ means "dripping with its fat", from their saying حَنَذْتُ الفرس, i.e. "I drove the horse one or two heats and put the horse-blanket on it in the sun to make it sweat."

semin-durr:70-70.t:
His words, the Exalted: {نَكِرَهُمْ}: i.e. أنكرهم ("he found them strange"), the two having the same meaning; they recited:
2678 - وأَنْكَرَتْني وما كان الذي نَكِرَتْ ... من الحوادثِ إلا الشَّيْبَ والصَّلعا
(She did not know me, and what she found strange among the vicissitudes was nothing but grey hair and baldness.)
Some distinguished between them, saying: the triliteral is for what is seen with the eye, and the quadriliteral for abstract notions that are not seen; and they took the verse in that way, for she denied his affection, which is among abstract notions not seen, and found strange his grey hair and baldness, which are seen. And of this is the saying of Abū Dhuʾayb:
2679 - فَنَكِرْنَه فَنَفَرْنَ وامْتَرَسَتْ به ... هَوْجاءُ هادِيَةٌ وهادٍ جُرْشُعُ
(They found him strange and fled, and a reckless leading she-ass and a stout leading male clung close to him.)
الإيجاس is the soul's inner talk; its origin is from entering, as though the fear entered him.
Al-Akhfash said: "[It means] it pervaded his heart." Al-Farrāʾ said: "He felt and sensed." الوجيس is what befalls the soul at the first onset of fright. وَجَسَ في نفسه كذا, i.e. it occurred to it; يَجِسُ وَجْساً ووُجوساً ووَجيساً. And يَوْجَس and يَجِس mean "he listens"; they recited:
2680 - وصادقتا سَمْعِ التوجُّسِ للسُّرى ... لِلَمْحِ خَفِيٍّ أو لصوتٍ مُنَدَّد
(And two [ears] true in listening keenly in the night journey, for a faint glimpse or for a raised sound.)
So خيفةً is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "he sensed a fear" or "harboured a fear".

semin-durr:71-71.t:
His words, the Exalted: {وامرأته قَآئِمَةٌ}: in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the nominative of «أُرْسِلْنا». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "from the pronoun of the agent in «أرسلنا»", and this is an unusual expression, since the object of a verb whose agent is unnamed is not called an agent according to the well-known usage. On the whole, making it a ḥāl is not clear; rather it is a resumptive statement. It may also be made a ḥāl from the agent of «قالوا», i.e. "they said that while his wife was standing".
His words: {فَضَحِكَتْ}: the generality read with kasra on the ḥāʾ; Muḥammad ibn Ziyād al-Aʿrābī, a man from Mecca, read it with fatḥa; they are two dialectal forms: one says ضَحِك and ضَحَك. Al-Mahdawī said: "The fatḥa is not known." The majority hold that the laughing is in its proper sense, and the exegetes differed over its cause. It was also said: it means "she menstruated" — ضحكت الأرنب, i.e. the hare menstruated; Abū ʿUbayda, Abū ʿUbayd and al-Farrāʾ rejected this. Others recited in support of it:
2681 - وضِحْكُ الأرانبِ فوق الصَّفا ... كمثلِ دمِ الجَوْفِ يوم اللِّقا
(And the "laughing" of hares on the rocks is like the blood of the belly on the day of battle.)
And another said:
2682 - وعهدي بسلمى ضاحكاً في لَبانةٍ ... ولم يَعْدُ حُقَّاً ثَدْيُها أن يُحَمَّلا
(My last sight of Salmā was of her "laughing" at the age of need, her breast not yet past the size of a little box.)
i.e. menstruating. ضحِكت الكافورة: [the spathe] split open. ضحكت الشجرة: its gum flowed. ضَحِك الحوضُ: [the basin] filled and overflowed. The apparent sense of Abū al-Baqāʾ's words is that ضَحَك with fatḥa is specific to menstruation, for he said: "meaning she menstruated; one says ضحَكت الأرنب with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ."
His words: {يَعْقُوبَ}: Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read it with fatḥa on the bāʾ, and the rest with ḍamma. As for the first reading, they differed over it: is the fatḥa a sign of the accusative or of the genitive? Those who said it is a sign of the accusative differed. It was said: it is accusative, conjoined to his words «بإسحاق». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "As if it were said: and We granted him Isḥāq, and after Isḥāq Yaʿqūb, in the manner of the saying:
2683 -. . . . . . . . . . . . ليسوا مصلحين عشيرةً ... ولا ناعِبٍ. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(… they are not ones who set a clan right, nor a croaking [crow] …)"
He means that it is conjunction by supposition (ʿaṭf ʿalā al-tawahhum), so it was made accusative, just as the poet conjoined on the supposition of the bāʾ in the predicate of «ليس» and so made it genitive; but this is not a basis for analogy. It was also said: it is accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being: "and We granted Yaʿqūb"; on this view it is not included in the glad tidings; al-Fārisī preferred this view. It was also said: it is accusative, conjoined to the position of «بإسحاق», because its position is accusative, as in His words {وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ} [al-Māʾida: 6] in the accusative, conjoined to «برؤوسكم». The difference between this and the first view is that the first makes the verb imply the meaning of «وَهَبْنا» by supposition, while here it remains in its own meaning without supposition.
Those who said it is genitive made it conjoined to «بإسحاق», the meaning being that she was given glad tidings of both. In this view and the one before it there is a point for discussion: the separation by the adverbial between the conjunction and the conjoined; this has been dealt with fully in al-Nisāʾ, so turn your attention to it.
Makkī attributed the genitive to al-Kisāʾī, then said: "It is weak except with repetition of the preposition, because you have separated the preposition and its genitive by the adverbial."
His saying "with repetition of the preposition": that is not necessary, since if it were placed earlier and not separated, it would not be required to bring it.
As for the nominative reading, there are several views on it. First, that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is the preceding adverbial; al-Zamakhsharī gave its implied form as "born" or "existing", and others as "being". When al-Naḥḥās reported this, he said: "The clause is a ḥāl included in the glad tidings, i.e. We gave her glad tidings of Isḥāq with Yaʿqūb joined to him." Second, that it is nominative as an agent by the preposition before it; this comes on the opinion of al-Akhfash. Third, that it is nominative by an implied verb, i.e. "and after Isḥāq Yaʿqūb will come about", and it has no part in the glad tidings. Fourth, that it is nominative by severance (qaṭʿ), by which they mean resumption; and this goes back to one of the preceding: its being a subject with a predicate, or an agent by the preposition after it [Translator's note: so in the source; the preposition is before it], or by an implied verb.

semin-durr:72-72.t:
His words, the Exalted: {ياويلتى}: the apparent view is that the alif is a substitute for the yāʾ of the speaker; for that reason Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim, in one transmission, pronounced it with imāla (inclination); and al-Ḥasan read with it «يا ويلتي» with an explicit yāʾ. It was also said: it is the alif of lament (nudba), and one pauses on it with the hāʾ of pause.
His words: {وَأَنَاْ عَجُوزٌ وهذا بَعْلِي شَيْخاًٌ}: the two clauses are in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «أَلِدُ», i.e. how can giving birth occur in these two states that are incompatible with it?
The majority read «شيخاً» in the accusative, and there are two views on it. The well-known one: that it is a ḥāl, and what governs it is either the alerting [particle], or the demonstrative, or both. Second, that it is accusative as the predicate of taqrīb according to the Kufans. This ḥāl is a necessary one (lāzima) for those who are not ignorant of the predicate; for those ignorant of it, it is not necessary. Ibn Masʿūd and al-Aʿmash read — and so it is in the codex of Ibn Masʿūd — «شيخٌ» in the nominative, and they mentioned several views on it: a predicate after a predicate; or two predicates in the sense of a single predicate, as in هذا حلو حامض ("this is sweet-sour"); or the predicate of «هذا», with «بعلي» an explicative apposition or a substitute; or «شيخ» a badal (substitute) from «بعلي»; or «بعلي» a subject and «شيخ» its predicate, the clause being the predicate of the first; or «شيخ» the predicate of an implied subject, i.e. "he is an old man".
The counterpart of شيخ is عجوز (old woman); شَيْخة is also said, rarely, as in the saying:
2684 - وتَضْحك مني شَيْخةٌ عَبْشَمِيَّةٌ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And an old woman of ʿAbd Shams laughs at me …)
It has many plurals. The explicit ones are أَشْياخ, شُيوخ and شِيخان, and شِيْخَة for those who hold that fiʿla is a plural and not a collective noun, like غِلْمة and فِتْيَة. Among its collective nouns are مَشِيخَة, شِيَخَة and مَشْيُوخاء.

semin-durr:73-73.t:
His words, the Exalted: {أَهْلَ البيت}: there are two views on its accusative. First, that it is a munādā (one addressed in the vocative). Second, that it is accusative in praise (manṣūb ʿalā al-madḥ). It was also said: by specification (ikhtiṣāṣ); and there is a difference between the two accusatives: the one accusative in praise is a word that by its coinage contains praise, just as the one [accusative] in blame is a word that by its coinage contains blame.
The one accusative by specification is only for praise or blame, but its wording does not contain by its coinage [praise] or blame, as in the saying:
2685 - بنا تميماً يُكْشَفُ الضبابُ
(Through us — [we] Tamīm — the fog is dispelled.)
So said the Shaykh, relying on the fact that Sībawayh put them in two chapters; and this is open to consideration.
المجيد is faʿīl, an intensive form from مَجَد يَمْجُد مَجْداً ومَجادة; one also says مَجُد, like شَرُف, and its origin is elevation. It was also said: from مَجَدَتِ الإبلُ تَمْجُد مَجادة ومَجْداً, i.e. "the camels ate their fill"; they recited from Abū Ḥayya al-Numayrī:
2686 - تزيدُ على صواحبِها وليسَتْ ... بماجدةِ الطعام ولا الشراب
(She surpasses her companions, though she is not one abundant in food or drink.)
i.e. not abundant in food or drink. It was also said: مَجَد الشيءُ, i.e. its qualities became fine. Al-Layth said: "أمجد فلانٌ عطاءَه and مَجَّده, i.e. he made it abundant."

semin-durr:74-74.t:
الرَّوْع is fright. The poet said:
2687 - إذا أخَذَتْها هِزَّةُ الرَّوْعِ أَمْسَكَتْ ... بمَنْكِبِ مِقْدامٍ على الهَوْلِ أرْوَعَا
(When the tremor of fright seized her, she held on to the shoulder of one bold in the face of terror, splendid.)
One says راعَه يَرُوْعُه, i.e. he frightened him. ʿAntara said:
2688 - ما راعني إلا حَمولةُ أهلِها ... وسطَ الديار تَسِفُّ حَبَّ الخِمْخِمِ
(Nothing alarmed me but her people's baggage camels in the midst of the dwellings, munching the seeds of the khimkhim.)
ارتاع is iftaʿala from it. Al-Nābigha said:
2689 - فارتاعَ من صَوْتِ كَلاَّبِ فباتَ له ... طَوْعَ الشَّوامِتِ من خوفٍ ومن صَرَدٍ
(He took fright at the voice of a hound-master, and spent the night, from fear and cold, as his gloating foes would wish.)
As for الرُّوْع with ḍamma, it is the soul, because it is the seat of fright; so they distinguished between what resides and the place where it resides. In the ḥadīth: «إنَّ رُوْحَ القدس نفث في رُوْعي» ("The Holy Spirit breathed into my soul").
His words: {وَجَآءَتْهُ البشرى}: conjoined to «ذَهَب», and the apodosis (jawāb) of «لَمَّا» on this view is omitted, i.e. "when such-and-such happened, he ventured to address them" or "he set about arguing with them"; and his words «يُجادلنا» on this view are a resumptive clause, and it is what indicates that omitted apodosis. It was also said: the implied apodosis is "he began to argue with Us", so يجادلنا on this view is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «أقبل». It was also said: its apodosis is His words «يجادِلُنا», the imperfect being put in place of the past. It was also said: the apodosis is His words {وَجَآءَتْهُ البشرى}, it being the apodosis with the wāw redundant. It was also said: «يجادلنا» is a ḥāl from «إبراهيم», and likewise His words «وجاءَتْه البشرى», with «قد» implied. «يجادِلُنا» may also be a ḥāl from the object pronoun in «جاءَتْه». «في قوم» means: concerning their affair.

semin-durr:75-75.t: His words, the Exalted: {أَوَّاهٌ}: faʿʿāl from أوَّهَ; its derivation has preceded.

semin-durr:76-76.t: His words, the Exalted: {آتِيهِمْ عَذَابٌ}: it may be a clause of mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of nominative as the predicate of «إنهم». «آتيهم» may also be the predicate and «عذاب» the subject; this is permissible because [عذاب] is specified by the adjective, and because «آتيهم» is indefinite, its annexation being impure. «آتيهم» may also be the predicate of «إنَّ», with «عذاب» its fāʿil (agent); this is indicated by the reading of ʿAmr ibn Harim: «وإنهم أتاهم», with the form of the past verb.

semin-durr:77-77.t:
His words, the Exalted: {سياء}: a verb in the passive. What stands in place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil) is the pronoun of Lūṭ, from your saying «ساءني كذا», i.e. harm befell me. «بهم» is attached to it, i.e. "because of them". «ذَرْعاً» is accusative as a tamyīz (specification); it is originally the maṣdar of ذَرَعَ البعير يَذْرَع بيديه في سَيْره, when the camel goes according to the measure of its stride, derived from الذِّراع (the forearm); then it was extended and put in place of capacity and effort, so it was said: ضاق ذَرْعُه, i.e. his capacity. [The poet] said:
2690 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فاقدِرْ بذَرْعِك وانظر أين تَنْسَلِكُ
(… so measure by your capacity, and see where you are going.)
And الذِّراع sometimes occurs in its place; [the poet] said:
2691 - إذا التَّيَّازُ ذو العَضَلاتِ قُلْنا ... إليك إليك ضاقَ بها ذِراعا
(When the brawny, muscular one — we said: "away, away!" — his forearm [i.e. capacity] was strained by it.)
It was said: it is a metonym for distress of the breast.
His words: {عَصِيبٌ}: العَصِيْب, العَصَبْصَب and العَصُوب mean a hard day, full of evil wound tightly together. [The poet] said:
2692 - وكنت لِزازَ خَصْمِكَ لم أُعَرِّدْ ... وقد سَلكوك في يومٍ عصيبِ
(I was a bar against your foe; I did not flee, when they had thrust you into a grievous day.)
From Abū ʿUbayd: "It was called عَصِيب because it binds people with evil." العِصابة is a group of people; they were so named because they surround [something] as a headband (ʿiṣāba) surrounds.
His words: {يُهْرَعُونَ}: in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The generality read «يُهرعون» in the passive. الإهراع is hastening; it was also said: it is walking between a trot and a gallop. Al-Harawī said: هَرَع and أَهْرَعَ mean "to urge on". A group read «يَهْرعون» with fatḥa on the yāʾ, as active, from the form «هَرَع».
His words: {هؤلاء بَنَاتِي}: a clause on its own, and «هنَّ أطهرُ لكم» is another clause.
