It is also possible that «هؤلاء» is a subject, «بناتي» a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), «هنَّ» a subject and «أَطْهَرُ» its predicate, the clause being the predicate of the first. It is also possible that «هنَّ» is a separating pronoun (faṣl) and «أطهر» a predicate either of «هؤلاء» or of «بناتي», the clause being the predicate of the first.
Al-Ḥasan, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and al-Suddī read «أطهرَ» in the accusative, and it was explained as a ḥāl. It was said: «هؤلاء» is a subject, «بناتي هُنَّ» a clause in the position of its predicate, and «أطهر» a ḥāl, governed either by the alerting [particle] or by the demonstrative. It was also said: «هنَّ» is a separating pronoun between the ḥāl and the one it describes, and they counted among this their saying: «أكثر أكلي التفاحةَ هي نضيجةً» ("most of my eating the apple is [when] it is ripe"). Some grammarians rejected this and explained the verse as «لكم» being the predicate of «هن»; this obliged him to have the ḥāl precede its abstract (maʿnawī) governor; and he explained the cited saying as «نضيجة» being accusative by an implied «كان».
His words: {وَلاَ تُخْزُونِ فِي ضَيْفِي}: الضيف is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun); then it was applied to the night-visitor because he inclines to the host. For that reason it applies to the singular and the masculine and their opposites with one form. It is sometimes made dual, so one says ضَيْفان, and pluralised, so one says أضايف and ضُيوف, like أبيات and بُيوت, and ضِيفان, like حَوْض and حِيضان.

semin-durr:79-79.t:
His words, the Exalted: {مِنْ حَقٍّ}: it may be a mubtadaʾ (subject) with the preposition [phrase] as its khabar (predicate), or a fāʿil (agent) of the preposition before it, because it rests on a negation; «مِنْ» is redundant on both views.
His words: {مَا نُرِيدُ}: [«ما»] may be maṣdariyya, or a relative noun meaning "that which". العلم here is recognition (ʿirfān), and for that reason it takes one object, i.e. "you know our wish" or "what we want". «ما» may also be interrogative, suspending (muʿalliqa) the [verb of] knowing before it.

semin-durr:80-80.t:
His words, the Exalted: {لَوْ أَنَّ}: its apodosis (jawāb) is omitted, its implied form being: "I would have done to you and dealt with you", as in His words {وَلَوْ أَنَّ قُرْآناً سُيِّرَتْ} [al-Raʿd: 31].
His words: {أَوْ آوي}: it may be conjoined according to the meaning, its implied form being: "or that I took refuge"; Abū al-Baqāʾ and al-Ḥūfī said this. It may also be conjoined to «قوة», because it is originally accusative by an implied أن; when «أن» was dropped, the verb became nominative, as in His words {وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ يُرِيكُمُ} [al-Rūm: 24].
Abū al-Baqāʾ considered this view weak because it is not accusative; its answer has preceded. What indicates that this is to be taken into account is the reading of Shayba and Abū Jaʿfar «أو آويَ» in the accusative, as in the saying:
2693 - ولولا رجالٌ من رِزامٍ أعزَّةٍ ... وآلُ سبيعٍ أو أسُوْءَك عَلْقما
(Were it not for mighty men of Rizām, and the family of Subayʿ, or [my] hurting you, ʿAlqama …)
And her saying:
2694 - لَلُبْسُ عباءةٍ وتقرَّ عَيْني ... أحبُّ إليَّ من لُبْس الشُّفوف
(Wearing a woollen cloak with my eye content is dearer to me than wearing sheer fabrics.)
It is also possible that this verbal clause is conjoined to its like, if you suppose that «أنَّ» is nominative by an implied verb after «لو», according to al-Mubarrad; the implied form being: "if the being-settled of strength were settled or established, or I took refuge"; these two verbs are then past in meaning, because [لو] turns the imperfect into the past. But on Sībawayh's opinion, that «أنَّ» is in the position of a subject, this is resumptive. It was also said: «أو» means "rather" (bal); this is according to the Kufans.
«بكم» is attached to an omitted element, because it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «قوة», since it is originally an adjective of the indefinite noun. It cannot be attached to «قوة», because it is a maṣdar.
الرُّكْن, with sukūn or ḍamma on the kāf, is the side of a mountain or the like; its plural is أركان and أَرْكُن. [The poet] said:
2695 - وزَحْمُ رُكْنَيْكَ شديدُ الأَرْكُنِ
(And the press of your two flanks is of mighty supports.)

semin-durr:81-81.t:
His words, the Exalted: {فَأَسْرِ}: Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr read {فاسْرِ بأهلك} here and in al-Ḥijr, and in al-Dukhān {فَأَسْرِ بِعِبَادِي} [verse 23], and His words {أَنْ أَسْرِ} [verse 77] in Ṭā Hā and al-Shuʿarāʾ, all of these with the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl), which drops in continuous reading and is pronounced with kasra when beginning. The rest read «فَأَسْر» with the disjunctive hamza (hamzat al-qaṭʿ), pronounced with fatḥa both in continuous reading and when beginning. The two readings are taken from the two dialectal forms of this verb, for one says سَرَى — and from it is {والليل إِذَا يَسْرِ} [al-Fajr: 4] — and أَسْرى — and from it is {سُبْحَانَ الذي أسرى} [al-Isrāʾ: 1]. Are they of one meaning, or is there a difference between them? There is a well-known disagreement. It was said: they are of one meaning; this is the view of Abū ʿUbayd. It was also said: rather, أَسْرى is for the beginning of the night and سَرَى for its end; this is the view of al-Layth. As for سار, it is specific to the daytime, and it is not a metathesis of سَرى.
His words: {بِأَهْلِكَ}: the bāʾ may be for making transitive (taʿdiya), or for the ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "accompanying them". His words «بقِطْعٍ» are a ḥāl from «أهلك», i.e. "accompanying a portion [of the night]", on the understanding that what is meant by it is darkness. It was also said: the bāʾ means «في». القِطْع here is half the night, because it is a portion of it equal to the rest of it; they recited:
2696 - ونائحةٍ تَنُوْحُ بقِطْعِ ليلِ ... على رَجُلٍ بقارعةِ الصعيد
(And many a wailing woman wails in a portion of the night over a man on the open face of the upland.)
The discussion of القِطْع has preceded in Yūnus more fully than this.
His words: {إِلاَّ امرأتك}: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «امرأتك» in the nominative, and the rest in the accusative. In this noble verse there is much discussion that must be given in full. As for the nominative reading, there are two views on it. The better known among the parsers is that it is a badal (substitute) from «أحد», and this is better than the accusative because the speech is non-affirmative. Abū ʿUbayd rejected this view on the grounds that it entails that they were forbidden to turn round except the wife, she not being forbidden it, and this is not permissible. Had the speech been «ولا يلتفت» with «يلتفت» in the nominative — that is, with «لا» being negative, so that the speech would be a report about them that they did not turn round except his wife, for she would turn round — the exception by substitution would have been clear; but no one read «يلتفت» in the nominative.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya approved this objection from Abū ʿUbayd and said: "It applies to the view that the wife is excepted from «أحد», whether you make المرأة nominative or accusative." I say: this is correct, for Abū ʿUbayd did not object to the nominative specifically because it is nominative, but because of the corruption of the meaning, and the corruption of the meaning goes with the exception from «أحد». Abū ʿUbayd explains the accusative as an exception from «بأهلك»; but that entails invalidating the nominative reading, and there is no way to that, since it is mutawātir.
Al-Mubarrad extricated himself from this difficulty raised by Abū ʿUbayd by saying that the prohibition is, in wording, addressed to «أحد», but in meaning to Lūṭ, upon him be peace, since the implied form is: "do not let any one of them turn round", as when you say to your servant: «لا يَقُمْ أحدٌ» ("let no one stand up"): the prohibition is to «أحد», but in meaning it is to the servant, since the meaning is: «لا تَدَعْ أحداً يقوم» ("do not let anyone stand up").
I say: so the answer comes down to the meaning: "do not let anyone turn round except your wife; let her turn round". This is what the exception requires, as when you say: «لا تَدَعْ أحداً يقوم إلا زيداً» ("do not let anyone stand up except Zayd"), whose meaning is: let him stand up. This is open to consideration, since the objectionable consequence that Abū ʿUbayd fled from is present here, or something close to it.
The second view: that the nominative is by way of the disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). The one who holds this also made the accusative reading a disconnected exception, so the two readings are, for him, on the same footing. Let us quote his words in full so that we may know them. He said: "What appears is that the exception in both readings is disconnected; it is not intended to exclude her from those whom he was commanded to take by night, nor from those forbidden to turn round; rather, a fresh statement is made about her, so the meaning is: but as for your wife, such-and-such will happen to her. This meaning is supported by the fact that the like of this verse came in the sura of al-Ḥijr, and there is no exception in it at all; the Exalted said: {فَأَسْرِ بِأَهْلِكَ} — the verse. So the concern there was only with mentioning those whom Allah the Exalted saved; and the account of his wife's state in the sura of Hūd came as an accessory, not intended as an exclusion from what preceded. When this meaning is clear, it is known that the two readings came according to what Arabic requires in the disconnected exception, in which there is the accusative and the nominative: the accusative is the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz, and most [readers] follow it, and the nominative is the dialect of Tamīm, and two of the readers follow it." The Shaykh said: "This, on which he has spoken at length, has no precision in it. For if it is not intended to exclude her from those he was commanded to take by night, nor from those forbidden to turn round, and it is made a disconnected exception, it would be of the disconnected kind towards which the governor cannot be directed at all, and in this kind the accusative is obligatory in both dialects. The two dialects only apply in what the governor may be directed towards. In both kinds, what follows «إلا» is not of the genus of the excepted [the source: المستثنى]. So the fact that the two dialects are permissible in it is evidence that the governor can be directed towards it; yet he supposed that the exception was not intended to exclude her from those he was commanded to take by night nor from those forbidden to turn round; so the accusative would then have been obligatory, by a single view."
[I say: the one who held that is al-Shaykh Shihāb al-Dīn Abū Shāma.] As for his saying "the governor cannot be directed towards it", it is not to be granted; rather it is directed towards it in a general way. What the grammarians said about [the exception] towards which the governor cannot be directed is in terms of meaning, such as: «ما زاد إلا ما نقص» ("it did not increase, except what decreased") and «ما نفع إلا ما ضر» ("it did not benefit, except what harmed"); and this is not of that kind, so how can it be raised as an objection against Abū Shāma?
As for the accusative, there are three views on it. First, that it is excepted from «بأهلك». They raised a difficulty against this in terms of meaning: it entails that he did not take her by night, whereas the supposition is that he did take her by night, as is shown by her turning round; had she not been with them, it would not have been fitting to report that she turned round; so the turning round shows decisively that she travelled by night with them.
This was answered by saying that he did not take her by night himself, but when he and his two daughters travelled by night she followed them and turned round. What supports its being an exception from the family is what ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] read, and what dropped from his codex: «فَأَسْر بأهلك بقطع من الليل إلا امرأتك», without mentioning His words {وَلاَ يَلْتَفِتْ مِنكُمْ أَحَدٌ}.
Second, that it is excepted from «أحد»; although the nominative is better, it came like the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir {مَّا فَعَلُوهُ إِلاَّ قَلِيلٌ مِّنْهُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 66] in the accusative despite an explicit negation preceding. Another explanation was given to you there which is not possible here.
Third, that it is a disconnected exception, according to what I cited from Abū Shāma. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Concerning his taking her out with his family there are two reports. It is related that he took her out with them and was commanded that none of them should turn round except her; when she heard the crash of the punishment, she turned round and said: O my people! — and a stone overtook her and killed her. And it is related that he was commanded to leave her behind with her people, for her inclination was towards them, and he did not take her by night. The difference between the two readings is due to the difference between the two reports."
The Shaykh said: "This is a gross error, since he based the two readings on the difference between the two reports — that he did take her by night or did not — and this is mutual contradiction in reporting; it is impossible that the two readings, which are the speech of Allah the Exalted, should rest on mutual contradiction." I say: Allah forbid that the two readings should rest on mutual contradiction! But what al-Zamakhsharī said is correct: the point is that both views have come in the tafsīr, and mutual contradiction does not follow from that. For whoever said that he took her by night means that she herself travelled by night accompanying them at the beginning of the affair, then the punishment seized her and her night journey was cut off; and whoever said that he did not take her by night means that he did not command her nor take her, and that her night journey with them did not continue but was cut off. So it is correct to say that he took her by night and did not take her by night. People have answered with this, and it is good.
Al-Shaykh Abū Shāma said: "In justifying what the grammarians parsed, a good meaning occurred to me: that there is an abridgement in the speech, to which the difference between the two readings draws attention. It is as though it were said: take your family by night except your wife — and likewise Abū ʿUbayda and others related that it is so in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh, without {وَلاَ يَلْتَفِتْ مِنكُمْ أَحَدٌ}; this is evidence of her being excepted from those taken by night. Then it is as though He, glory be to Him, said: if she goes out with you and follows you without your having taken her by night, then forbid your family to turn round, except her, for she will turn round, and what befell her people will befall her. So the accusative reading indicates the earlier meaning, and the nominative reading the later meaning, and the two together indicate the whole of the meaning explained." This is a good statement, bearing witness to what I mentioned.
His words: {إِنَّهُ مُصِيبُهَا}: the pronoun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); «مُصيبها» is a fronted khabar (predicate) and «ما أصابهم» a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), a relative noun meaning "that which"; and the clause is the predicate of إنَّ, because the pronoun of the matter is explained by a clause with both its parts explicit.
The Shaykh parsed «مُصيبها» as subject and «ما أصابهم» as predicate. This is open to consideration in terms of technical grammar: the relative noun is definite, so it should be the subject, while «مُصيبها» is indefinite, because it governs implicitly, so its annexation is impure. And in terms of meaning: what is intended is to state about that which befell them that it will befall her, not the reverse. According to the Kufans, «مصيبُها» may be a subject and the relative «ما» its agent, because they permit the pronoun of the matter to be explained by a single word governing what follows it, as in: «إنه قائمٌ أبواك» ("indeed, standing are your parents").
His words: {إِنَّ مَوْعِدَهُمُ}: i.e. the appointed time of their destruction. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read «الصبح» with two ḍammas [الصُّبُح]. It was said: they are two dialectal forms; it was also said: rather, it is vowel harmony (itbāʿ). The discussion of this has preceded.

semin-durr:82-82.t: His words, the Exalted: {عَالِيَهَا سَافِلَهَا}: the two objects of جعل in the sense of "making into". As for «سِجِّيل», it was said: it is originally a compound of «سكر كل», which in Persian is "stone and clay"; it was Arabicised and its letters altered. It was also said: سِجِّيل is a name for the heaven; this is weak or a mistake, because it is described as مَنْضود. It was also said: it is from أَسْجَلَ, i.e. "he sent", so it would be fiʿʿīl. It was also said: it is from التسجيل (recording), and the meaning is that it is among what Allah wrote down and decreed, that the people of Lūṭ be punished with it. The first view is supported by Ibn ʿAbbās's explanation that it is stone and clay, like baked brick. From Abū ʿUbayd: it is hard stone. «منضود» is an adjective of سِجِّيل. النَّضْد is placing things one on top of another; and from it is {وَطَلْحٍ مَّنضُودٍ} [al-Wāqiʿa: 29], i.e. layered; what is meant is describing the stones as numerous.

semin-durr:83-83.t:
«مُسَوَّمة» is a naʿt (adjective) of «حجارة»; in that case it necessarily follows that a non-explicit description precedes an explicit one, since «مِنْ سجيل» is an adjective of «حجارة». It is better to make it a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «حجارة», its coming from an indefinite noun being justified by the indefinite noun's being specified by the adjective. التَّسْويم is marking. It was said: on each stone was marked the name of the one who would be pelted with it. Its derivation has preceded in Āl ʿImrān. «عند» is either accusative by «مُسَوَّمة», or by an omitted element, being an adjective of «مُسَوَّمة».
His words: {وَمَا هِيَ}: the apparent view is that this pronoun refers to the destroyed towns. It was also said: it refers to the stones, which are the nearest thing mentioned. It was also said: it refers to the punishment understood from the context. «ببعيد» was not made feminine, either because it is originally an adjective of an omitted «مكان», its implied form being: "and it is not at a distant place, but rather it is near" — what is meant being the heaven or the destroyed towns; or because العقوبة and العقاب are the same; or by interpreting the stones as a punishment or as something distant.

semin-durr:84-84.t:
His words, the Exalted: {وَلاَ تَنقُصُواْ}: «نَقَصَ» takes two objects, the first by itself and the second by a preposition, which is sometimes omitted; you say: نَقَصْت زيداً مِنْ حقَّه ("I diminished Zayd of his due"), and so it is here, since what is meant is: "and do not diminish people [their due] of the measure". It may also take one object according to the meaning, the meaning being: "do not lessen and give short measure". It is also possible that «المكيالَ» is the first object and the second is omitted, which contains intensification; the implied form is: "and do not diminish the measure and the balance their due that is owed to them", and this is more forceful as a command to give them in full.
His words: {مُّحِيطٍ}: an adjective of «اليوم»; it is used as its description from their saying أحاط به العدوُّ ("the enemy surrounded him"), and His words {وَأُحِيطَ بِثَمَرِهِ} [al-Kahf: 42]. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Describing the day as encompassing is more forceful than describing the punishment so." He said: "Because the day is a time that comprises events, so if it encompasses with its punishment, everything of it that the day comprises is gathered upon the one punished, just as when it encompasses with its bliss."
Some claimed that it is genitive by proximity (jiwār), because in meaning it is an adjective of the punishment, the origin being: عذاب يوم محيطاً. Others said: the implied form is: "the punishment of a day whose punishment is encompassing." Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "This is far-fetched, because محيط has then been applied to something other than what it belongs to, so its agent would have to be made overt, annexed to the pronoun of the thing described."

semin-durr:86-86.t: His words, the Exalted: {إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ}: Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The apodosis (jawāb) of this condition precedes it," meaning according to the school of those who hold this, not according to [the school of] the majority of the Basrans. The generality read the yāʾ of «بقيَّة» doubled; Ismāʿīl ibn Jaʿfar, of the people of Medina, read it light. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is a dialectal form." This should not be said; rather one should say: if indicating intensiveness is not intended, it is brought in the light form. That is because faʿila with kasra on the middle radical, when intransitive, has as the regular form of its adjective faʿil with kasra on the middle radical, as in سَجِيَت المرأة فهي سَجِيَة; if you intend intensiveness, سَجِيَّة is said, because faʿīl is among the intensive patterns; and so likewise بقيَّة and بَقِية, i.e. with the doubled and the light [yāʾ].

semin-durr:87-87.t:
The disagreement over his words «أصلاتك», regarding the singular and plural, has preceded in the sura of Barāʾa.
His words: {أَوْ أَن نَّفْعَلَ}: the generality read «نفعل» and «نشاء» with the nūn of the group or of majesty. Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Ibn Abī ʿAbla and al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Qays read both with the tāʾ of address. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Ṭalḥa read the first with nūn and the second with tāʾ. Those who read both with nūn conjoin it to the object of «نترك», namely the relative «ما», the implied form being: "Does your prayer command you that we leave what our fathers worship, or that we leave doing with our wealth what we will?" — namely the giving of short measure and weight mentioned before. «أو» is for variety, or in the sense of the wāw; two views. It cannot be conjoined to the object of «تأمرك», because the meaning would change, since the implied form would become: "does your prayer command you that we do with our wealth …"
Those who read both with tāʾ may take it as conjoined to the object of «تأمرك» or to the object of «نترك», the implied form being: "Does your prayer command you that you do with our wealth what you will, or that we leave what our fathers worship?" or "… that we leave your doing with our wealth what you will?"
Those who read the first with nūn and the second with tāʾ have «أن نفعل» conjoined to the object of «تأمرك» [Translator's note: so in the source; by the author's own scheme in the next sentence, the reading with nūn in «نفعل» and tāʾ in «تشاء» is the one in which conjunction to the object of «تأمرك» is required]. So there are three categories: a category in which conjunction to the object of «نترك» is required, namely the reading with nūn in both; a category in which conjunction to the object of «تأمرك» is required, namely the reading with nūn in «نفعل» and tāʾ in «تشاء»; and a category in which both are permissible, namely the reading with tāʾ in both. What is apparent in terms of meaning, in the reading with tāʾ in both or in «تشاء», is that what they meant by saying that was giving full measure and weight, because he used to command them to do both. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The meaning is: it commands you to impose on us that we leave; the muḍāf was omitted, because a person is not commanded to do another's act."

semin-durr:88-88.t:
His words, the Exalted: {أَرَأَيْتُمْ}: this has been dealt with more than once. Al-Zamakhsharī said here: "If you say: where is the apodosis (jawāb) of «أرأيتم», and why was it not stated as it was stated in the stories of Nūḥ and Ṣāliḥ? I say: its apodosis is omitted; it was not stated only because its statement in the two stories indicated its place, and the meaning of the speech proclaims it. The meaning is: tell me, if I am upon a clear proof and certainty from my Lord, and [am] a prophet in truth, is it right that I should not command you to abandon the worship of idols and to refrain from sins, when the prophets are sent only for that?"
The Shaykh said: "Calling this an apodosis of «أرأيتم» is not according to the technical usage; rather this clause that he supplied is in the position of the second object of «أرأيتم», [because أرأيتم], when made to imply the meaning of "tell me", takes two objects, and the second is mostly an interrogative clause, which together with the first object originally forms a nominal clause, as in the Arabs' saying: «أرأيتك زيداً ما صنع» ("Tell me about Zayd: what did he do?")." Al-Ḥūfī said: "The apodosis of the condition is omitted because the speech indicates it, its implied form being: shall I swerve from what I am upon?" Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The apodosis of the condition in his words «إن كنت» is omitted, its implied form being: shall I go astray as you have gone astray, or abandon conveying the message — and the like of this that befits this disputation." The Shaykh said: "His saying «أضلّ» is not the apodosis of the condition; for if it is affirmative, it cannot be the apodosis, because it does not follow from the condition; and if it is a question with the hamza dropped, it is in the position of the second object of «أرأيتم», and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by the preceding clause with what is attached to it."
His words: {أَنْ أُخَالِفَكُمْ}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "خالفني فلان إلى كذا is said when he heads for it while you are turning away from it; and خالفني عنه when he turns away from it while you are heading for it. A man meets you returning from the water, and you ask him about his companion, and he says: «خالَفَني إلى الماء» ("he went the other way, to the water"), meaning that he is going to it, arriving, while I am going away from it, returning. And of this is His words, the Exalted: {وَمَآ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُخَالِفَكُمْ إلى مَآ أَنْهَاكُمْ عَنْهُ}, meaning: that I should get ahead of you to your desires which I have forbidden you, to have them to myself without you." What Abū al-Qāsim mentioned is a good, subtle meaning; he did not deal with the parsing of its individual words, because by understanding the meaning the parsing is understood. Let us mention what is in it.
I say: «أن أخالفكم» may be in the position of an object of «أريد», i.e. "I do not wish to differ from you", with fāʿala in the sense of faʿala, as in جاوَزْتُ الشيءَ and جُزْته ("I passed the thing"), i.e. "I do not wish to go behind your backs", i.e. to be behind you [Translator's note: the source has «أكونَ خَلَفاً منكم»]. His words {إلى مَآ أَنْهَاكُمْ} are attached to «أخالفكم»; or they may be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "inclining to what I forbid you"; and for that reason some supplied an omitted element to which this preposition is attached, its implied form being: "and I incline to differ from you". «أن أخالفكم» may also be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), with «إلى» attached to his words «أريد», meaning: "and I do not aim, for the sake of differing from you, at what I forbid you"; for that reason al-Zajjāj said: "and I do not aim, by differing from you, at committing what I forbid you."
It is also possible that by أن أخالفكم its meaning of "opposition" is intended, it being in the position of the direct object of أريد, with "inclining to" implied.
His words: {مَا استطعت}: several views are possible on this «ما». First, that it is maṣdariyya ẓarfiyya (a temporal verbal-noun particle), i.e. "as long as I am able". Second, that «ما» is a relative noun meaning "that which", a badal (substitute) from «الإصلاح», the implied form being: "I desire only the amount of reform that I am able to." Third, that it is with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "only reform, the reform of what I am able", it too being a substitute. Fourth, that it is a direct object of the definite maṣdar, i.e. "I desire only to reform what I am able to reform", as in the saying:
2697 - ضعيفُ النِّكايةِ أعداءَه ... يخالُ الفِرارُ يُراخي الأجَلْ
(Feeble in harming his enemies, he imagines that flight postpones the appointed term.)
Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned these three views [Translator's note: so in the source, though four are listed]; but the governing of a definite maṣdar is rare according to the Basrans, and its governing a direct object is disallowed according to the Kufans. The two prepositional phrases «عليه» and «إليه» were placed first for restriction (ikhtiṣāṣ), i.e. upon Him and not upon another, and to Him and not to another.

semin-durr:89-89.t:
His words, the Exalted: {لاَ يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ}: the generality read the yāʾ of the imperfect with fatḥa, from the triliteral جَرَم. Al-Aʿmash and Ibn Waththāb read it with ḍamma, from أجرم. It has been stated that «جَرَمَ» takes one object or two, like كسب: one says جَرَم زيدٌ مالاً, like كَسَبه ("Zayd earned wealth"), and جَرَمْتُه ذَنْباً, i.e. "I made him earn a sin", so it is like كَسَب. Al-Zamakhsharī recited, for its taking two objects, the poet's saying:
2698 - ولقد طَعَنْتُ أبا عُيَيْنَة طعنَةً ... جَرَمَتْ فَزارةُ بعدها أن يَغْضَبوا
(I pierced Abū ʿUyayna with a thrust after which [the tribe of] Fazāra earned [the right] to be angry.)
So the kāf and mīm are the first object, and the second is «أن يُصيبكم», i.e. "let not my enmity earn for you the striking of the punishment". It has been stated that جَرَم and أَجْرم are of one meaning, or that there is a difference between them. Al-Zamakhsharī attributed the ḍamma of the yāʾ, from أجرم, to Ibn Kathīr.
The generality also read the lām of «مثلُ» with ḍamma, nominative as the fāʿil (agent) of «يُصيبكم». Mujāhid and al-Jaḥdarī read it with fatḥa, and there are two views on it. First, that it is a fatḥa of indeclinability (bināʾ): it is the agent, as in the well-known reading, and was only made indeclinable on fatḥa because it is annexed to a non-declinable word, as in His words, the Exalted: {إِنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ مِّثْلَ مَآ أَنَّكُمْ تَنطِقُونَ} [al-Dhāriyāt: 23], and as in the saying:
2699 - لمَ يَمْنَعِ الشُّرْبَ منها غيرَ أَنْ نَطقَتْ ... حَمامةٌ في غُصون ذات أَوْقالِ
(Nothing prevented her from drinking but that a dove cooed in branches bearing doum-palm fruit.)
The verification of this rule has preceded in al-Anʿām. Second, that it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, so the fatḥa is of declension, and the agent on this view is implied, explained by the context of the speech, i.e. "that the punishment strike you with a striking like what struck …".
His words: {بِبَعِيدٍ}: «بعيد» was brought in the singular although it is a predicate about a plural for one of several reasons: either because of the omission of a muḍāf, its implied form being: "and the destruction of the people is not …"; or with regard to a time, i.e. "at a distant time"; or with regard to a place, i.e. "at a distant place"; or with regard to a described noun other than these, i.e. "a distant thing". So al-Zamakhsharī gave its implied forms, and the Shaykh followed him. There is a difficulty in this, in that supplying "time" entails predicating a time of a concrete entity (juththa). Al-Zamakhsharī also said: "It is possible that in «قريب», «بعيد», «قليل» and «كثير» masculine and feminine are treated alike, because they come on the pattern of maṣdars such as الصَّهيل (neighing), النهيق (braying) and the like."

semin-durr:90-90.t: {والوَدُود} (al-wadūd) is an intensive form (bināʾ mubālagha) from وَدَّ الشيءَ يَوَدُّه وُدَّاً، ووِداداً، ووِدادَةً وودَادة, meaning "he loved it and preferred it." The well-known form is وَدِدْت with kasra on the ʿayn, and al-Kisāʾī heard وَدَدْت with fatḥa. {الوَدود} has the sense of the active participle (fāʿil), that is, He loves His servants and has mercy on them. It was also said to have the sense of the passive participle (mafʿūl), meaning that His servants love Him and show affection to His friends, so that they are, figuratively, in the position of the "beloved" (al-muwādd).

semin-durr:91-91.t:
{والرَّهْط} (al-rahṭ) is a man's group. It was also said: al-rahṭ and al-rāhiṭ are for fewer than ten men, and al-rahṭ, al-ʿaṣab and al-nafar apply only to men. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "From three to ten; it was also said, up to seven." Its plural is أَرْهُط, and أَرْهُط has the plural أراهِط. The poet said:
2700 - يا بُؤْسَ للحَرْب التي ... وَضَعَتْ أراهِطَ فاستراحوا
(Alas for the war that laid small groups low, so that they found rest.)
Al-Rummānī said: "The origin of the word is from al-rahṭ, which is tightening; from it comes al-tarhīṭ, which is intensity of eating." And al-rāhiṭāʾ is the name of one of the burrows of the jerboa, because it makes itself secure in it and its young live in it.
His saying: {وَمَآ أَنتَ عَلَيْنَا بِعَزِيزٍ}: Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Placing his pronoun directly after the negative particle shows that the statement concerns the agent, not the object, as if it were said: 'You are not mighty to us; rather your clan, they are the mighty ones to us.' That is why he said in reply to them: {أرهطي أَعَزُّ عَلَيْكُم مِّنَ الله}. Had it been said: 'We have not held you mighty' (وما عَزَزْتَ علينا), this reply would not have been valid."

semin-durr:92-92.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {واتخذتموه}: The verb may be the one taking two objects, the first being the hāʾ and the second «ظِهْرِيَّا». It may also be that the second is the adverbial (ẓarf) and «ظِهْرِياً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); or it may be the verb taking one object, in which case «ظِهْرِيَّاً» is only a ḥāl. In «وراءكم» it is permissible that it be an adverbial of the taking, or a ḥāl from «ظهريَّاً». The pronoun in «اتخذتموه» refers to Allah, because they were ignorant of His attributes; so they made, that is, they made His commands «ظِهْريَّاً», that is, cast behind their backs.
And al-ẓihrī is that which is attributed to al-ẓahīr; it is one of the alterations of relative adjectives (nisba), as they said for أَمْس: إمْسِيّ with kasra on the hamza, and for al-dahr: duhrī with ḍamma on the dāl.
It was also said: the pronoun refers to disobedience, that is, "you took disobedience as a helper against enmity towards me"; al-ẓihrī on this reading means the helper and supporter.

semin-durr:93-93.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَن يَأْتِيهِ}: A parallel has already been given in the story of Nūḥ. Ibn ʿAṭiyya, after relating from al-Farrāʾ that it may be a relative noun (mawṣūla) serving as object of «تَعْلمون», or an interrogative (istifhāmiyya) serving as mubtadaʾ that suspends the action (muʿallaqa) of «تعلمون», said: "The first is better." Then he said: "What decides in favour of its being a relative is that the one conjoined to it is certainly a relative." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "That is not necessarily so, since it is possible that the second is also interrogative, conjoined to the interrogative before it, the implied meaning being: 'You will soon know which of us a punishment will come to, and which of us is a liar.'" Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: what is the difference between inserting the fāʾ and omitting it in «سوف تعلمون»? I say: inserting the fāʾ is an overt connection by a particle set down for connection, while omitting it is a hidden, implied connection by resumption (istiʾnāf), which is the answer to an implied question, as if they had said: 'What will happen if we act according to our position and you act according to yours?' So it was said: 'You will soon know.' He connected sometimes with the fāʾ and sometimes by resumption for variety in eloquence, as is the habit of the eloquent among the Arabs; and the stronger and more eloquent of the two connections is resumption, which is a chapter of the science of bayān whose merits are many."
[Translator's note: the source text contains a stray slash in "يأتيه/ عذابٌ"; translated as written.]

semin-durr:94-94.t: His saying, the Exalted: {وَلَمَّا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا}: Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: what is the matter with the two outer ends of the story of ʿĀd and the story of Madyan, that they came with the wāw, while the two middle ones came with the fāʾ? I say: the two middle ones occurred after mention of the promise, namely His saying {إِنَّ مَوْعِدَهُمُ الصبح} and {ذلك وَعْدٌ غَيْرُ مَكْذُوبٍ}, so the fāʾ of causation (tasabbub) was used, as you say: 'I promised him, and when the appointed time came, such and such happened.' As for the other two, they did not occur in that position; they occurred as beginnings, so the proper thing was for them to be conjoined with the conjunctive particle to what precedes them, as one story is conjoined to another." And this is among the finest of al-Zamakhsharī's words.

semin-durr:98-98.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَأَوْرَدَهُمُ}: This issue may belong to the chapter of iʿmāl (the competition of two operators for one word), because «يَقْدُمُ» can govern «النار» by means of a preposition, that is, "he leads his people to the Fire," and likewise «أَوْرَدَهم» can govern it too. The second operator would then be the one that acts, with omission from the first; had the first acted, it would have been made transitive by «إلى» and a pronoun would have been supplied in the second. «أَوْرَدَ» has no grammatical position, because it is resumptive. It is past in form but future in meaning, because it is conjoined to something explicit about the future. The hamza in «أَوْرَدَ» is for transitivity, because before it the verb takes one object. The Exalted said: {وَلَمَّا وَرَدَ مَآءَ مَدْيَنَ}. It was also said: the past is used here because its occurrence is certain. And it was said: rather it is a true past, and this has already happened and is over, for he brought them to the Fire in this world. The Exalted said: {النار يُعْرَضُونَ عَلَيْهَا} [Ghāfir: 46]. And it was said: he brought them to what necessitates it and its causes; but this is remote because of the conjunction with the fāʾ.
Al-wird may be a verbal noun (maṣdar) with the sense of al-wurūd (arrival), or may mean the thing that is brought to, like al-ṭiḥn (what is ground) and al-riʿy (what is pastured). It is also used for the one who arrives. On this basis, if you take al-wird as a maṣdar or as meaning the one who arrives, an omitted muḍāf is necessary, its implied form being: "wa-biʾsa makānu l-wirdi l-mawrūd" (evil is the place of arrival that is arrived at), namely the Fire. This implied form is needed only because it is a condition that the agent of niʿma and biʾsa and its specified subject (makhṣūṣ) refer to the same thing; one does not say "niʿma l-rajulu l-faras" (excellent is the man, the horse). It was also said: rather «المورود» is an adjective of al-wird, and the makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm is omitted, its implied form being: "biʾsa l-wirdu l-mawrūdu l-nāru" (evil is the arrival that is arrived at: the Fire). Abū l-Baqāʾ and Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed this, and it is the apparent sense of al-Zamakhsharī's words. It was also said that the implied form is: "biʾsa l-qawmu l-mawrūdu bihim hum" (evil are the people who are led to it, they), so that on this view «الورد» means the plural, those who arrive, «والمورود» is their adjective, and the makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm is the omitted pronoun «هم»; the censure then applies to those who arrive, not to the place of arrival. So said the Shaykh. There is an obvious problem in it: how can al-wird be meant as the plural "those who arrive" and then he says that «المورود» is their adjective? And regarding describing the specified subject of niʿma and biʾsa there is a disagreement among the grammarians; Ibn al-Sarrāj and Abū ʿAlī forbade it.
[Translator's note: the source has a stray slash after "لموضع الوِرْد".]

semin-durr:99-99.t:
And {بِئْسَ الرفد المرفود} is like the one before it. His saying «ويومَ القيامة» is conjoined to the position of «في هذه», and the meaning is that a curse was attached to them in this world and in the Hereafter; the pause on this reading is complete, and one begins with «بِئْس».
A group claimed that the division is: they have a curse in this world, and on the Day of Resurrection, "evil is what they are given as a gift"; so it is one curse first and an ugly gift later. This is not sound, because it leads to «بئس» acting upon what precedes it, which is not permitted because it is not a conjugated verb. Had it come later it would be permitted, as in his saying:
2705 - ولَنِعْمَ حَشْوُ الدِّرْعِ أنت إذا ... دُعِيَتْ نَزَالِ ولُجَّ في الذُّعْرِ
(How excellent a one to fill the coat of mail you are, when "Dismount!" is called and panic rages.)
The origin of al-rifd, as al-Layth said, is giving and help; from it comes rifādat Quraysh. "I gave him a rifd" (rafadtuhu arfiduhu rifdan and rafdan, with kasra or fatḥa on the rāʾ) means "I gave him and helped him." It was also said: with fatḥa it is a maṣdar and with kasra a noun, as if like al-riʿy and al-dhibḥ. One says "rafadtu l-ḥāʾiṭ," meaning "I propped up the wall," which is from the sense of helping.

semin-durr:100-100.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {ذَلِكَ مِنْ أَنْبَآءِ القرى نَقُصُّهُ}: «نقصُّه» may be the khabar and «مِنْ أنباء» a ḥāl, or the reverse. It was said that there is an omitted muḍāf, that is, "from the reports of the people of the towns," which is why the pronoun is returned to them in His saying «وما ظلمْناهم».
His saying: {مِنْهَا قَآئِمٌ وَحَصِيدٌ}: «حصيد» is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, as the khabar of the first indicates it, that is, "and of them some are mown down"; this is by necessity of the meaning.
Does this sentence have a grammatical position? Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It has none, because it is resumptive." Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the object of «نَقُصُّه»."
In «ذلك» several analyses are allowed. First: it is a mubtadaʾ, as already given. Second: it is accusative by an implied verb which «نقصُّه» explains, so it belongs to the chapter of ishtighāl, that is, "We relate that while it is among the reports of the towns." Analyses were already given for His saying {ذلك مِنْ أَنَبَآءِ الغيب نُوحِيهِ إِلَيكَ} [Āl ʿImrān: 44], and they apply here again.
«الحَصِيد» has the sense of «محصود» (mown); its plural is ḥaṣdā and ḥiṣād, like marīḍ, marḍā and mirāḍ. This is the view of al-Akhfash. However, the pattern faʿīl/faʿlā normally applies to rational beings, like qatīl and qatlā.

semin-durr:101-101.t: His saying, the Exalted: {لَّمَّا جَآءَ أَمْرُ}: Al-Zamakhsharī said: «لما» is accusative by «أَغْنَتْ». This is built on his view that «لمَّا» is adverbial (ẓarfiyya). The apparent sense is that «ما» is negative, that is, "did not avail." It may also be interrogative. «يَدْعون» is a depiction of a past state, that is, "those they used to call upon." In «ما زادوهم» the nominative pronoun refers to the idols and the accusative one to their worshippers; the idols are referred to with the wāw of rational beings because the worshippers set them in the position of the rational.

semin-durr:102-102.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وكذلك}: a fronted khabar, and «أَخْذُ» a delayed mubtadaʾ; the implied form is: "and like that seizing by which Allah seized the earlier nations is the seizing of your Lord." «إذا» is a pure adverbial (ẓarf), governed by the maṣdar before it, which is close to a depiction of a past state. The issue belongs to the chapter of tanāzuʿ (competition between two operators), since the maṣdar al-akhdh seeks «القرى» and the verb «أَخَذَ» also seeks it, and the matter is one of the second operator acting with omission from the first.
Abū Rajāʾ and al-Jaḥdarī read: «أَخَذ ربك، إذ أَخَذَ», making both past verbs with «ربُّك» as agent. Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read likewise, except with «إذا» like the majority. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is a reading firm in meaning, but the reading of the majority gives the threat and its continuation in time, which is the typical use of putting the future in place of the past."
His saying: {وَهِيَ ظَالِمَةٌ} is a circumstantial clause (jumla ḥāliyya).
Al-tatbīb is causing loss. One says: "tabbaba another, then he himself perished (tabba)"; so it is used both intransitively and transitively, and from it {تَبَّتْ يَدَآ أَبِي لَهَبٍ وَتَبَّ} [al-Masad: 1]. "I caused him loss" (tabbabtuhu tatbīban) means "I made him lose." Labīd said:
2706 - ولقد بَلِيْتُ وكلُّ صاحبِ جِدَّةٍ ... لِبِلىً يعودُ وذاكمُ التَّتْبيبُ
(I have worn out, and every owner of newness returns to decay; that is perdition.)

semin-durr:103-103.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {ذلك يَوْمٌ}: «ذلك» points to the Day of Resurrection, which the context indicates through His saying «عذابَ الآخرة». «مجموع» is an adjective of «اليوم» that runs on something other than the one it describes; therefore it raises the overt noun, which is «الناس». This is the i'rāb, as in "I passed by a man whose slave is beaten" (مررت برجلٍ مضروبٍ غلامُه). Ibn ʿAṭiyya parsed «الناس» as a delayed mubtadaʾ and «مجموع» as its fronted khabar. This is weak; for were it so, it would have been said «مجموعون», as one says "al-nās qāʾimūn and maḍrūbūn," and one does not say "qāʾim" and "maḍrūb" except weakly. And on his parsing a returning pronoun must be omitted, since the sentence is an adjective of the day; it is the hāʾ in «له», that is, "the people are gathered for it." «مشهود» must be an adjective, and so too what precedes it.
His saying {مَّشْهُودٌ} is an instance of extension (ittisāʿ) in the adverbial, in that He made it "witnessed," when what is witnessed is something in it. It is like his saying:
2707 - ويومٍ شَهِدْناه سُلَيْماً وعامِراً ... قليلٌ سوى الطعنِ النِّهالِ نوافلُهْ
(Many a day we witnessed, with Sulaym and ʿĀmir, its extra spoils little besides the thirsty spear-thrusts.)
The original is "witnessed in it" and "we witnessed in it"; extension was made by having the verb reach its pronoun directly, without an intermediary, as it reaches the direct object. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: what is the benefit of preferring the passive participle to the verb? I say: the passive participle indicates the permanence of the meaning of gathering for the day, that it must be an appointed time fixed for gathering people for it, and that it is characterised by that as a constant attribute."
[Translator's note: the source has a stray slash after "في الظرف" and the quotation marks in the first paragraph are as printed.]

semin-durr:104-104.t: The pronoun in «نُؤَخِّره» refers to «يوم». Al-Ḥūfī said: "To the requital (al-jazāʾ)." Al-Aʿmash read: «وما يُؤَخِّره», meaning Allah the Exalted.

semin-durr:105-105.t:
Abū ʿAmr, al-Kisāʾī and Nāfiʿ read «يأتي» with the yāʾ retained in connected speech and dropped in pause. Ibn Kathīr read it with the yāʾ retained in both connected speech and pause, and the rest of the Seven read it dropped in both connected speech and pause. The codices have come down both with it and without it: in the codex of Ubayy it is retained, in the codex of ʿUthmān it is dropped. Retaining it is the sounder form, because it is the lām of the word (the final radical); they dropped it only in rhyme-endings and verse-endings, since these are places of pause, and they said "lā adri" and "lā ubāli." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Making do with the kasra in place of the yāʾ is frequent in the dialect of Hudhayl," and Ibn Jarīr cited in this regard:
2708 - كفَّاك كفٌّ ما تُليقُ دِرْهماً ... جُوْداً وأخرى تُعْطِ بالسيف الدَّما
(Your two hands: one hand holds no dirham back, out of generosity, and the other gives blood by the sword.)
The governor of this adverbial has several analyses. First: «لا تَكَلَّمُ», the implied form being "no soul speaks on the day that day comes." This is a good meaning and there is no need for another. Second: it is accusative by an implied «واذكر» ("and remember"). Third: it is accusative by the omitted "ending" (intihāʾ) in His saying «إلا لأجل», that is, "the term ends on the day it comes." Fourth: it is accusative by an implied «لا تَكَلَّم», and there is no need for it.
The sentence «لا تَكَلَّمُ» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun of the day mentioned earlier in «مشهود», or as an adjective of it because it is indefinite. The implied form is "no soul speaks in it except by His leave." So said al-Ḥūfī. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «لا تكلَّم نفسٌ» may be a sentence in the position of ḥāl from the pronoun in «يأتي», which refers to His saying «ذلك يومٌ»; on this there is an omitted returning pronoun, its implied form being "no soul speaks in it." It may also be that {لاَ تَكَلَّمُ نَفْسٌ} is an adjective of «يوم يأتي».
The agent of «يأتي» has two analyses. The more apparent: it is the pronoun of the preceding «يوم». Second: it is the pronoun for Allah the Exalted, as in His saying {هَلْ يَنظُرُونَ إِلاَّ أَن يَأْتِيَهُمُ الله} [al-Baqara: 210] and His saying {أَوْ يَأْتِيَ رَبُّكَ}. The pronoun in «فمنهم» apparently refers to the people in {مَّجْمُوعٌ لَّهُ الناس}. Al-Zamakhsharī made it refer to the people of the standing place, although they were not mentioned, saying: "because that is known, and because His saying {لاَ تَكَلَّمُ نَفْسٌ} indicates it." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said likewise.
His saying: {وَسَعِيدٌ}: its khabar is omitted, that is, "and among them some are blessed," as in His saying {مِنْهَا قَآئِمٌ وَحَصِيدٌ} [Hūd: 100].

semin-durr:106-106.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {شَقُواْ}: The majority read it with fatḥa on the shīn, because it is from shaqiya, an intransitive verb. Al-Ḥasan read it with ḍamma, using it transitively, so that one says shaqāhu llāh, as one says ashqāhu llāh.
The two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) and Ḥafṣ read «سُعِدُوا» with ḍamma on the sīn, and the rest with fatḥa. The first is from their saying "saʿadahu llāh," that is, asʿadahu. Al-Farrāʾ related from Hudhayl that they say saʿadahu llāh in the sense of asʿada. Al-Jawharī said: "saʿida, so he is saʿīd, like salima, so he is salīm; and suʿida, so he is masʿūd." Ibn al-Qushayrī said: "saʿadahu llāh is attested, so he is masʿūd, and asʿada, so he is musʿad." It was also said: one says saʿadahu and asʿadahu, and he is masʿūd, being content with the passive participle of the triliteral. It was related from al-Kisāʾī that he said: "They are two dialectal forms with one meaning," meaning faʿala and afʿala. Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said: "One says suʿida l-rajul as one says junna." It was also said that saʿidahu is a dialectal form.
A group considered the reading of the two brothers weak. Al-Mahdawī said: "Whoever read «سُعِدوا» has based it on masʿūd, and it is rare and anomalous (shādhdh), because one does not say saʿadahu llāh; one says only asʿadahu llāh." Some said: al-Kisāʾī argued from their saying "masʿūd." It was said: there is no proof in it, because one says "a masʿūd place" meaning "a place in which one is made happy," then "فيه" (in it) was dropped and it was used as a name. ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān used to marvel at al-Kisāʾī's reading «سُعِدوا» despite his knowledge of Arabic, and the marvel is at his marvelling. Makkī said: "The reading of Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī «سُعِدوا» with ḍamma on the sīn is based on their saying «مسعود»; it is a rare, anomalous dialectal form, and their saying «مَسْعود» came only by dropping the augments, as if from asʿadahu llāh, and one does not say saʿadahu llāh. It is like their saying ajannahu llāh, so he is majnūn, which came from jannahu llāh although that is not said, just as saʿadahu llāh is not said."
The ḍamma on the sīn is remote according to most grammarians, except on the basis of dropping the augments. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "This is not known in the language, nor is it analogically derived."
His saying: {لَهُمْ فِيهَا زَفِيرٌ}: this sentence has two possibilities. One: it is resumptive, as if a questioner asked, when it was reported that they are in the Fire, "What will they have?" and it was said "They have such and such." Two: it has a position of accusative, and its owner has two analyses: one, that it is the pronoun in the preposition and its genitive noun, that is «ففي النار»; two, that it is a ḥāl from «النار».
Al-zafīr is the beginning of the donkey's cry and al-shahīq is its end. Ruʾba said:
2709 - حَشْرَجَ في الصدر صَهِيْلاً وشَهَقْ ... حتى يُقالَ ناهِقٌ وما نَهَقْ
(He rattled in his chest a neighing and gasped, until it was said "a brayer," though he had not brayed.)
Ibn Fāris said: "Al-shahīq is the opposite of al-zafīr, because al-shahīq is drawing the breath back in, and al-zafīr is expelling the breath out of intense grief, taken from al-zifr, which is a load carried on the back, because of its heaviness." Al-Zamakhsharī said the like, and cited a verse by al-Shammākh:
2710 - بعيدٌ مدى التَّطْريْبِ أولُ صوتِه ... زفير ويَتْلوه شهيق مُحَشْرِج
(Far-reaching in its trilling range, its first sound a zafīr, followed by a rattling shahīq.)
It was also said: al-shahīq is the prolonged breath, taken from their saying "a jabal shāhiq," that is, high. Al-Layth said: "Al-zafīr is when a man fills his chest with breath while in intense distress and then lets it out, and al-shahīq is letting that breath out; it is close to their saying 'he sighed deeply.'" Abū l-ʿĀliya and al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas said: "Al-zafīr is in the throat and al-shahīq in the chest." It was also said: al-zafīr is for the donkey and al-shahīq for the mule.
[Translator's note: the source has a stray slash before «سُعِدوا» in the passage on ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān, and the quotation marks in the Ibn Fāris and Makkī passages are unbalanced as printed.]

semin-durr:107-107.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {خَالِدِينَ}: accusative as an implied ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara). I say: there is no need for their saying "implied"; they needed the implication only in a case like His saying {فادخلوها خَالِدِينَ} [al-Zumar: 73], because abiding comes after entering, unlike here.
His saying: {مَا دَامَتِ}: «ما» is a temporal maṣdar particle, that is, "for the duration of their remaining." «دام» here is complete (tāmma, not needing a predicate), because it means "remained."
His saying: {إِلاَّ مَا شَآءَ رَبُّكَ}: there are many scattered views on it, which I have summarised in fourteen analyses.
First: that which al-Zamakhsharī mentioned. He said: "If you ask: what is the meaning of the exception in His saying {إِلاَّ مَا شَآءَ رَبُّكَ}, when the eternal abiding of the people of Paradise and of the Fire is established without exception? I say: it is an exception from abiding in the punishment of the Fire and from abiding in the bliss of the people of Paradise. For the people of the Fire do not abide in its punishment alone; rather they are punished by the zamharīr (bitter cold), by other kinds of punishment, and by something more severe than that, namely Allah's wrath upon them. Likewise the people of Paradise have, along with the bliss of Paradise, something greater than it, as in His saying {وَرِضْوَانٌ مِّنَ الله أَكْبَرُ} [al-Tawba: 72]. The proof of it is His saying {عَطَآءً غَيْرَ مَجْذُوذٍ} [Hūd: 108], and in contrast to it {إِنَّ رَبَّكَ فَعَّالٌ لِّمَا يُرِيدُ}, that is, He does to them what He wills of punishment, just as He gives the people of Paradise what has no end." The Shaykh said: "What he mentioned about the people of the Fire may work, because they leave the Fire for the zamharīr, so the exception is sound; but the people of Paradise do not leave Paradise, so the exception is not sound for them." I say: the apparent view is that it is not sound for either, because the people of the Fire, even while punished with the zamharīr, are also in the Fire.
Second: that it is an exception from the time indicated by His saying «خالدين فيها ما دامَتِ السماواتُ والأرضُ»; the meaning being: except the time that Allah has willed, in which they do not abide in it.
Third: that it is from His saying «ففي النار» and «ففي الجنة», that is, except the time that Allah has willed, in which one is neither in the Fire nor in Paradise. It is possible that this excepted time is the time in which Allah judges between creatures on the Day of Resurrection, if the exception is from being in the Fire or in Paradise, because it is a time in which the wretched and the blessed are free of entering the Fire and Paradise. As for if the exception is from abiding, this is possible with respect to the people of the Fire, and the excepted time would be the time that passes for the sinning believers among the people of the Fire, who leave the Fire and enter Paradise, so they are not abiding in the Fire, since they have been brought out of it and gone to Paradise. This meaning is reported from Qatāda, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and others, and «الذين شَقُوا» on this view includes unbelievers and sinners. This is possible on the side of the wretched sinners; as for the other side, this interpretation cannot be applied to it, since none of them enters Paradise and then does not abide in it.
The Shaykh said: That is possible, by taking it that what is meant is the time that passes for the sinning believers among the people of the Fire, or that passes for the people of al-Aʿrāf; for with the passing of that period in which the believers enter Paradise and abide in it, it holds true of the sinning believers and the people of al-Aʿrāf that they did not abide in Paradise with the abiding of those who entered it at the first moment.
Fourth: that it is an exception from the latent pronoun in the preposition and its genitive noun, His saying «ففي النار» and «ففي الجنة», because when it occurs as a khabar it carries the pronoun of the mubtadaʾ.
Fifth: that it is an exception from the latent pronoun in the ḥāl, «خالدين». On these two views «ما» refers to one who has intellect, according to those who hold that, or to kinds of those with intellect, as in {مَا طَابَ لَكُمْ مِّنَ النسآء} [al-Nisāʾ: 3]. What is meant by «ما» then is the sinning believers on the side of the people of the Fire; and on the side of the people of Paradise, they may be those same ones or the people of al-Aʿrāf, because they did not enter Paradise at the first moment and did not abide in it with the abiding of those who entered first.
Sixth: Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It was said that this is by way of the exception (istithnāʾ) that the Lawgiver recommended using in all speech, so it is like His saying {لَتَدْخُلُنَّ المسجد الحرام إِن شَآءَ الله آمِنِينَ} [al-Fatḥ: 27], an exception in something certain; and this exception has the force of a condition, as if He said 'if Allah wills,' so it does not need to be described as connected or disconnected."
Seventh: it is an exception from the length of the period. It is reported from Ibn Masʿūd and others that Jahannam will be emptied of people and its doors will bang, and that is His saying {إِلاَّ مَا شَآءَ رَبُّكَ}. This is refuted by the apparent texts of the Book and the Sunna; and as for what I mentioned from Ibn Masʿūd, its interpretation is that Jahannam is the highest level and it empties of the sinning believers; this is on the assumption that what was transmitted from Ibn Masʿūd is sound.
Eighth: that «إلا» is a conjunction in the sense of the wāw, so the meaning of the verse is: "and whatever your Lord wills in addition to that."
Ninth: that the exception is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), so it is taken as "lākin" or "siwā" (except/besides), and they compared it to your saying "You owe me two thousand dirhams, except the thousand I lent you," meaning besides that one. So it is as if it were said: "abiding in it as long as the heavens and the earth endure, besides what your Lord wills in addition to that." It was also said: besides what He has prepared for them of punishment other than the punishment of the Fire, such as the zamharīr and the like.
Tenth: that it is an exception from the duration of the heavens and the earth that was set for them in the life of this world.
Eleventh: that it is an exception from the gradual progression between this world and the Hereafter.
Twelfth: that it is an exception from the intervals between them in entering the Fire, since they enter only in groups, one after another.
Thirteenth: that it is an exception from His saying «ففي النار», as if He said: "except what your Lord wills of some people being held back from that." This is reported from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī and Jābir.
Fourteenth: that «إلا ما شاء» is equivalent to "as He wills." It was said: like His saying {مَا نَكَحَ آبَاؤُكُمْ مِّنَ النسآء إِلاَّ مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ} [al-Nisāʾ: 22], that is, "as has already passed."
[Translator's note: the source has a stray slash in the Shaykh's passage ("يمكن ذلك/ باعتبار"); the quotation marks are unbalanced in places as printed.]

semin-durr:108-108.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {عَطَآءً}: accusative as a confirming maṣdar of the meaning of the preceding sentence, because His saying «ففي الجنة خالدين» entails giving and bestowing favour, so it is as if it were said: "He gives them a gift." ʿAṭāʾ is a noun of the verbal noun (ism maṣdar), and the true maṣdar is al-iʿṭāʾ on the pattern of ifʿāl; or it is a maṣdar by dropping the augments, as in His saying {أَنبَتَكُمْ مِّنَ الأرض نَبَاتاً} [Nūḥ: 17]; or it is accusative by an implied verb of the same root, that is, "so you grew a growth." Likewise here one says ʿaṭawtu in the sense of "I took."
«غيرَ مَجْذوذ» is its adjective. Al-majdhūdh is "cut off." The fragments of gold, silver and stone are called judhādh, from that, and it is close in meaning to al-jadd with the undotted dāl, except that al-Rāghib made jadda with the undotted dāl mean cutting level ground, and from it "he went hard (jadda) in his journey, yajiddu jaddan." Then he said: "From jadadtu [the ground] the bare cutting was conceived, so it was said jadadtu l-thawb when you cut it for the purpose of repair; and thawb jadīd originally means cut, then it was applied to everything newly produced." The apparent view is that the two roots are close in meaning, and I have mentioned parallels for them, such as ʿatā and ʿathā, kathaba and kataba.

semin-durr:109-109.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مِّمَّا يَعْبُدُ}: «ما» in «ممَّا يعبد» and in «كما يَعبْدُ» is a maṣdar particle. It is permissible for the first to be a noun (ismiyya, relative) but not the second.
His saying: {لَمُوَفُّوهُمْ}: the majority read it with shadda, from waffāhu (with shadda). Ibn Muḥaysin read «لَمُوْفُوْهم» without shadda, from awfā, as in His saying {وَأَوْفُواْ بعهدي} [al-Baqara: 40]; it was already mentioned in al-Baqara that it has three dialectal forms.
His saying: {غَيْرَ مَنقُوصٍ}: a ḥāl from «نصيبهم», and there are two possibilities. One: it is a confirming ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida), because the wording of tawfiya (paying in full) implies absence of shortfall, so its meaning is derived from its operator, which is the nature of the confirming ḥāl. Two: it is a clarifying ḥāl (ḥāl mubayyina). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: how is «غيرَ منقوص» put in the accusative as a ḥāl from the portion paid in full? I say: it may be paid in full while deficient, and paid in full while complete. Do you not see that you say: 'I paid him half of his right, a third of his right, and his right complete and deficient'?" The apparent sense of this statement is that it is clarifying, since its operator admits its meaning and others. But the Shaykh said after quoting him: "This is a fallacy. When he says 'I paid him half of his right,' the paying occurred in the half, and likewise in the third, and the meaning is: I gave him the half and the third complete, not diminishing anything of it. As for his saying 'and his right complete and deficient': 'complete' is sound, and it is a confirming ḥāl, because tawfiya requires completion; but 'deficient' is not said, because it contradicts tawfiya." There is something to consider in the Shaykh's prohibition of saying "I paid him his right deficient," since it is common in the usage of people whose speech is reliable, because what is meant by tawfiya is simply discharging.
[Translator's note: the source has a stray slash after «ما» at the beginning of the entry, and the quotation marks are unbalanced as printed.]

semin-durr:110-110.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فاختلف فِيهِ}: that is, about the Book. «في» is in its basic sense of containment (ẓarfiyya), which is figurative here, that is, about its matter. It was also said that it denotes cause (sababiyya), that is, it is the cause of their disagreement, as in the saying of the Exalted {يَذْرَؤُكُمْ فِيهِ} [al-Shūrā: 11], that is, He multiplies you by means of it. It was also said that it means «على» (upon), and the pronoun then refers to Mūsā, peace be upon him, that is, "they disagreed about him."
«مُرِيْب» is from arāba, when doubt (rayb) is produced in another, or when he himself becomes one having doubt; this has already been given.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {كِتَابٌ}: It is permissible that it be the khabar (predicate) of «ألر», He reporting of these letters that they are a book described by such-and-such; and that it be the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: "that is a book", which is indicated by its appearing overtly in His saying, the Exalted: {ذَلِكَ الكتاب} [al-Baqara: 2]; and what suffices you on that was given at the beginning of this work.
His saying: {أُحْكِمَتْ آيَاتُهُ}: It is in the position of nominative as an adjective of «كتاب». The hamza in «أُحْكِمَتْ» may be for transfer (naql) from «حَكُمَ» with ḍamma on the kāf, that is: "became wise", in the sense "were made wise", as in His saying, the Exalted: {تِلْكَ آيَاتُ الكتاب الحكيم} [Luqmān: 2]. It may be from their saying «أَحْكَمْتُ الدابة» when you put the ḥakama (bridle-bit) on it to prevent it from bolting, as in the saying of Jarīr:
2633 - أبني حَنِيْفَةَ أَحْكِموا سُفَهاءَكمْ ... إني أخاف عليكمُ أَنْ أَغْضبا (O sons of Ḥanīfa, restrain your fools; I fear for you that I may grow angry)
so the meaning is that they were prevented from corruption. It may also be not for transfer, from iḥkām, which is perfecting, like a well-built, well-ordered structure; the meaning is: that they were composed in a firm, perfected composition.
His saying: {ثُمَّ فُصِّلَتْ}: «ثم» is in its usual sense of delay, because they were first made firm and then set out in detail, according to the occasions of revelation. ʿIkrima, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Jaḥdarī, Zayd b. ʿAlī and Ibn Kathīr in one transmission read «فَصَلَتْ» with two fatḥas and a light ʿayn. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "The meaning is: separated, as in His saying {فَلَمَّا فَصَلَ طَالُوتُ} [al-Baqara: 249], that is: departed." Others explained it here as "distinguished between the one in the right and the one in the wrong", which is better. Al-Zamakhsharī made «ثم» for ordering in reporting and not for ordering of occurrence in time, and said: "If you say: what is the meaning of «ثم»? I say: its meaning is not delay in time but in rank, as you say: it is perfectly firm, then perfectly detailed; and so-and-so is noble in origin, then noble in action." It was also read: «أحْكَمْتُ آياتِه ثم فَصَّلْتُ» with both verbs ascribed to the tāʾ of the first person and «آياته» accusative as direct object, that is: "I made its verses firm, then I set them out in detail"; al-Zamakhsharī reported this reading.
His saying: {مِن لَّدُنْ}: It is permissible that it be a second adjective of «كتاب», and that it be a second khabar according to those who permit that; and it is permissible that it be governed by one of the two preceding verbs, I mean «أُحْكِمَتْ» or «فُصِّلَتْ», this being of the chapter of conflict (tanāzuʿ), with the second verb taking effect, since had the first been given effect, a pronoun would have been implied in the second. Al-Zamakhsharī leaned to this in his saying: "and that it be connected with «أُحْكِمت» and «فُصِّلَتْ», that is: from the presence of One whose is their making firm and their setting out in detail, and there is a fine antithesis in it, because the meaning is: a Wise One made them firm, and a Well-Informed One of the manners of things set them out in detail, that is, explained and clarified them." The Shaykh said: "He does not mean that «مِنْ لدن» is attached to both verbs together from the point of view of the craft of i'rab, but means that it is of the chapter of effect (iʿmāl), so it is attached to them both by meaning." And that is also the meaning of the saying of Abū l-Baqāʾ: "and it is permissible that it be an object, the operator in it being «فُصِّلَتْ»."

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَن لاَّ تعبدوا}: There are several aspects regarding it. One: that it is the lightened form of the heavy «أنَّ», and «لا تَعْبُدوا» is a prohibitive clause in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the lightened «أنْ», and its ism, as established, is an omitted pronoun of the matter and affair (ḍamīr al-amr wa-l-shaʾn). Second: that it is the maṣdar particle that governs the accusative, and here it has been connected with the prohibition; it is also permissible that «لا» be negative, with the verb after it accusative by «أَنْ» itself. On all these analyses «أَنْ» is either in the position of genitive, accusative or nominative. The accusative and genitive are on the basis that the origin is «لأنْ لا تَعْبدوا» or «بأن لا تعبدوا»; when the preposition was dropped, the well-known disagreement arose. The operator is either «فُصِّلَتْ», which is the well-known view, or «أُحْكِمَتْ» according to the Kufans, so that the question is of the chapter of effect (iʿmāl), because the meaning is: "they were made firm so that you do not worship" or "that you not worship", or "they were set out in detail so that you not worship" or "that you not worship". It was also said: it is accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being: "He made the verses of the Book contain that you not worship", so «أنْ لا تعبدوا» is the second object of «ضَمَّن» and the first stands in the place of the agent.
The nominative is in several ways. One: that it is a mubtadaʾ, with an omitted khabar; it was said its implied form is: "of the consideration is that you not worship any but Allah"; it was said its implied form is: "in the Book is that you not worship any but Allah". The second: the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; it was said its implied form is: "its detailing is that you not worship any but Allah"; it was said its implied form is: "it is that you not worship any but Allah". The third: that it is nominative as a badal (substitute) from «آياته». The Shaykh said: "As for the one who gave the i'rab that it is a badal from the wording of «آيات» or from its position." I say: he means that in origin it is a direct object, so its position is accusative; and it is a matter of disagreement: whether it is permissible to take into account the origin of the object that stands in place of the agent, so that its wording is followed at one time and its position at another, so that one says «ضُرِبَتْ هندٌ العاقلة» with «العاقلة» accusative by considering the position and nominative by considering the wording, or not; two schools; the well-known one takes the wording alone into account.
The third [sic]: that it be explicative (tafsīriyya), because in the detailing of the verses there is the meaning of saying, as if it had been said: "Do not worship any but Allah", or "He commanded you"; and this is the most apparent of the views, because it does not require any implication. [Translator's note: the source numbers this "third" a second time.]
His saying: «منه»: There are two aspects regarding this pronoun. One, which is the apparent, is that it refers back to Allah the Exalted, that is: "I am to you a warner and bearer of glad tidings from the side of Allah." The Shaykh said: "So it would be in the position of an adjective, attached to an omitted word, that is: 'coming from His side'." On its face this is not good, because an adjective may not precede what it qualifies, so how can it be made an adjective of «نذير»? It is as if he means that it is in origin an adjective had it come after, but when it came first it became a ḥāl; so also Abū l-Baqāʾ stated explicitly; so the proper wording for him is to say: "so it would be in the position of ḥāl, the implied form being: 'coming from His side'." The second: that it refers back to the Book, that is: "a warner to you against opposing it, and a bearer of glad tidings from it to whoever believes and does good."
Regarding what this preposition and noun is attached to there are also two aspects. One: that it is a ḥāl from «نذير», so it is attached to an omitted word as mentioned. The second: that it is attached to «نذير» itself, that is: "I warn you of it and of its punishment if you disbelieve, and I give you glad tidings of its reward if you believe." He put the warning first because frightening is more important, since deterrence results from it.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَأَنِ استغفروا}: There are two aspects regarding it. One: that it is conjoined to the first «أنْ», whether the «لا» after it is negation or prohibition, so the aspects reported regarding it return to this «أَنْ». The second: that it is accusative as an incitement (ighrāʾ). Al-Zamakhsharī said on this aspect: "It may be a fresh speech, cut off from what precedes it, on the tongue of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, as an incitement from him to confine worship to Allah the Exalted; and what indicates it is His saying «إني لكم منه نذيرٌ وبشير», as if he said: 'Abandon the worship of any but Allah! I am to you a warner from Him', like His saying, the Exalted: {فَضَرْبَ الرقاب} [Muḥammad: 4]."
His saying: {ثُمَّ توبوا}: It is conjoined to the preceding command to seek forgiveness, and «ثم» is in its usual sense of delay, because one first seeks forgiveness, then repents and strips oneself of that sin for which forgiveness was sought. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what is the meaning of «ثم» in {ثُمَّ توبوا إِلَيْهِ}? I say: its meaning is: seek forgiveness from polytheism, then return to Him in obedience; or: seek forgiveness, and seeking forgiveness is repentance, then make the repentance sincere and be steadfast in it, as in His saying, the Exalted: {ثُمَّ استقاموا} [al-Aḥqāf: 13]." I say: his saying "or seek forgiveness" to the end means that some made seeking forgiveness and repentance one meaning, so he needed to interpret «توبوا» as «أَخْلِصوا التوبة» (make repentance sincere).
His saying: {يُمَتِّعْكُمْ}: It is the response to the command (jawāb al-amr). The disagreement about what makes it jussive has already been given: whether it is the request clause itself or an implied conditional particle. Al-Ḥasan, Ibn Hurmuz, Zayd b. ʿAlī and Ibn Muḥayṣin read «يُمْتِعْكم» in the light form, from amtaʿa; and it has already been mentioned that Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read {فَأُمَتِّعُهُ قَلِيلاً} [al-Baqara: 126] in al-Baqara in the light form like this reading.
His saying: {مَّتَاعاً}: There are two aspects for its accusative. One: that it is accusative as a maṣdar by dropping the additional letters, as the implied form is: "tamtīʿan"; so it is like His saying: {أَنبَتَكُمْ مِّنَ الأرض نَبَاتاً} [Nūḥ: 17]. The second: that it is accusative as a direct object, "matāʿ" meaning the name of what is enjoyed, so it is like your saying: «متَّعْتُ زيداً أثواباً» ("I gave Zayd garments to enjoy").
His saying: {كُلَّ ذِي فَضْلٍ فَضْلَهُ}: «كلَّ» is the first object and «فضلَه» the second object; al-Suhaylī's disagreement on this has already been given. The pronoun in «فضله» may refer back to Allah the Exalted, that is: "He gives every possessor of merit his merit", that is, his reward; or refer back to the word «كل», that is: "He gives every possessor of merit the requital of his merit, not diminishing anything of it", that is, the requital of his deeds.
His saying: {وَإِن تَوَلَّوْاْ}: The majority read «تَوَلَّوا» with fatḥa on the tāʾ and the wāw and a doubled lām, and there are two possibilities in it. One: that the verb is the imperfect of tawallā, one of the two tāʾs having been dropped for lightness, like tanazzalu — which of the two was dropped has already been given — and this is the apparent one, and for that reason the address came in His saying «عليكم». The second: that it is a past verb ascribed to the pronoun of the absent plural, and the address came on the implication of saying, that is: "so say to them: I fear for you", and were it not for that, the construction would have been: «فإني أخاف عليهم».
Al-Yamānī and ʿĪsā b. ʿUmar read «تُوَلُّوا» with ḍamma on the tāʾ, fatḥa on the wāw and ḍamma on the lām, which is the imperfect of wallā, like your saying zakkā yuzakkī. The author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» reported from al-Yamānī and ʿĪsā: «وإن تُوُلُّوا» with three ḍammas, passive. I say: he did not make clear what it is or its morphology. It is a past verb; when it was made passive its first letter was given ḍamma for the passive, and its second letter too, because it begins with a tāʾ of mutual action (muṭāwaʿa), and every verb that begins with a tāʾ of muṭāwaʿa has its first and second letters given ḍamma; and the lām was given ḍamma too, although its origin is kasra, because of the wāw of the pronoun; the origin is «تُوُلِّيُوا», like tudūḥirajū; the ḍamma on the yāʾ was found heavy, so it was dropped and two sukūns met, so the yāʾ was dropped because it was the first of them, leaving what precedes the wāw of the pronoun with kasra, which was given ḍamma to match the pronoun; its pattern thus became «تُفُعُّوا» with its lām dropped, and the wāw standing in place of the agent.
Al-Aʿraj read «تُوْلُوا» with ḍamma on the tāʾ, sukūn on the wāw and ḍamma on the lām, the imperfect of awlā; no weighty meaning appears for this reading here, and the object is omitted, to be implied in a way fitting the meaning.
And «كبير» is an adjective of «يوم», as an exaggeration of the terrors that occur in it. It was also said: rather «كبير» is an adjective of «عذاب», and it is accusative but was put in the genitive by proximity (jiwār), like their saying «هذا جُحْرُ ضَبٍّ خَرِبٍ» with «خَرِبٍ» in the genitive though it is an adjective of «جُحر», and the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
2634 - كأن ثَبِيراً في عَرانين وَبْلِه ... كبيرُ أناسٍ في بِجادٍ مُزَمَّل (As if Thabīr, amid the first drops of its downpour, were a great man of the people wrapped in a striped cloak)
with «مُزَمّل» in the genitive, though it is an adjective of «كبيرُ». The discussion of this has already been given at length in Sūrat al-Māʾida.

[Translator's note: In the source, the last paragraph («و "كبير" صفةٌ ل "يوم" …») appears without a heading and belongs to the commentary on {عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ كَبِيرٍ}; also the source's sentence on «تُوْلُوا» and the omitted object ends without a full stop.]

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {يَثْنُونَ}: The reading of the majority is with fatḥa on the yāʾ and sukūn on the thāʾ (mathalatha), the imperfect of thanā yathnī thanyan, that is: to fold and to turn aside; and «صدورَهم» is the direct object, and the meaning is: "they turn their breasts and their faces away from the truth and from accepting it". The origin is «يَثْنِيُون», which was modified by dropping the ḍamma from the yāʾ, then the yāʾ was dropped because of the meeting of two sukūns.
Saʿīd b. Jubayr read «يُثْنُون» with ḍamma on the yāʾ, the imperfect of athnā, like akrama.
People found this reading difficult. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "Its past is athnā, which is not known in the language, unless it is said that its meaning is: they exposed them to bending, as one says abaʿtu al-faras when you expose it for sale." The author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» said: "Ithnāʾ is not known in this chapter, unless what is meant is: I found them bent, like aḥmadtuhu and amjadtuhu; perhaps he put fatḥa on the nūn, and this is among what is done to them, so «صدورَهم» would be accusative by removal of the preposition; and in addition to that it is permissible that «صدورهم» be nominative as a badal (substitute), a badal of the part from the whole." I say: by his saying "perhaps he put fatḥa on the nūn" he means that perhaps Ibn Jubayr read «يُثْنَون» with fatḥa on the nūn, so that it is passive, which is the meaning of his saying "and this is among what is done to them", that is: they were found thus.
