On this «صدورَهم» would be accusative by removal of the preposition, that is: "in their breasts", that is: the bending is found in their breasts; for that reason he permitted its nominative as a badal, like your saying «ضُرِب زيدٌ الظهرُ». And for whoever permits the definiteness of the tamyīz (specification), it is not remote that «صدورَهم» be accusative as tamyīz with this implied form that he implied.
Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿAlī b. al-Ḥusayn and his two sons Zayd and Muḥammad and his son Jaʿfar, Mujāhid, Ibn Yaʿmar, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Abzā and Abū l-Aswad read «تثنونى», the imperfect of «اثنونى», on the pattern ifʿawʿala from al-thany, like iḥlawlā from ḥalāwa, which is a pattern of intensity, with «صدورُهم» nominative as agent. It was reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Yaʿmar, Mujāhid and Ibn Abī Isḥāq: «يثنونى صدورُهم» with tāʾ and yāʾ, because the feminine is figurative, so it is permissible to make the verb masculine in consideration of its agent being interpreted as a plural, and feminine in consideration of its agent being interpreted as a collective.
Ibn ʿAbbās also read, as did ʿUrwa, Ibn Abzā and al-Aʿshā, «تَثْنَوِنُّ» with fatḥa on the tāʾ, sukūn on the thāʾ, fatḥa on the nūn, kasra on the wāw and a doubled last nūn; the origin is «تَثْنَوْنِنُ» on the pattern tafʿawʿilu, from al-thinn, which is the tender and weak part of pasture, wishing to express the compliance of their souls to bending as tender plants are bent, or intending the weakness of their faith and the sickness of their hearts. And «صدورُهم» is nominative as agent.
Mujāhid and ʿUrwa also read it likewise, except that they put in place of the wāw with kasra a hamza with kasra, making it like «تطمئن». There are two explanations of it. One: that the wāw was turned into a hamza because of the heaviness of the kasra upon it, and the like of it are ʾiʿāʾ and ʾishāḥ for wiʿāʾ and wishāḥ; when they found the kasra heavy on the wāw they replaced it with a hamza.
The second: that its pattern is tafʿaylu from al-thinn, which is the weak part of plants as mentioned; that is because it is the imperfect of «اثْنانَّ», like iḥmārra and iṣfārra, and you have already been told that some Arabs turn the like of this alif into a hamza, as in the saying:
2635 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . بالعَبيطِ ادْهَأَمَّتِ (… with fresh blood it turned dark green)
So the imperfect of ithnaʾanna comes out in that way, like your saying iḥmaʾarra yaḥmaʾirru, like iṭmaʾanna yaṭmaʾinnu. As for «صدورُهم», it is nominative as already given.
Al-Aʿshā also read «تَثْنَؤُوْنَ» with fatḥa on the tāʾ, sukūn on the thāʾ, fatḥa on the nūn, and a hamza with ḍamma and a sākin wāw, on the pattern tafʿalūna like tarhabūna. «صدورَهم» is accusative. The author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» said: "I do not know its aspect, because one says «ثَنَيْتُ» and I have not heard «ثَنَأْت»; it is possible that he turned the yāʾ into an alif, in the dialect of those who say «أَعْطَات» for aʿṭaytu, then pronounced the alif with a hamza, in the dialect of those who say {وَلاَ الضألين} [al-Fātiḥa: 7]."
Ibn ʿAbbās also read «تَثْنَوي» with fatḥa on the tāʾ, sukūn on the thāʾ, fatḥa on the nūn and kasra on the wāw followed by a sākin yāʾ, on the pattern tarʿawī; this is an extremely problematic reading, so that Abū Ḥātim said: "This reading is a mistake and cannot be made to work." He said it is a mistake only because the wāw has no meaning in this verb, since one does not say «ثَنَوْتُه فانثوى», like «رَعَوْته», that is, "I restrained him so he restrained himself" (fa-irtawā), and its pattern is ifʿalla like iḥmarra.
Naṣr b. ʿĀṣim, Ibn Yaʿmar and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read «يَثْنُون» with the sākin nūn put before the thāʾ.
Ibn ʿAbbās also read «لتَثْنَوْنِ» with the lām of emphasis in the khabar of «inna», fatḥa on the tāʾ, sukūn on the thāʾ, fatḥa on the nūn, sukūn on the wāw followed by a nūn with kasra; it is on the pattern tafʿawʿilu as already mentioned, except that the tāʾ which is the lām of the verb was dropped for lightness, like their saying «لا أدرِ» and «ما أَدْرِ». And «صدورُهم» is the agent as already given.
A group read «تَثْنَؤُنَّ» with fatḥa on the tāʾ, then a sākin thāʾ, then a nūn with fatḥa, then a hamza with ḍamma, then a doubled nūn, like «تَقْرَؤُنَّ»; it is from thanaytu, except that he turned the yāʾ into a wāw because the ḍamma is incompatible with it, so the vowel was given to its congener, and the form became «تَثْنَوُوْنَ»; then the wāw with ḍamma was turned into a hamza, as they say «أُجوه» for «وُجوه» and «أُقِّتَتْ» for «وقِّتت», so it became «تَثْنَؤُون»; when the verb was emphasised with the nūn of emphasis, the nūn of the nominative was dropped and two sukūns met, namely the wāw of the pronoun and the first nūn of the nūn of emphasis, so the wāw was dropped and the ḍamma remained to indicate it, so it became «تَثْنَؤُنَّ» as you see. And «صدورَهم» is accusative as direct object. These are eleven readings, whose vocalisation by word and clarification of morphology I have taken pains over, because I saw them in the books left without precise wording and most of their morphology, as if they relied on the vocalisation by marks in writing; and that is very tiring.
His saying {لِيَسْتَخْفُواْ}: There are two aspects. One: that this lām is attached to «يَثْنُون», and so said al-Ḥawfī, the meaning being that they bend their breasts for this cause. This meaning is reported in the exegesis and there is no strain in it. The second: that the lām is attached to an omitted word. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«ليَسْتَخْفُوا منه», meaning 'and they want to hide from Allah, so that He not inform His Messenger and the believers of their turning away'; and the like of implying 'they want', because the meaning returns to implying it, is the implication in His saying, the Exalted: {أَنِ اضرب بِّعَصَاكَ البحر فانفلق} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 63], whose meaning is «فضرب فانفلق» (so he struck and it split)." I say: the meaning that leads us to imply the verb there is not like the meaning here, because there an omitted conjoined verb must be implied, which the mind is compelled to supply, since the splitting of the sea is not a necessary consequence of the command to strike, so «فضرب فانفلق» must be understood; as for this one, concealment is a fitting cause for their bending their breasts, so we are under no compulsion to imply the wanting.
The pronoun in «منه» has two aspects. One: that it refers back to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, which is apparent on the lām being attached to «يَثْنون». The second: that it refers back to Allah the Exalted, as al-Zamakhsharī said.
His saying: {أَلا حِينَ يَسْتَغْشُونَ}: There are two aspects regarding this adverb. One: that its governor is implied; al-Zamakhsharī implied it as «يريدون», as already mentioned, and said: "The meaning of «ألا حين يَسْتَغْشُون ثيابهم» is: and they want concealment also when they cover themselves with their garments, out of dislike of hearing the words of Allah, like the saying of Nūḥ, peace be upon him: {جعلوا أَصَابِعَهُمْ في آذَانِهِمْ واستغشوا ثِيَابَهُمْ} [Nūḥ: 7]." Abū l-Baqāʾ implied it and said: «ألا حين يَسْتَغْشون ثيابهم يَسْتخفون» ("when they cover themselves with their garments, they conceal themselves"). The second: that its governor is «يَعْلَمُ», that is: "Does He not know their secret and their open act when they do such-and-such?", and this is a clear meaning; it is as if they permitted something else only so as not to be forced to restrict His knowledge of their secret and open act to this particular time, whereas He, the Exalted, knows that at every time. This is not necessary, because if their secret and open act is known at the time of covering, in which a secret is hidden, then all the more so at any other time; and this is by custom, otherwise Allah the Exalted has no variation in His knowledge. And «ما» may be a maṣdar particle, and may be in the sense of «الذي» with the returning pronoun omitted, that is: "what you conceal and what you disclose".

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مُسْتَقَرَّهَا وَمُسْتَوْدَعَهَا}: It is permissible that both be maṣdars, that is: "its settling and its deposit"; and permissible that both be places, that is: "the place of its settling and of its deposit". It is also permissible that «مستودعها» be a passive participle since its verb is transitive; but that is not permissible for «مستقر», because its verb is intransitive. The like of it as maṣdar is the saying of the poet:
2636 - ألم تعلمْ مُسَرَّحِيَ القوافي ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . (Do you not know my sending out of the verses …)
that is: my sending out (tasrīḥī).
His saying: {كُلٌّ}: The word it is annexed to is omitted, its implied form being: "every creature, and its provision, its settling-place and its deposit-place, are in a clear book."

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ}: There are two aspects regarding this lām. One: that it is attached to an omitted word. It was said its implied form is: "He made known by that, so that He might test you." It was said: there are omitted clauses there and the implied form is: "and His creating them for benefits whose use returns to you in this world and not the next, and He did that to test you." It was said: its implied form is: "and He created you to test you." The second: that it is attached to «خلق». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "that is: He created them for a profound wisdom, which is that He make them dwellings for His servants and bestow on them in them kinds of favours, and charge them to perform acts of obedience and avoid acts of disobedience; whoever is grateful and obeys, He rewards, and whoever disbelieves and disobeys, He punishes. Since that resembles the testing of a tester, He said «ليبلوَكم», meaning: to do with you what one who tries your conditions does."
His saying: {أَيُّكُمْ أَحْسَنُ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of accusative by removal of the preposition, because it suspends (muʿallaq) His saying «ليبلوكم». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: how is it permissible to suspend the verb of testing? I say: because testing contains the meaning of knowledge, since it is a way to it, so it is connected with it, as you say «انظر أيُّهم أحسنُ وجهاً» ('see which of them has the finer face') and «واسمع أيُّهم أحسنُ صوتاً» ('and listen to which of them has the finer voice'), because seeing and listening are among the ways of knowledge." The Shaykh took him to task for his example with his saying «واسمع», and said: "I do not know anyone who mentioned that «استمع» is suspended; they mentioned, other than verbs of the heart, «سَلْ» and «انظر», and there is a disagreement about the permissibility of suspending the visual «رأى»."
His saying: {وَلَئِن قُلْتَ}: This is the lām of preparation for the oath, and «ليقولُنَّ» is its response, the response of the condition being omitted because the response of the oath indicates it; and «إنكم» is quoted after saying, and for that reason it has kasra in the reading of the majority. It was also read with fatḥa, and there are two interpretations of it mentioned by al-Zamakhsharī. One: that it is in the sense of «لعلَّ». He said: "from their saying «ائت السُّوق أنك تشتري لحماً»" (go to the market; perhaps you will buy meat), that is, "perhaps you", that is: "if you say to them: perhaps you will be raised, meaning: expect your being raised and think it likely, and do not make a flat denial of it, they would say…". The second: that «قلتَ» is made to contain the meaning of «ذَكَرْتَ» (you mentioned), meaning the hamza takes fatḥa because it is the object of «ذكرْتَ».
His saying: {إِنْ هاذآ إِلاَّ سِحْرٌ}: It has already been mentioned that «سِحْر» and «ساحر» were both read. For the one who read «سِحْر», «هذا» points to the resurrection, which is indicated by what precedes, or points to the Qurʾān, because it speaks of the resurrection. For the one who read «ساحر», «هذا» points to the Prophet ﷺ. It is also permissible that «هذا» in the first reading mean the Prophet ﷺ as well, and that they made him "magic" as an exaggeration, or on the omission of a muḍāf, that is: "except a possessor of magic". It is also permissible that «ساحر» mean the Qurʾān itself figuratively, like their saying «شعرٌ شاعرٌ» (a poet's poetry) and «جَدَّ جَدُّه» (his fortune became fortunate).

semin-durr:111-111.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِنَّ كُلاًّ لَّمَّا لَيُوَفِّيَنَّهُمْ}: This noble verse is among those on which people have spoken, anciently and recently, and most of them have found it hard to summarise, as to reading and analysis. Allah the Exalted has made it easy, so I have mentioned their statements and which of them is preferred.
Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read «وإنْ» with lightening (takhfīf), and the others with shadda. As for «لمَّا», Ibn ʿĀmir, ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza read it with shadda here, in Yā Sīn, in Sūrat al-Zukhruf, and in Sūrat al-Samāʾ wa-l-Ṭāriq; except that there is a disagreement about Ibn ʿĀmir in al-Zukhruf: Hishām related two ways from him, and Ibn Dhakwān related only the lightening from him. The others read all of those with lightening. The upshot: Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr read «وإنْ» and «لَمَا» both lightened; Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim lightened «إنَّ» and doubled «لمَّا»; Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim doubled both «إنَّ» and «لمَّا»; and Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī doubled «إنَّ» and lightened «لَمَّا». These are four levels of the readers on these two particles.
This concerns the mutawātir readings. As for the irregular ones, four more readings were read. One: the reading of Ubayy, al-Ḥasan and Abān ibn Taghlib, «وإنْ كل» with «إنْ» lightened and «كل» in the nominative, and «لَمَّا» with shadda. Two: the reading of al-Yazīdī and Sulaymān ibn Arqam, «لمَّاً» with shadda and tanwīn; they did not address lightening or doubling of «إنَّ». Three: the reading of al-Aʿmash, which is also so in the letter (ḥarf) of Ibn Masʿūd: «وإنْ كلٌّ إلا», with «إنْ» lightened and «كل» in the nominative. Four: Abū Ḥātim said: "What is in the codex of Ubayy is {وإنْ مِنْ كلٍ إلا لَيُوَفِّيَنَّهم}."
This is what concerns it from the side of recitation. As for what concerns it from the side of analysis, people have been greatly troubled by it, so that Abū Shāma said: "As for this verse, its meaning on the various readings is among the most difficult of verses. The way to make it easy, with Allah's help, is for me to mention each reading on its own and what has been said about it."
As for the reading of the two Ḥaramayn readers (Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr): in it the lightened «إنْ» is made to act, which is a second dialectal usage of the Arabs. Sībawayh said: "One we trust told us that he heard from the Arabs someone who says: «إنْ عمراً لمنطلقٌ»," just as they said:
2711 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... كأن ثَدْيَيْهِ حُقَّانِ
(as if her two breasts were two small boxes)
He said: "Its justification by analogy is that «إنْ» resembles the verb in its governing the accusative, and a verb acts when omitted as it acts when not omitted, as in «لم يكُ زيد منطلقاً» and {فَلاَ تَكُ فِي مِرْيَةٍ} [Hūd: 109], and likewise «لا أَدْرِ»." I say: this is the position of the Basrans, that is, that when some of these particles are lightened they may act or be left unused, like «إنْ», the more frequent being non-action, and there is consensus on it in His saying {وَإِن كُلٌّ لَّمَّا جَمِيعٌ لَّدَيْنَا [مُحْضَرُونَ]}. Some of them must act, like «أنْ» with fatḥa and «كأنْ», but these two do not act on an overt noun or an overt pronoun except by poetic necessity; and some of them must be left unused according to the majority, like «لكن».
As for the Kufans, they make non-action obligatory for the lightened «إنْ», but the transmitted usage is proof against them, by the evidence of this mutawātir reading. Sībawayh cited as evidence of these particles acting when lightened his verse:
2712 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... كأنْ ظبيةٌ تَعْطُو إلى وارِقِ السَّلَمْ
(as if a gazelle were reaching toward the green leaves of the salam tree)
Al-Farrāʾ said: "We have not heard the Arabs lighten and make it act except with the attached pronoun, as in his saying:
2713 - فلو أنْكِ في يومِ الرَّخاء سَأَلْتِني ... طلاقَكِ لم أَبْخَلْ وأنتِ صديقُ
(If you had asked me, in a day of ease, for your divorce, I would not have been niggardly, and you a true friend.)
He said: "because no case ending shows in an attached pronoun, whereas with an overt noun it is nominative." I say: what Sībawayh cited has already been given, and the saying of another:
2714 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... كأنْ ثَدْيَيْه حُقَّانِ
and [his saying]:
2715 - كأنْ وَرِيْدَيْه رِشاءُ خُلْبِ
(as if his two jugular veins were a rope of palm fibre)
This is what concerns «إنْ». As for «لَمَا» in this reading, the lām in it is the lām of «إنْ» entering the khabar. «ما» may be a relative noun (mawṣūla) meaning "the one who," applied to one with intellect, as in the saying of the Exalted {فانكحوا مَا طَابَ لَكُمْ مِّنَ النسآء} [al-Nisāʾ: 3], where «ما» is applied to a rational being. The lām in «ليوفِّيَنَّهم» is the answer of an implied oath, and the sentence of the oath and its answer is the ṣila of the relative, the implied form being: "and every one of them is of those whom, by Allah, He will pay in full." It is also possible that here it is an indefinite described noun (nakira mawṣūfa), and the oath sentence and its answer is the description of «ما», the implied form being: "and every one is a creation, or a group, whom, by Allah, He will pay in full," the relative and its ṣila, or the described and its description, being the khabar of «إنْ».
Some said: the first lām is the one that prepares for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa), and when the two lāms came together and were identical in form, they were separated by «ما», as they separate with an alif the two nūns in «يَضْرِبْنانِّ» and the two hamzas in a case like «أأنت». The apparent sense of this statement is that «ما» here is redundant, brought in for separation to improve the wording. Al-Fārisī's statement indicates this, except that he made the first lām the lām of «إنْ», saying: "The custom is to enter the lām of ibtidāʾ on the khabar; the khabar here is the oath, and in it is a lām that enters its answer. When the two lāms came together, the oath being omitted, and they were alike in form and in receiving the oath, they separated them as they separated between inna and the lām."
Al-Zamakhsharī stated this explicitly, saying: "The lām in «لَمَا» is the one preparing for the oath and «ما» is added." Al-Ḥūfī stated that it is the lām of «إنْ». Abū Shāma said: "The lām in «لَمَا» is the distinguishing lām (al-fāriqa) between the lightened form of the heavy particle and the negative." There is something to consider in this, because the distinguishing lām is brought only when it would be confused with the negative, and confusion arises only when it is left unused, as in «إنْ زيدٌ لقائم»; in the noble verse it acts, so there is no confusion with the negative, so it is not said to be a distinguishing lām.
In summary, for each of the lām and «ما» there are three analyses. For the lām: first, that it is the lām of ibtidāʾ entering the khabar of «إنْ»; second, a lām preparing for the oath; third, that it is the answer of the oath, repeated for emphasis. For «ما»: first, that it is a relative; second, that it is indefinite; third, that it is added to separate the two lāms.
As for the reading of Abū Bakr, it has several analyses. One: what al-Farrāʾ and a group of the grammarians of Basra and Kufa held, that the origin is «لَمِنْ ما» with kasra on the mīm, «مِنْ» being the preposition entering the relative or indefinite «ما», as established, that is: "of those whom, by Allah, He will pay in full," or "of a creation whom, by Allah, He will pay in full." When the nūn, being sukūn, came before the mīm of «ما», assimilation became obligatory, so it was changed into a mīm and assimilated, and three identical letters appeared in the pronunciation, so the word was lightened by dropping one of them, and the word became, as you see, «لمَّا». Naṣr ibn ʿAlī al-Shīrāzī said: "He joined the prepositional «مِنْ» to «ما», and the nūn was also changed into a mīm for assimilation, so three mīms came together and one of them was dropped, leaving «لمَّا» with shadda." He said: "«ما» here has the sense of «مَنْ», which is a noun for a group of people, as the Exalted said {فانكحوا مَا طَابَ لَكُمْ مِّنَ النسآء}, that is, whoever pleases you; and the meaning is: 'Every one of those whom your Lord will pay in full for their deeds, or a group whom your Lord will pay in full for their deeds.'"
Al-Mahdawī specified the mīm that is dropped, saying: "The mīm with kasra is dropped, and the implied form is «لَمِنْ خلقٍ ليوفِّيَنَّهم»."
Two: what al-Mahdawī and Makkī held, that the origin is «لمَنْ ما» with fatḥa on the mīm of «مَنْ», it being a relative or indefinite, with «ما» after it added. He said: "The nūn was changed into a mīm and assimilated into the mīm after it, so three mīms came together and the middle one among them, which is the one substituted for the nūn, was dropped, so it was said «لَمَّا»." Makkī said: "The implied form is: «وإنْ كلاً لَخَلْقٌ لَيوفينَّهم ربك أعمالهم»," so it returns to the meaning of the first reading with lightening. This is what al-Zajjāj related from some, saying: "Some of the grammarians claimed that its origin is «لمَنْ ما», then the nūn was changed into a mīm, so three mīms came together and the middle one was dropped." He said: "This statement is nothing, because one may not drop part of «مَنْ», for it is a noun of two letters."
Al-Naḥḥās said: "Abū Isḥāq said: This is a mistake, because the nūn of «مَنْ» would be dropped and one letter would remain." Al-Fārisī also rejected it, saying: "Since assimilation was not strong enough to move a sākin before the assimilated letter, as in «قدم مالك», it is all the more fitting that dropping not be allowed." He said: "Moreover, in this sūra there are mīms that come together in assimilation more than would come together in «لَمَنْ ما», and nothing was dropped from them, namely in His saying {وعلى أُمَمٍ مِّمَّن مَّعَكَ} [Hūd: 48]; so if nothing is dropped from this, then it is all the more fitting that nothing be dropped there." I say: in «أمم ممَّن مَعَك» eight mīms came together, because «أمماً» has two mīms and a tanwīn, and the tanwīn is changed into a mīm for assimilation into the mīm of «مِنْ»; and we have two nūns, the nūn of the prepositional «مِنْ» and the nūn of the relative «مَنْ», which are likewise changed into a mīm for assimilation into the mīm after them; and we have the mīm of «معك»; so we have five pronounced mīms and three changed ones, one from tanwīn and two from nūn.
Al-Farrāʾ cited as proof that the origin of «لَمَّا» is «لمِنْ ما» the poet's saying:
2716 - وإنَّا لمِنْ ما نَضْرِبُ الكبشَ ضَرْبَةً ... على رأسِه تُلقي اللسانَ من الفم
(We are of those who strike the ram a blow on his head that throws the tongue from the mouth.)
and the saying of another:
2717 - وإني لَمِنْ ما أُصْدِرُ الأمرَ وجهَه ... إذا هو أَعْيا بالسبيل مصادرُهْ
(I am of those who bring a matter out the right way when its ways of exit have wearied the path.)
I say: it has already been given in Sūrat Āl ʿImrān, in the reading of one who read {وَإِذْ أَخَذَ الله مِيثَاقَ النبيين لَمَآ آتَيْتُكُم} [Āl ʿImrān: 81] with «لمَّا» doubled, that the origin is «لمن ما» and what was said above was done with it; that is one of the analyses mentioned for this particle in its sūra, and I mentioned there what people said about it, so look into it.
Abū Shāma said: "What al-Farrāʾ said is a fine deduction, and it is close to their saying {لَّكِنَّ هُوَ الله رَبِّي} [al-Kahf: 38], whose origin is «لكن أنا», then the hamza was dropped and the nūn assimilated into the nūn; and likewise their saying «أمَّا أنت منطلقاً انطلقت», in which they said the meaning is «لأِنْ كنتَ منطلقاً»." I say: there is something to consider in what he said, for there is no dropping at all in it; the comparison would have been good only if what he brought involved assimilation and then dropping; as for a mere comparison by change and assimilation, it is of no use.
Then Abū Shāma said: "How fine was what he (al-Farrāʾ) derived as evidence from the verse." Then al-Farrāʾ wanted to unite the lightened and doubled readings of «لمَّا» in a single meaning, so he said: "Then it is lightened, as some readers read {والبغي يَعِظُكُمْ} [al-Naḥl: 90]  by dropping the yāʾ before the yāʾ. Al-Kisāʾī recited to me:
2718 - وأَشْمَتَّ العُداةَ بنا فأَضْحَوا ... لَدَيْ يَتباشَرُون بما لَقِينا
(You made our enemies gloat over us, so they became, in our presence, rejoicing at what we met with.)
So he dropped its yāʾ because of the meeting of yāʾs." I say: it is better to say that the yāʾ of the genitive construct was dropped from «لديّ», leaving the sākin yāʾ before it, which is changed from the alif in «لدى»; this is like the reading of one who read {يابني} with sukūn, as already given. As for the yāʾ of «يتباشرون», it is retained because it indicates the imperfect.
Then al-Farrāʾ said: "Similar to it:
2719 - كأنَّ مِنْ آخِرِها إلقادِمِ
he means «إلى القادم», and he dropped the lām before the lām."
I say: the justification of their saying «من آخرها إلقادم» is that the alif of «إلى» was dropped because of the meeting of two sākin letters; for the alif of «إلى» is sākin and the lām of definiteness in «القادم» is sākin, and the hamzat al-waṣl is dropped in connected speech; when the two met, the first was dropped, so two lāms met, the lām of «إلى» and the lām of definiteness, and the second was dropped on his view. It is better to drop the first, because the second indicates definiteness. Nothing remained of the letters of «إلى» but the hamza, which joined the lām of «القادم», and the hamza stayed with its kasra; that is why this word is pronounced from its end «ءِ القادم» with a kasra hamza retained in connected speech, because it is a hamzat al-qaṭʿ.
Abū Shāma said: "This is close to their saying «مِلْكذب», «عَلْماءِ بنو فلان» and «بَلْعنبر», meaning «من الكذب», «على الماء بنو فلان» and «بنو العنبر»." I say: he means the saying:
2720 - أبْلِغْ أبا دَخْتنوسَ مَأْلُكَةً ... غيرُ الذي [قد] يُقال مِلْكذب
(Convey to Abū Dakhtanūs a message other than what is said, of lying.)
and the saying of another:
2721 - فما سَبَقَ القَيْسِيَّ مِن سُوءِ فِعْلِهِ ... ولكنْ طَفَتْ عَلْماءِ غُرْلَةُ خالدِ
(The Qaysī was not outstripped through his bad deed, but Khālid's foreskin floated on the water.)
Some have rejected al-Farrāʾ's statement, saying that the nūn of «مِنْ» is dropped only by necessity, and they cited: «مِلكذبِ».
Three: that its origin is «لَما» lightened and then doubled. Abū ʿUthmān held this. Al-Zajjāj said: "This is nothing, because we do not double what is of two letters; and further, the speech of the Arabs is the reverse of this: they lighten what is doubled, as in «رُبَ» for «رُبَّ»." It was said in justifying it: that applies only to a letter when it is final, whereas the mīm here is in the middle, because the alif follows it; unless it is said that he made the middle letter take the rule of the final one, as in his saying:
2722 - ... مثلَ الحريقِ وافَقَ القَصَبَّا
meaning «القصبَ»; when he lengthened the fatḥa an alif was generated from it and the letter was doubled. Likewise his saying:
2723 - ببازِلٍ وَجْناءَ أو عَيْهَلِّي
where he doubled the lām although it is in the middle, with the yāʾ of release. One may distinguish by saying that the alif and the yāʾ in these two verses are in the rule of the discarded, because they arose from a vowel, unlike the alif of «لما», which is original and fixed. In sum, it is a very weak analysis.
Four: that its origin is «لَمَّاً» with tanwīn, from which a pattern faʿlā was then built; if you make its alif for the feminine, you do not make it fully declinable, and if you make it for annexation (ilḥāq), you do, just as they said of «تَتْرى» with tanwīn and without. It is taken from your saying lamamtuhu, that is, "I gathered it," and the implied form is: "and every one, all together, He will pay in full," «جميعاً» having in it the sense of emphasis like «كل», and without doubt «جميعاً» gives, according to some, a sense additional to «كل». He said: "And what shows that is the reading of one who read «لمَّاً» with tanwīn."
Five: that the origin is also «لَمَّاً» with tanwīn, then the tanwīn was changed into an alif in pause, then connected speech was made to take the rule of pause. Abū ʿUbayd forbade this analysis, saying: "because that is permitted only in poetry," meaning changing the tanwīn into an alif in connected speech, treating it as pause. The justification of the reading «لَمَّاً» with tanwīn will come after this.
Abū ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥājib said: "Using «لَمَّا» in this sense is remote, and dropping the tanwīn from a fully declinable word in connected speech is more remote. If it is said: «لَمَّاً» is a faʿlā from al-lamm, and is made diptote because of the alif of the feminine, with the meaning like that of the declinable «لمَّاً», it is more remote still, since «لمَّا» as a faʿlā is not known in this sense or any other; and these people would then have to incline the alif (imāla) like those who incline it, which is contrary to consensus, and to write it with a yāʾ, and that is not right."
Six: that «لَمَّا» is redundant, as «إلا» is added; Abū l-Fatḥ and others said this. This is an analysis not to be considered, for it is also built on a weak analysis, namely that «إلا» comes as redundant.
Seven: that «إنْ» is negative, equivalent to «ما», and «لمَّا» means «إلا»; so it is like His saying {إِن كُلُّ نَفْسٍ لَّمَّا عَلَيْهَا} [al-Ṭāriq: 4], that is, "every soul has only a guardian over it," and {وَإِن كُلُّ ذَلِكَ لَمَّا مَتَاعُ} [al-Zukhruf: 35], that is, "all that is only the enjoyment of." This analysis was objected to on the ground that the negative «إنْ» does not put the noun after it in the accusative, whereas this is an accusative noun after it. Some answered that «كلاً» is accusative by an implied verb, which some, among them Abū ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥājib, supplied as: "and I see every one," "and I know," and the like. He said: "On this account it is less problematic than the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir, because it accepts this analysis which is not as improbable, even though there is improbability in putting the noun after a negative particle in the accusative. That is why there is disagreement about a case like his saying:
2724 - ألا رجلاً جزاه اللَّه خيراً ... يَدُلُّ على مُحَصِّلةٍ تَبيتُ
(Is there not a man, may Allah reward him well, to guide me to a means of earning that I may spend the night on?)
whether it is accusative by an implied verb or took tanwīn by necessity; al-Khalīl preferred the implied verb, and Yūnus preferred tanwīn by necessity." Some supplied after «لمَّا» a verb from the wording of «ليُوَفِّينَّهم», the implied form being: "and every one, only to be paid in full, He will pay them in full." There is great remoteness or impossibility in this implication, because what follows «إلا» does not act on what precedes it. The holders of this view, namely that «لَمَّا» comes with the sense of «إلا», argued from the explicit statement of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh on it, and al-Zajjāj supported it. One said: "It is the dialect of Hudhayl; they say: 'I ask you by Allah, lammā you do it', meaning 'only that you do it'." Al-Farrāʾ and Abū ʿUbayd denied that «لمَّا» comes in the sense of «إلا». Abū ʿUbayd said: "As for one who doubled «لمَّا» with the interpretation of «إلا», we have not found this in the speech of the Arabs, and whoever said this would have to say «قام القوم لمَّا أخاك», meaning 'except your brother', and that is not found."
Al-Farrāʾ said: "As for one who made «لَمَّا» the equivalent of «إلا», it is an analysis we do not know. The Arabs in Yemen said 'by Allah, lammā you rose from us' and 'illā you rose from us', but in exception we have not said it in poetry or anything else. Do you not see that if it were permitted, you would hear in speech 'the people went, lammā Zayd'?"
So Abū ʿUbayd denied «لمَّا» coming with the meaning of «إلا» altogether, while al-Farrāʾ allowed that only in the oath, and al-Fārisī followed him in that, for he said regarding the doubling of «لمَّا» in this verse: "It cannot be in the sense of «إلا», because this «لَمَّا» does not separate from the oath." People rejected his statement by what al-Khalīl and Sībawayh related, and by its being the dialect of Hudhayl absolutely; but there is something to consider in that, for when they related the Hudhaylī dialect they related it in the oath, as given above, such as «نَشَدْتُك باللَّه لمَّا فعلت» and «أسألك باللَّه لمَّا فعلت». Abū ʿAlī also, finding the doubling of «لمَّا» in this sūra problematic on the supposition that «لمَّا» in the sense of «إلا» is not restricted to the oath, said, in meaning: that doubling «لمَّا» is weak whether you double «إن» or lighten it. He said: "because «كلاً» is put in the accusative by it, and when it is put in the accusative by the lightened one it is like the heavy one; and as «إنَّ زيداً إلا منطلق» is not good, because it is affirmation after negation, and here nothing precedes except an emphatic affirmation, so likewise «إن زيداً لما منطلق» is not good, because it means the same. «نَشَدْتُك اللَّهَ إلا فعلت ولمَّا فعلت» is permissible only because its meaning is a request, as if he said 'I ask nothing of you except that you do,' so the negative particle is intended, like {تَالله تَفْتَؤُاْ} [Yūsuf: 85]." He also gave as an example their saying «شَرٌ أهرُّ ذاناب», that is, "nothing made him growl except evil." He said: "And in the verse there is neither the sense of negation nor of request." Al-Kisāʾī said: "I do not know the justification for the doubling in «لمَّا»." Al-Fārisī said: "He did not go far from the mark in what he said." It was also related from al-Kisāʾī that he said: "Allah the Mighty and Majestic knows best about this reading; I do not know a justification for it."
Eight: al-Zajjāj said: "Some said a view for which no other is permitted: that «لمَّا» means «إلا», like {إِن كُلُّ نَفْسٍ لَّمَّا عَلَيْهَا حَافِظٌ} [al-Ṭāriq: 4]." Then he followed that with a long, difficult discussion whose gist returns to this: that the meaning of «إنْ زيدٌ لمنطلق» is «ما زيد إلا منطلق», so you treat the doubled one the same in this meaning when the lām is in its khabar, and its action of putting its noun in the accusative remains as it is, doubled and lightened; the meaning is negation by «إنْ» and affirmation by the lām which means «إلا», and «لمَّا» means «إلا».
I say: Abū ʿAlī's denial of the permissibility of «إلا» in a construction like this has already been given, so how could «لمَّا», which has its meaning, be permitted?
As for the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza and Ḥafṣ, it has several analyses. One: that it is the doubled «إنَّ» as it is, so what follows is accusative as its noun; as for «لمَّا», the discussion about it is as given above, that the origin is «لَمِنْ ما» with kasra or «لَمَنْ ما» with fatḥa, and all the analyses I mentioned come back here. The view that it means «إلا» is problematic, as al-Fārisī's treatment of it was set out here.
Two: al-Māzinī said: «إنَّ» is the lightened one made heavy, and it is negative with the sense of «ما», just as «إنَّ» was lightened while having the meaning of the heavy, and «لَمَّا» means «إلا». This is a thoroughly invalid view, not to be considered, because making the negative «إنْ» heavy is not known, and moreover «كلاً» after it is accusative, and the negative does not put the accusative.
Three: that «لَمَّا» here is the one that makes the imperfect jussive, with its jussive verb omitted for understanding of the meaning. The Shaykh Abū ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥājib said in his Amālī: "This «لمَّا» is the jussive one, and its verb is omitted because it is indicated, on account of the established permissibility of omitting its verb in their saying «خَرَجْتُ ولمَّا» and «سافرتُ ولمَّا», which is common and eloquent. The meaning would be: 'and every one is not neglected or left,' because of what preceded that indicates it, namely the detailing of those gathered in His saying {فَمِنْهُمْ شَقِيٌّ وَسَعِيدٌ} [Hūd: 105], then the detailing of the wretched and the blessed and their requital, and then He explained that with His saying {لَيُوَفِّيَنَّهُمْ رَبُّكَ أَعْمَالَهُمْ}." He said: "I know of no analysis more fitting than this, even if souls find it remote because its like has not occurred in the Qur'an." He said: "But verification refuses its being found remote." I say: the grammarians stated explicitly that the jussive of «لمَّا» is regularly omitted, saying: because it is for negating «قد فَعَلَ», and the verb after it may be omitted, as in his saying:
2725 - أَفِدُ الترحل غيرَ أن رِكابَنا ... لَمَّا تَزُل برحالِنا وكأنْ قَدِ
(The departure is near, except that our mounts have not yet moved with our saddles, though it is as if they had.)
that is, "as if «قد زالت»"; so too its negated verb. Among those who stated explicitly that its jussive verb is omitted is al-Zamakhsharī; and Yaʿqūb cited on this, in his book Maʿānī al-Shiʿr, the poet's saying:
2726 - فجِئْتُ قبوَرُمْ بَدْءاً ولمَّا ... فنادَيْتُ القبورَ فلم يُجِبْنَهْ
(I came to your graves as a chief, and not yet... then I called to the graves and they did not answer me.)
He said: "His saying «بدءاً» means 'a chief,' for the badʾ of a people is their chief, and the badʾ of a slaughtered camel is the best of its portions. He said: and his saying «ولما» means 'I had not been a chief until they died, then I became chief after them,' like the saying of another:
2727 - خَلَتِ الدِّيارُ فسُدْتُ غيرَ مُسَوَّدِ ... ومن العَناءِ تَفُّردي السُّؤْدُدِ
(The abodes emptied, so I became chief, though not made a chief; and it is among hardships that I am alone in lordship.)
He said: "The parallel of stopping at «لمَّا» without its verb is stopping at «قد» without its verb in the verse of al-Nābigha: «أَفِدَ الترحُّل»: the verse."
I say: this analysis has no specificity to this reading, but applies to the reading of one who doubled «لمَّا», whether he doubled «إن» or lightened it.
As for the reading of Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī, it is very clear. It is the doubled «إنَّ» acting its action; the first lām is the lām of ibtidāʾ entering the khabar of «إنَّ», and the second is the answer of an omitted oath, that is: "and every one is of those whom, by Allah, He will pay in full." The application of «ما» to rational beings has already been established. The parallel of this verse is His saying {وَإِنَّ مِنْكُمْ لَمَن لَّيُبَطِّئَنَّ} [al-Nisāʾ: 72], except that the lām in «لمَنْ» enters the noun and in «لمَّا» it enters the khabar. Some said: this «ما» is redundant, added to separate the two lāms, the lām of emphasis and the lām of the oath. It was also said: the lām in «لَمَا» is the one preparing for the oath, like the lām in His saying {وَلَئِنْ أَشْرَكْتَ لَيَحْبَطَنَّ عَمَلُكَ} [al-Zumar: 65], and the meaning is: "all of them, by Allah, your Lord will pay them in full for their deeds, of good and evil, belief and denial."
Al-Farrāʾ said, mentioning this reading: "He made «ما» a noun for people, as is allowed in {فانكحوا مَا طَابَ لَكُمْ مِّنَ النسآء} [al-Nisāʾ: 3], then made the lām in it an answer to «إنَّ», and made the lām in «ليوفِّيَنَّهم» a lām that entered intending an oath between «ما» and its ṣila, as you say 'this is one who will surely go' and 'I have something other than it that is better than it'; and the like of it {وَإِنَّ مِنْكُمْ لَمَن لَّيُبَطِّئَنَّ} [al-Nisāʾ: 72]." Then after that he said what shows that the lām is repeated, saying: "When the Arabs hasten with the lām to the wrong place, they bring it back to its place, like «إنَّ زيداً لإِليك لمُحْسن», and the like of it:
2728 - ولو أنَّ قومي لم يكونوا أعِزَّةً ... لبَعْدُ لَقَد لاقيتُ لا بُدَّ مَصْرَعا
(Had my people not been mighty, then afterwards I would surely have met, inevitably, a place of fall.)
He said: "He put it in «بَعْد», which is not its place; and I heard Abū l-Jarrāḥ say: «إني لبحمد اللَّه لصالحٌ»."
Al-Fārisī said, justifying this reading: "Its justification is clear: he made «كلاً» accusative by «إنَّ», and entered the lām of ibtidāʾ in the khabar, and another lām entered the khabar, namely the one that receives the oath, which is specific to entering the verb; when the two lāms came together, they were separated as «إنَّ» and the lām are separated, and it entered them although it is redundant, for separation; and the like of it in speech: «إن زيداً لَمَا لينطلقَنَّ»."
This is what I have summarised of the justifications of these four readings. Some people have attacked some of them with what has no verification, and one should not pay attention to what they said. Al-Mubarrad said (and it is a boldness from him): "This is a solecism (laḥn)," meaning the doubling of «لمَّا». He said: "because the Arabs do not say «إن زيداً لَمَّا خارج»."
This is refuted. The Shaykh said: "The structure of the verse is not like the structure of the example he gave, «إنَّ زيداً لَمَّا خارج»; that example is a solecism."
I say: if he means it is not like it in structure in every respect, that is granted, but it does not help in what we are dealing with; and if he means it is not like it in the doubled «لمَّا» entering the khabar of «إنَّ», that is not so; rather it is like it in that, so granting a solecism in the mentioned example is not right, because it entails what must not be said.
Abū Jaʿfar said: "The reading with both doubled is, according to most grammarians, a solecism. It was related from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd that he said: 'This is not permitted, and one does not say «إنَّ زيداً إلا لأضربنَّه» or «لَمَّا لأضربنَّه».'" He said: "And al-Kisāʾī said: Allah the Mighty and Majestic knows best; I do not know a justification for this reading." That has already been given, and it has also been given that al-Fārisī said: "as «إنَّ زيداً إلا لمنطلق» is not good, because «إلا» is affirmation after negation, and here nothing precedes except an emphatic affirmation, so likewise «إنَّ زيداً لما منطلق» is not good, because it means the same; and «نَشَدْتُك باللَّه لمَّا فعلت» is permissible only..." to the end of what I mentioned from him. All these are views to be turned away from, because they oppose the definitively mutawātir reading.
As for the irregular readings, the first is the reading of Ubayy and those who followed him: {وَإِن كُلٌّ لَّمَّا} with «إنْ» lightened and «كل» nominative, «إنْ» being the negative and «كلٌّ» a mubtadaʾ, «لمَّا» doubled in the sense of «إلاَّ», and «لَيُوَفِّيَنَّهم» the answer of an omitted oath, that oath and its answer being the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. This is a clear, evident reading, as they all read {وَإِن كُلٌّ لَّمَّا جَمِيعٌ} [Yā Sīn: 32], and like it {وَإِن كُلُّ ذَلِكَ لَمَّا مَتَاعُ} [al-Zukhruf: 35]; and no attention is paid to the statement of one who denied that «لمَّا» is equivalent to «إلاَّ», for his arguments have been given.
As for the reading of al-Yazīdī and Ibn Arqam «لَمَّاً» with shadda and tanwīn, «لمَّاً» in it is a maṣdar from their saying «لَمَمْتُه», that is "I gathered it, a gathering," and from it the saying of the Exalted {وَتَأْكُلُونَ التراث أَكْلاً لَّمّاً} [al-Fajr: 19]. There are two analyses of it. One is what Abū l-Fatḥ said, that it is accusative by His saying «ليوفينَّهم», on the line of their saying «قياماً لأقومَنَّ، وقعوداً لأقعدَنَّ», the implied form being: "a payment that gathers their deeds, He will pay them in full"; he means that it is accusative as a maṣdar that meets its operator in meaning but not in derivation.
The second is what Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī said, that it is a description of «كل», a description by maṣdar for emphasis. On this, the muḍāf ilayhi of «كل» must be supplied as indefinite so that describing «كل» with an indefinite is sound; for were the muḍāf ilayhi supplied as definite, «كل» would become definite, and had it become definite, describing it with an indefinite would be impossible; therefore the muḍāf ilayhi was supplied as indefinite. The parallel of that is the saying of the Exalted {وَتَأْكُلُونَ التراث أَكْلاً لَّمّاً} [al-Fajr: 19], where «لمَّا» occurs as an adjective of «أكلاً», which is indefinite.
Abū ʿAlī said: "It cannot be a ḥāl, because nothing in the speech is an operator of the ḥāl."
[The apparent sense of al-Zamakhsharī's statement is that it is an emphasis following «كلاً», as «أجمعون» follows it, or that it is accusative as an adjective of «كلاً"]; for he said: {وَإِنَّ كُلاًّ لَّمَّا لَيُوَفِّيَنَّهُمْ} is like «أكلاً لمَّاً», "gathered," meaning "collected," as if it were said: "and every one, altogether," like His saying {فَسَجَدَ الملائكة كُلُّهُمْ أَجْمَعُونَ} [al-Ḥijr: 30]. End. He does not mean by that a technical emphasis; rather he explained the meaning of that, and meant that it is an adjective of «كلاً», which is why he supplied "collected." It has been given in some analyses of the doubled «لَمَّا» without tanwīn that the one with tanwīn is its origin, and that connected speech was made to take the rule of pause, and what is in that is known. The khabar of «إنْ» on this reading is the sentence of the implied oath and its answer, whether by the analysis of Abū l-Fatḥ or that of his teacher.
As for the reading of al-Aʿmash, it is very clear, and it explains the reading of al-Ḥasan given above, were it not for its departure from the orthography of the written text.
As for the reading in the codex of Ubayy as Abū Ḥātim transmitted it, «إنْ» in it is negative, «مِنْ» is redundant in the negation, «كل» is a mubtadaʾ, and «ليوفِّينَّهم» with its implied oath is its khabar; so it amounts to the reading of al-Aʿmash before it, since the implied form without «مِنْ» becomes: {وإنْ كلٌ إلا ليوفِّينَّهم}.
The tanwīn in «كلاً» is a substitute for the muḍāf ilayhi. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "He means: and all of them, and all those who differed about it." It has been given that on the reading «لَمَّاً» with tanwīn, in al-Fārisī's analysis, the muḍāf ilayhi of «كل» is supplied only as indefinite because it is described with an indefinite.
And look at what this noble verse contains of emphasis: among it, emphasis by «إنَّ», by «كل», by the lām of ibtidāʾ entering the khabar of «إنَّ», by the addition of «ما» on one view, by the implied oath, by the lām that occurs as its answer, by the nūn of emphasis, by its being doubled, and by following it with the sentence after it, His saying {إِنَّهُ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ}, which contains a severe threat for the disobedient and a good promise for the obedient.
The majority read «يعملون» with the yāʾ of the third person, following on from the disagreeing ones mentioned before. Ibn Hurmuz read «بما تعملون» in the second person, so it may be a shift (iltifāt) from third person to second, the addressed being the absent ones mentioned earlier, or a shift to address others.

In verse 2726 the printed word «قبوَرُمْ» is translated as "your graves" as the context requires.
