semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لَّيَقُولُنَّ}: This verb is declinable (muʿrab) according to the well-known view, because the nūn is separated by implication, since the origin is «ليقولونَنَّ»: the first nūn is of the nominative, and after it a doubled nūn; the succession of three similar letters was found heavy, so the nūn of the nominative was dropped, because it does not indicate in meaning what the nūn of emphasis indicates; then two sukūns met, so the wāw, which is the pronoun of the agent, was dropped because of their meeting; the verification of that has already been given.
And «ما يَحْبِسُه» is interrogative: «ما» is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and «يحبسُه» its khabar (predicate); the agent of the verb is a pronoun referring to the interrogative noun, and the accusative pronoun refers to the punishment; the meaning is: "What thing of all things holds back the punishment?"
His saying: {يَوْمَ يَأْتِيهِمْ}: It is accusative by «مصروفاً», which is the khabar of «ليس». The majority of the Basrans cited it as proof of the permissibility of putting the khabar of «ليس» before it. The aspect of that is that putting the governed word first implies putting its governor first; and «يومَ» is accusative by «مصروفاً» and has been put before «ليس», so putting the khabar first should be permissible a fortiori, because if the derivative precedes, it is more fitting that the original precede. Some have rejected this proof on two grounds. One: that an adverb is given latitude not given to other things. Second: that this rule is breached, since we have places where the governed precedes and the governor does not precede, and he adduced the like of His saying, the Exalted: {فَأَمَّا اليتيم فَلاَ تَقْهَرْ وَأَمَّا السآئل فَلاَ تَنْهَرْ} [al-Ḍuḥā: 9-10], where «اليتيمَ» is accusative by «تقهرْ» and «السائلَ» accusative by «تَنْهَرْ», and both have preceded the prohibitive «لا», while the governor, which is jussive, cannot precede «لا»; and the discussion of this question has a place more fitting for it. The Shaykh said: "I have searched through a number of the Arabs' collections of poetry and did not find the khabar of «ليس» put before it, nor its governed word, except what the apparent sense of this verse indicates and the saying of the poet:
2637 - فيأبى فما يَزْدادُ إلا لَجاجَةً ... وكنتُ أَبِيَّاً في الخَفَا لستُ أُقْدِمُ (He refuses, and increases only in obstinacy; and I was proud in secrecy, I do not advance)"
The ism of «ليس» is a pronoun referring to «العذاب», and likewise the agent of «يأتيهم»; the implied form is: "Truly, the punishment will not be turned away from them on the day when the punishment comes to them." Abū l-Baqāʾ related from some that the governor of «يومَ يأتيهم» is omitted, its implied form being: "the punishment will not be turned away from them on the day it comes to them", this omitted word being indicated by the flow of the speech.

semin-durr:10-10.t: His saying, the Exalted: {لَفَرِحٌ}: The majority read it with kasra on the rāʾ, which is the regular form of the active participle of the intransitive faʿila with kasra on the ʿayn, such as ashira, so he is ashir, and baṭira, so he is baṭir. It was also read, irregularly, «لَفَرُح» with ḍamma on the rāʾ, like yaqiẓ and yaqúẓ, and nadis and nadus.

semin-durr:11-11.t: His saying, the Exalted: {إِلاَّ الذين صَبَرُواْ}: There are three aspects. One: that it is accusative as a connected exception, since what is meant by it is the genus of mankind and not one particular individual. The second: that it is disconnected, since what is meant by "man" is a particular person; and on these two aspects it is accusative in position. The third: that it is a mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is the clause of His saying {أولئك لَهُمْ مَّغْفِرَةٌ}, and it is also disconnected. And His saying «مغفرةٌ» may be a mubtadaʾ with «لهم» its khabar, the clause being the khabar of «أولئك»; and it may be that «لهم» is the khabar of «أولئك» and «مغفرة» an agent by the sense of settledness (istiqrār).

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَلَعَلَّكَ}: The best is that it be in its usual sense of hope (tarajjī) in relation to the one addressed. It was said: it is for the interrogative, as in his saying, peace be upon him: «لعلنا أعجلناك» ("Perhaps we have hurried you").
His saying: {وَضَآئِقٌ}: a conjunction on «تارك». He turned away from «ضيّق», although it is more frequent than «ضائق». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "to show that it is a passing straitness, not a lasting one; and the like of it are sayyid and jawād, so when you want occurrence you say sāʾid and jāʾid." The Shaykh said: "This ruling is not specific to these words; rather everything built from the triliteral for permanence and settledness on a pattern other than fāʿil is returned to it when the meaning of occurrence is wanted; you say ḥāsin, thāqil and sāmin for ḥasuna, thaqula and samuna", and he cited:
2638 - بمنزلةٍ أمَا اللئيمُ فسامِنٌ ... بها وكرامُ الناسِ بادٍ شُحوبُها (In a position where the mean one grows fat in it, while the noble among people show pallor)
It was also said: he turned from «ضيِّق» to «ضائق» only to match the pattern of «تارك».
The hāʾ in «به» refers back to «بعض»; it was said: to «ما»; it was said: to the denial. And «صدرُك» is the agent of «ضائق». It is also permissible that «ضائقٌ» be a fronted khabar and «صدرك» a postponed mubtadaʾ, the clause being a khabar for the kāf in «لعلك», so that it reports with two khabars, one a single word and the other a clause conjoined to a single word, since it is in its meaning; so it is like «إنَّ زيداً قائم وأبوه منطلق», that is: "Zayd, whose father is departing, is standing".
His saying: {أَن يَقُولُواْ}: It is in the position of accusative or genitive according to the well-known disagreement about «أنْ» after the dropping of the preposition or the muḍāf, its implied form being: "out of dislike or fear that they say", or "so that they do not say", or "by their saying". Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«لأن يقولوا», that is, «لأَنْ قالوا», so it is in the sense of the past"; there is no need for this, and how can this be claimed for it when with it is that which is explicit for the future, namely the accusative-governing particle? And «لولا» is exhortative, and the exhortative clause is accusative as the object of saying.

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَمْ يَقُولُونَ}: There are two aspects regarding this «أم». One: that it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), so it is implied as «بل» with the hamza, the implied form being: "Rather, do they say: he has forged it?" The pronoun in «افتراه» refers to what is revealed. The second: that it is connected (muttaṣila), and they implied it in the sense of: "Are they content with what We have revealed to you of the Qurʾān, or do they say that it is not from Allah?"
His saying: {مِّثْلِهِ}: an adjective of «سُوَر». «مثل», although in the singular form, is used to qualify the dual, the plural and the feminine, as in His saying, the Exalted: {أَنُؤْمِنُ لِبَشَرَيْنِ مِثْلِنَا} [al-Muʾminūn: 47]; and agreement is also permissible, the Exalted said: {وَحُورٌ عِينٌ كَأَمْثَالِ} [al-Wāqiʿa: 23], and the Exalted said: {ثُمَّ لاَ يكونوا أَمْثَالَكُم} [Muḥammad: 38]. The hāʾ in «مثلِه» refers back to what is revealed also; and «مفتريات» is an adjective of «سُوَر», the plural of muftarāh, like muṣṭafayāt for muṣṭafāh, so the alif turned into a yāʾ as in the dual.

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَنَّمَآ أُنزِلِ}: «ما» may be a restrictive particle that prepares (kāffa muhayyiʾa). In «أُنْزِل» there is a pronoun referring to what is revealed to you; «بعلمٍ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is: "connected with His knowledge". It is also permissible that «ما» be a relative, either a noun or a particle, being the ism of «إنَّ», the khabar being the preposition and its noun, the implied form being: "so know that its sending down", or "that what was sent down is connected with knowledge".
Zayd b. ʿAlī read «نَزَّل» with fatḥa on the nūn and a doubled zāy, the agent of «نَزَّل» being a pronoun of Allah the Exalted; and {وَأَن لاَّ إله إِلاَّ هُوَ} is a conjunction on the preceding «أنَّ», but this one is lightened, so its ism is omitted and the negative clause is its khabar.
His saying: {نُوَفِّ}: The majority read «نُوَفِّ» with the nūn of majesty and a doubled fāʾ, from waffā yuwaffī; Ṭalḥa and Maymūn read it with the yāʾ of the third person, and Zayd b. ʿAlī likewise, except that he lightened the fāʾ, from awfā yūfī; the agent in these two readings is a pronoun of Allah the Exalted. «تُوَفَّ» was also read, with ḍamma on the tāʾ and a doubled fatḥa on the fāʾ, from wufiya yuwaffā, passive, with «أعمالُهم» nominative standing in place of the agent. «نُوَفِّ» is jussive on these readings because it is the apodosis of the condition, as in His saying, the Exalted: {مَن كَانَ يُرِيدُ حَرْثَ الآخرة نَزِدْ لَهُ [فِي حَرْثِهِ] وَمَن كَانَ يُرِيدُ حَرْثَ الدنيا نُؤْتِهِ مِنهَا} [al-Shūrā: 20].
Al-Farrāʾ claimed that «كان» is redundant, and said: "for that reason he made its apodosis jussive". Perhaps this is not sound, since if it were redundant, «يريد» would be the condition, and if it were the condition it would be jussive, and one would say «مَنْ كان يُرِدْ».
Some claimed that the verb of the condition is not put in the past with the apodosis in the imperfect except with «كان» in particular, and for this reason it has come in the Qurʾān only so. This is not correct, for it occurs with other than «كان». Zuhayr said:
2639 - ومَنْ هاب أسبابَ المنايا يَنَلْنَه ... ولو رام أسبابَ السماء بسُلَّمِ (Whoever fears the causes of death, they will reach him, even if he were to seek the causes of heaven by a ladder)
As for the Qurʾān, it came about by coincidence that it is so.
Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read «نوفِي» with a light fāʾ and the yāʾ retained, from awfā. This reading admits that the verb is jussive, its jussive being implied by the dropping of an implied vowel, as in the saying:
2640 - ألم يَأْتيك والأنباءُ تُنمي ... بما لاقَتْ لَبُونُ بني زياد (Has it not come to you — and news spreads — what the milch-camel of Banū Ziyād met with?)
considering that this can occur in ordinary speech, like {إِنَّهُ مَن يَتَّقِ} [Yūsuf: 90], which will come with full treatment in its sūra; and it admits that the verb is nominative, because the condition occurs in the past, as in the saying:
2641 - وإنْ شُلَّ رَيْعانُ الجميعِ مخافةً ... نقولُ جِهاراً ويَلْكُمْ لا تُنَفِّروا (And if the front of the whole company is scattered in fear, we say openly: Woe to you, do not cause stampede)
and as in the saying of Zuhayr:
2642 - وإنْ أتاه خليلٌ يومَ مَسْألةٍ ... يقولُ لا غائبٌ مالي ولا حَرِمُ (And if a friend comes to him on a day of asking, he says: my wealth is neither absent nor forbidden)
Is the nominative because it is on the intention of fronting, which is the view of Sībawayh, or on the intention of the fāʾ, as is the view of al-Mubarrad? A well-known disagreement.

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَحَبِطَ مَا صَنَعُواْ فِيهَا}: It is permissible that «فيها» be attached to «حَبِط», and the pronoun on this refers to the Hereafter, that is: "and the nullity of what they did became manifest in the Hereafter". It is permissible that it be attached to «صنعوا», in which case the pronoun refers to the life of this world, as it referred to it in His saying {نُوَفِّ إِلَيْهِمْ أَعْمَالَهُمْ فِيهَا}. And «ما» in «ما صنعوا» may be in the sense of «الذي» with the returning pronoun omitted, that is: "what they did"; or a maṣdar particle: "and their doing became void".
His saying: {وَبَاطِلٌ مَّا كَانُواْ}: The majority read it with «الباطل» nominative, and there are three aspects. One: that «باطل» is a fronted khabar and {مَّا كَانُواْ يَعْمَلُونَ} a postponed mubtadaʾ; and «ما» may be a maṣdar particle, that is: "and their having been doers is void", or in the sense of «الذي» with the returning pronoun omitted, that is: "what they used to do"; this on the basis that the speech is of the conjunction of clauses, this clause being conjoined to what precedes it. Second: that «باطل» is a mubtadaʾ and {مَّا كَانُواْ يَعْمَلُونَ} its khabar; so said Makkī b. Abī Ṭālib, and it is not far from a mistake, and the wonder is that he mentioned nothing else. Third: that «باطل» is conjoined to the khabars before it, that is: "those: void is what they used to do", and {مَّا كَانُواْ يَعْمَلُونَ} is the agent of «باطل»; this is supported by what Zayd b. ʿAlī read: {وَبَطَلَ مَا كَانُواْ يَعْمَلُونَ}, making it a past verb conjoined to «حَبِط».
Ubayy and Ibn Masʿūd read, Makkī said "and it is so in their codex", and al-Zamakhsharī reported it from ʿĀṣim, «وباطلاً» in the accusative, and there are three aspects. One: that it is accusative by «يعملون» with «ما» redundant; to this Makkī, Abū l-Baqāʾ and the author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» leaned; and it involves putting the governed word of the khabar of «كان» before «كان», a matter of disagreement, the correct view being that it is permissible, as in His saying, the Exalted: {أهؤلاء إِيَّاكُمْ كَانُواْ يَعْبُدُونَ} [Sabaʾ: 40], where the apparent sense is that «إياكم» is accusative by «يعبدون». The second: that «ما» is indefinite-intensifying (mubhama) and is accusative by «يعملون», its meaning being: "a falsehood, what a falsehood they used to do". The third: that «باطلاً» is in the sense of a maṣdar, "what they used to do became void, a voiding". Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned these two aspects. The meaning of his saying that «ما» is mubhama is that here it is an adjective of the indefinite noun before it, and for that reason he implied it as «باطلاً أيَّ باطل»; it is therefore like the saying:
2643 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وحديثٌ ما على قِصَرِهْ (… and a tale, such a tale, for all its brevity)
and «لأمرٍ ما جَدَعَ قصيرٌ أَنْفَه» ("It was for some matter that Qaṣīr cut off his nose"), and he has already given that in His saying, the Exalted: {مَثَلاً مَّا بَعُوضَةً} [al-Zumar: 9].

[Translator's note: the source cites {مَثَلاً مَّا بَعُوضَةً} as al-Zumar: 9, which is probably an error for al-Baqara: 26; translated as written.]

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَفَمَن كَانَ}: There are two aspects. One: that it is a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is omitted, its implied form being: "Is the one who is on these things like another?" So Abū l-Baqāʾ implied it; better than it is: "Is the one who is such-and-such like the one who wants the life of this world and its adornment?" The omission of the counterpart that the hamza was attached to is frequent, as in {أَفَمَن زُيِّنَ لَهُ سواء عَمَلِهِ} [Fāṭir: 8], {أَمَّنْ هُوَ قَانِتٌ} [al-Zumar: 9], and the like. This question is in the sense of affirmation (taqrīr). The second, to which al-Zamakhsharī leaned: that this is conjoined to something omitted before it, its implied form being: "Is the one who wants the life of this world and its adornment like the one who is on clear proof?", that is: they do not follow them in rank and do not approach them; he means that between the two groups there is a gulf; and the one meant is whoever of the Jews believed, such as ʿAbd Allāh b. Salām. This is according to his principle of implying a conjoined word between the interrogative hamza and the conjunction; and it is also a mubtadaʾ, with the khabar omitted as already presented.
His saying: {وَيَتْلُوهُ}: They differed over these pronouns, I mean in «يتلوه», in «منه» and in «قبله». It was said: the hāʾ in «يتلوه» refers back to «مَنْ», and the Prophet ﷺ is meant, and likewise the two pronouns in «منه» and «قبله»; by the witness (shāhid) his tongue, peace be upon him, is meant; the implied form is: "and his tongue follows that one who is on clear proof", that is: "follows Muḥammad", that is, attests to Muḥammad's truthfulness, "and before him", that is, before Muḥammad. It was said: the witness is Jibrīl, the pronoun in «منه» being for Allah the Exalted and «من قبله» for the Prophet. It was said: the witness is the Injīl, and «كتاب موسى» is conjoined to «شاهد»; the meaning is that the Torah and the Gospel follow Muḥammad in confirmation, and he has separated between the conjunction particle and the conjoined by his saying «من قبله»; the implied form is: "a witness from Him, and the book of Mūsā before it"; the discussion of separating the conjunction from the conjoined has already been given at length in al-Nisāʾ.
It was said: the pronoun in «يتلوه» is for the Qurʾān and in «منه» for Muḥammad, peace be upon him. It was said: for Jibrīl, the implied form being: "and a witness from Muḥammad, which is his tongue, or from Jibrīl, follows the Qurʾān". The hāʾ in «من قبلِه» is also for the Qurʾān. It was said: the hāʾ in «يَتْلوه» refers back to the explanation (bayān) indicated by the clear proof (bayyina). It was said: by the witness the inimitability of the Qurʾān is meant, so the three pronouns are for the Qurʾān. This is enough, and beyond it are confused opinions, most of which return to what I have mentioned.
Muḥammad b. al-Sāʾib al-Kalbī read «كتابَ موسى» in the accusative, and there are two aspects. One, which is the apparent: that it is conjoined to the hāʾ in «يتلوه», that is: "it follows him and follows the book of Mūsā", with a preposition and its noun separating the conjunction from the conjoined. The second: that it is accusative by an implied verb. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It was said: the speech was completed at His saying «منه», and «كتابَ موسى», that is: «ويتلو كتابَ موسى»", so he implied a verb like the one uttered, as if he did not see separation between the conjunction and the conjoined, and for that reason implied a verb.
And «إماماً ورحمةً» are accusative as ḥāl from «كتاب موسى», whether it is read nominative or accusative.
The hāʾ in «به» may refer back to «كتاب موسى», which is the nearest mentioned; it was said: to the Qurʾān; it was said: to Muḥammad; and likewise the hāʾ in «به».
Al-aḥzāb: the group in which there is coarseness, as if because of their numbers they were described thus; from it comes the description of the wild ass as «حَزَابِيَة» for its coarseness. Al-aḥzāb is the plural of ḥizb, which is a group of people.
«المِرْية», with kasra on the mīm and with ḍamma, is doubt; two dialects, the more famous being kasra, which is the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz, and which the great majority of people read; the ḍamma is the dialect of Asad and Tamīm, and al-Sulamī, Abū Rajāʾ and Abū l-Khaṭṭāb al-Sadūsī read it. And «أولئك» points to the one who was on clear proof, being pluralised in accordance with its meaning; this if by «مَنْ كان» the Prophet and his Companions are meant; and if he alone is meant, it is permissible that he be honoured with the plural pointing, as in the saying:
2644 - فإن شِئْتِ حَرَمْتُ النساءَ سواكمُ ... وإن شِئْتِ لم أَطْعَمْ نُقاخاً ولا بَرْدا (If you wish, I will forbid myself women other than you; and if you wish, I will not taste cold sweet water nor sleep)
And «موعده» is a noun of place of its promise. Ḥassān, may Allah be pleased with him, said:
2645 - أورَدْتُموها حِياضَ الموتِ ضاحيةً ... فالنارُ موعدُها والموتُ ساقيها (You led them openly to the pools of death; so the Fire is their appointed place, and death their cupbearer)

semin-durr:18-18.t: Al-ashhād is the plural of shāhid, like ṣāḥib and aṣḥāb; or the plural of shahīd, like sharīf and ashrāf.

semin-durr:19-19.t: And His saying, the Exalted: {وَهُمْ بالآخرة هُمْ}: The second «هم» is emphasis (tawkīd) of the first, a verbal emphasis.

semin-durr:20-20.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَا كَانُواْ يَسْتَطِيعُونَ}: Three aspects are permissible for this «ما». One: that it be negative, He having negated that of them since they did not benefit from it, even though they were possessors of hearing and sight; or the object of hearing and sight is something specific. The second: that it be a maṣdar particle, and there are then two interpretations of it. One: that it stands in the place of an adverb, that is: "for the duration of their ability"; and «ما» is accusative by «يُضاعف», that is: "the punishment is doubled for them for the duration of their ability to hear and see". The second interpretation: that it is accusative in position by dropping the preposition, as it is dropped before «أنْ» and «أنَّ», its two sisters; to this al-Farrāʾ leaned, and that preposition is also attached to «يُضاعَف», that is: "it is doubled for them because they used to hear and see and not benefit". Third: that «ما» is in the sense of «الذي», and also on the dropping of the preposition, that is: "for what they used to"; and there is remoteness in it because dropping the preposition is not regular.
The clause of His saying «يُضاعف» is resumptive. It was said: the pronoun in His saying «ما كانوا» refers back to «أولياء», who are their gods, that is: "they in reality had no protectors, even though they believed them to be protectors"; on this {يُضَاعَفُ لَهُمُ العذاب} is parenthetical.

semin-durr:112-112.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {كَمَآ أُمِرْتَ}: The kāf is in the position of accusative, either as an adjective (naʿt) of an omitted maṣdar, which is the well-known view of the parsers. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "that is, 'be upright with an uprightness like the uprightness you were commanded, on the highway of the truth, not deviating from it'"; or as a ḥāl from the pronoun of that maṣdar. «استفعل» here is for seeking, as if it were said: "seek to be firm in the religion," as he said: "as you say «استغفر», that is, 'seek forgiveness'."
His saying: {وَمَن تَابَ مَعَكَ}: «مَنْ» has two analyses. One: it is accusative as mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment); so Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned it, and the meaning becomes "be upright, accompanied by those who repented accompanying you," and in this meaning there is a departure from the apparent wording. Two: it is nominative, being conjoined to the latent pronoun in «استقم», and the separation by the preposition and its genitive noun suffices in place of emphasising it with a detached pronoun for the soundness of the conjunction. This discussion has already been given for you in His saying {اسكن أَنْتَ وَزَوْجُكَ} [al-Baqara: 35], and that the sound view is that it is a conjunction of sentences, not of single words; that is why al-Zamakhsharī supplied: «فاستقم أنت وليستقم مَنْ تاب», supplying a verb suitable for governing it overtly in the nominative.
The majority read {بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ} with tāʾ, following the address before it. Al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿmash and ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī read it with yāʾ of the third person, which is a shift (iltifāt) from address to the third person, the reverse of what preceded in {بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ} [Hūd: 111].

semin-durr:113-113.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَلاَ تركنوا}: The majority read it with fatḥa on the tāʾ and the kāf; the past of this is rakina with kasra on the ʿayn, like ʿalima, and this is the most eloquent form; so said al-Azharī. Others said: "It is the dialect of Quraysh." Abū ʿAmr in one transmission read «تِرْكَنوا», and the precise treatment of that was given at the start of this topic.
Qatāda, Ṭalḥa and al-Ashhab ibn Rumayla read, and it was also transmitted from Abū ʿAmr, «تَرْكُنوا» with ḍamma on the ʿayn, which is the imperfect of rakana with fatḥa, like qatala yaqtulu. Some said: "It is from tadākhul (mixing of dialects)," meaning that one who pronounced «رَكِنَ» with kasra on the ʿayn says «يَرْكُن» with ḍamma, though its right was to have fatḥa; so when they put ḍamma, we knew he had dispensed with his own dialect in the imperfect in favour of another's. As for this reading, we have no need to claim mixing; rather we claim that one who put fatḥa on the kāf took it from rakina with kasra, and one who put ḍamma took it from rakana with fatḥa. That is why al-Rāghib said: "The correct thing is to say rakina yarkanu, and rakana yarkunu: kasra in the past with fatḥa in the imperfect, and fatḥa in the past with ḍamma in the imperfect." The saying rakana yarkanu with fatḥa in both is anomalous, and is from mixing. The upshot is that one says rakina with kasra on the ʿayn, which is the highest dialect as already given, and rakana with fatḥa, which is the dialect of Qays and Tamīm; al-Kisāʾī added "and Najd"; and in the imperfect there are three: fatḥa, kasra and ḍamma.
Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «تُرْكَنوا», passive, from arkanahu when he inclined him, so it is of the chapter of «لا أُرَيَنَّك ههنا» and {فَلاَ يَكُنْ فِي صَدْرِكَ حَرَجٌ مِّنْهُ} [al-Aʿrāf: 2], which has been given.
Al-rukūn is inclining, and from it al-rukn (the pillar), to be leaned on.
His saying: {فَتَمَسَّكُمُ}: it is accusative by an implied «أنْ» in the answer to a prohibition. Ibn Waththāb, ʿAlqama and al-Aʿmash, with others, read «فتِمَسَّكم» with kasra on the tāʾ, and that has been given.
His saying: {وَمَا لَكُمْ}: this sentence may be circumstantial (ḥāliyya), that is, "it touches you while there is no helper for you"; and it may be resumptive. In «مِنْ أولياء», «مِنْ» is redundant, either in the agent or in the mubtadaʾ, because a preposition and its genitive noun, when it relies on something one of which is negation, raises the agent.
His saying: {ثُمَّ لاَ تُنصَرُونَ}: the majority have the nūn of the nominative retained, because it is a nominative verb, since it is of the chapter of conjunction of sentences, a verbal sentence being conjoined to a nominal sentence. Zayd ibn ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with the two of them, read it with the nūn of the nominative dropped, conjoining it to «تمسَّكم»; and the sentence, by what was given above, is circumstantial or resumptive, in which case it is parenthetical. «ثمَّ» is brought as a warning of the distance in rank.

semin-durr:114-114.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {طَرَفَيِ النهار}: an adverbial (ẓarf) of «أَقِمْ». It is weak to take it as an adverbial of the prayer, as if it were said: "establish the prayer that falls in these two times." Al-ṭaraf, though not an adverbial, took the case of the adverbial when it was annexed to the adverbial, like your saying «أتيته أولَ النهار وآخرَه ونصفَ الليل», with all of these in the accusative as adverbials when they are annexed to it, although they were not set down to be adverbials.
The majority read «زُلَفاً» with ḍamma on the zāy and fatḥa on the lām; it is the plural of «زُلْفة» with sukūn on the lām, like ghuraf as plural of ghurfa and zulam as plural of zulma. Abū Jaʿfar and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read it with ḍamma on the lām as well, and in this reading there are three analyses. One: it is also the plural of zulfa, and the ḍamma is for harmony (ittibāʿ), as they said busra and busur with ḍamma on the sīn, in harmony with the ḍamma of the bāʾ. Two: it is a singular noun on this pattern, like ʿunuq and the like. Three: it is the plural of zalīf; Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It has been pronounced," meaning that they said zalīf, and faʿīl is pluralised on fuʿul, like raghīf, rughuf and qaḍīb, quḍub.
Mujāhid and Ibn Muḥaysin read it with sukūn on the lām. It has two analyses. One: this reading may be a lightening of the ḍamma on the ʿayn, so what has been given applies to it. Two: it is an original sukūn, of the chapter of the generic noun, like busra and busr, without harmony.
Mujāhid and Ibn Muḥaysin also read, in one transmission, «وزُلْفَى» on the pattern of «حُبْلَى», making it the description of the feminine singular, considering the meaning, because the meaning is "the nearer station" or "the nearer hour," that is, the close one. It was also said that the two might have changed the tanwīn into an alif and then made connected speech take the rule of pause, since they read it with sukūn on the lām, and that is possible. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Al-zulfā has the sense of al-zulfa, as al-qurbā has the sense of al-qurba," meaning that it is among the words in which the tāʾ of the feminine and its alif alternate.
In the accusative of «زُلَفاً» there are two analyses; the more apparent: it is conjoined to «طرفي», so it is put in the accusative as an adverbial, since what is meant by it is the nearby hours of the night. Two: it is accusative as a direct object, conjoined to «الصلاة». Al-Zamakhsharī said, after mentioning the readings above: "It is what is near the end of the day and of the night. It was also said: zulafan from the night, meaning nearness from the night; and its due on this interpretation is that it be conjoined to «الصلاة», that is: 'establish the prayer at the two ends of the day, and establish zulafan from the night,' in the sense of prayers by which you draw near to Allah the Mighty and Majestic in part of the night."
Al-zulfa is the first hours of the night; so said Thaʿlab. Al-Akhfash and Ibn Qutayba said: "Al-zulaf are the hours of the night and its periods, and every hour of it is a zulfa"; so they did not restrict it to the beginning of the night. Al-ʿAjjāj said:
2729 - ناجٍ طواه الأَْيْنُ مِمَّا وَجَفا ... طَيَّ الليالي زُلَفاً فَزُلَفا
سَماوَةَ الهلالِ حتى احْقَوْقَفا
(A swift one whom weariness folded from his running, as the nights fold, hour upon hour, the crescent's contour, until he became bent like a bow.)
The origin of the word is from al-zulfā, which is nearness. One says azlafahu fa-izdalafa, that is, "he brought him near, so he drew near." The Exalted said: {وَأَزْلَفْنَا ثَمَّ الآخرين} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 64]. In the ḥadīth: "Draw near (izdalifū) to Allah with two rakʿas." Al-Rāghib said: "Al-zulfa is the station and favour; and al-zulfa has been used in the sense of punishment, as 'good tidings' and the like are used; and al-mazālif are the steps; and the night of al-Muzdalifa was so named for their nearness to Minā after the pouring forth."
His saying: {مِّنَ الليل} is an adjective of «زُلَفاً».
[Translator's note: the source has a stray slash in "أتيته/ أولَ النهار", a page-break mark, not translated.]

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لاَ جَرَمَ}: There is a disagreement among the grammarians about this expression, which can be summarised in five aspects. One, which is the view of al-Khalīl, Sībawayh and the great majority of people: that the two were compounded from the negative «لا» and «جَرَم», and were built on their compounding like khamsata ʿashara (fifteen), and their meaning became the meaning of a verb, which is «حقَّ» (it is true / it is due). On this, what follows them is nominative as agent; so His saying, the Exalted: {لاَ جَرَمَ أَنَّ لَهُمُ النار} [al-Naḥl: 62] means: "it is due and established that the Fire is theirs", or "that it is settled for them". The second aspect: that «لا جَرَمَ» is like «لا رجل» in that «لا» is the lā of generic negation and «جَرَم» is its ism, built with it on fatḥa, the two together being in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, and what follows them being the khabar of the negative «لا»; and its meaning became: "no escape, and it must be".
The third: like the one before it, except that «أنَّ» and what follows it are in the position of accusative or genitive after the dropping of the preposition, the implied form being: "There is no escape from their being in the Hereafter", that is, in their loss. The fourth: that «لا» is a negation of earlier speech spoken by the unbelievers, which Allah refuted by His saying «لا», as this «لا» refutes before the oath in His saying: {لاَ أُقْسِمُ} [al-Qiyāma: 1], and His saying, the Exalted: {فَلاَ وَرَبِّكَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ} [al-Nisāʾ: 65], whose verification has already been given; then after it He brought a verbal clause, namely «جرم أنَّ لهم كذا». And «جَرَمَ» is a past verb meaning "earned", its agent latent, referring to their deed, which the flow of the speech indicates; and «أنَّ» with what is in its scope is in the position of direct object, because «جَرَم» is transitive, being in the sense of "earned". The poet said:
2646 - نَصَبْنا رأسَه في جِذْعِ نَخْلٍ ... بما جَرَمَتْ يداه وما اعتدَيْنا (We set up his head on the trunk of a palm tree for what his hands earned, and we did not transgress)
that is: for what they earned; the verification of that has already been given in al-Māʾida. And jarīmat al-qawm is "their earner". He said:
2647 - جريمةُ ناهِضٍ في رأسِ نِيْقٍ ... ترى لعظامِ ما جَمَعَتْ صَليبا (The earner of a fledgling on a mountain peak; you see a hard marrow-grease for the bones of what she has gathered)
So the implied form of the verse is: "their deed, or their saying, earned them their loss". This is the view of Abū Isḥāq al-Zajjāj, and on this the pause is at His saying «لا», and then one begins with «جَرَمَ», in contrast to what preceded.
The fifth aspect: that its meaning is "no repelling and no prevention", «جَرَمَ» being in the sense of cutting; you say jaramtu, that is, "I cut"; so «جرم» is the ism of «لا», built with it on fatḥa as already mentioned, and its khabar is «أنَّ» and what is in its scope, or on the dropping of the preposition, that is: "no prevention from their loss", whereupon the well-known disagreement returns.
There are dialects of this expression: one says «لا جِرَمَ» with kasra on the jīm, «لا جُرَم» with ḍamma, «لا جَرَ» with the mīm dropped, «لا ذا جَرَم», «لا إنَّ ذا جَرَم», «لا ذو جَرَم», «لا عن ذا جَرَم», «لا إنْ جَرَم», «لا عن جَرَم», and «لا ذا جَرَ واللَّهِ لا أفعل ذلك».
From Abū ʿAmr: «لا جَرُم أنَّ لهم النار» on the pattern of «لا كَرُم», meaning with ḍamma on the rāʾ, and «لا جَر». He said: "They dropped it because of frequent use, as they said «سَوْ ترى» meaning «سوف»."
And His saying {هُمُ الأخسرون}: «هم» may be a separator (faṣl), may be emphasis, and may be a mubtadaʾ with what follows as its khabar, the clause being the khabar of «أنَّ».

semin-durr:23-23.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِنَّ الذين آمَنُواْ}: The relative noun is the ism of «إنَّ», and the clause of His saying {أولئك أَصْحَابُ الجنة} is its khabar.
Al-ikhbāt: calm, humility and lowliness; its origin is from al-khabt, which is the calm place, that is, the low-lying part of the land. Akhbata al-rajulu: the man entered a khabt place, like anjada and atham when he enters one of those two places; then latitude was given to it, so it was said khabata dhikruhu, that is, "his mention died down"; and a base thing is called al-khabīt. The poet said:
2648 - ينفع الطيِّبُ القليلُ من الرِّزْ ... قِ ولا يَنْفَعُ الكثير الخبيتُ (A little of the good provision benefits, and a great deal of the base does not benefit)
Thus they recite this verse in this root, al-Zamakhsharī and others; and the apparent sense is that it is with the thāʾ (mathalatha), especially because it is set against al-ṭayyib; but the apparent sense of their wording is that it is with the tāʾ (mathnāt), since they bring it in this root. What shows that the meaning of the verse is on the thāʾ is al-Zamakhsharī's saying: "It was said: the tāʾ in it is a substitute for the thāʾ." Of khabt occurring in the sense of a calm place is the saying:
2649 - أفاطمُ لو شَهِدْتِ ببطنِ خَبْتٍ ... وقد قتل الهزبرَ أخاك بشرا (O Fāṭima, if only you had witnessed in the hollow of Khabt, when your brother Bishr killed the lion)
There is awkwardness in the construction of the verse, and its resolution is: "if only you had seen your brother Bishr when he killed the lion", so the agent of «قتل» is a pronoun referring to «أخاك». Akhbata is made transitive with «إلى», as in this verse, and with the lām, as in His saying, the Exalted: {فَتُخْبِتَ لَهُ قُلُوبُهُمْ} [al-Ḥajj: 54].

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَثَلُ الفريقين}: a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «كالأعمى» its khabar (predicate). Then this kāf may be itself the khabar, so it is implied as «مثل», its implied form being: "the likeness of the two groups is the likeness of the blind man". It is also permissible that «مثل» be in the sense of "description", and the meaning of the kāf be the meaning of "like", so an omitted muḍāf is implied, that is: "like the likeness of the blind". And His saying {مَثَلُ الفريقين كالأعمى} may be of the chapter of likening two things to two things, setting blindness against sight and deafness against hearing, which is of ṭibāq (antithesis); and may be of likening one thing with its two attributes to one thing with its two attributes, in which case His saying «كالأعمى والأصمِّ» and His saying «والبصير والسميع» are of the chapter of conjoining attributes, like the saying:
2650 - إلى المَلِكِ القَرْمِ وابنِ الهُمامِ ... ولَيْثِ الكتيبةِ في المُزْدَحَمْ (To the noble king, son of the chief, and lion of the squadron in the throng)
Al-Zamakhsharī did well to express this, saying: "He likened the group of unbelievers to the blind and deaf, and the group of believers to the seeing and hearing; this is of laff and ṭibāq, and there are two meanings in it: that he likens the two groups with two likenesses, as Imruʾ al-Qays likened the hearts of birds to the dried date and the jujube; and that he likens (them) to the one who combines blindness and deafness, and the one who combines sight and hearing, so that the wāw in «والأصمِّ» and in «والسميع» is for conjoining an attribute to an attribute, as in the saying:
2651 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ال ... صَابحِ فالغانِمِ فالآئِبِ (… the one who attacks at dawn, then plunders, then returns)"
I say: by his saying "laff" he means that he enfolded (laffa) the believers and the unbelievers, who are the two likened ones, in his saying «الفريقين»; and had he explained them, he would have said: the likeness of the believing group is like the seeing and hearing, and the likeness of the unbelieving is like the blind and deaf; and it is a famous expression in the science of bayān: two corresponding expressions: laff and nashr (enfolding and unfolding). He alluded to the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays, which is:
2652 - كأنَّ قلوبَ الطيرِ رَطْباً ويابِساً ... لدى وكرِها العُنَّابُ والحَشَفُ البالي (As if the hearts of birds, fresh and dry, at their nest, were the jujube and the worn-out dried date)
The original speech is: as if the fresh of the hearts of birds were the jujube, and the dry of them the dried date; so he enfolded and unfolded; and laff and nashr in the science of bayān is a large division, this not being the place for it.
By his saying «الصابح فالغانم» he alluded to the saying:
2653 - يا ويحَ زَيَّابَةَ للحارثِ ال ... صابحِ فالغانم فالآئِبِ (Alas for Zayyāba, because of al-Ḥārith, who attacks at dawn, then plunders, then returns)
This has already been given at the beginning of al-Baqara with its verification.
If you say: why did he put the likening of the unbeliever before that of the believer? The answer is that the preceding mention was of the unbelievers, so he put their likening first. If it is said: what is the wisdom in turning away from this construction, had it been said «كالأعمى والبصير والأصم والسميع» so that every expression matches its opposite and the opposition appears by that? The answer: that when the Exalted mentioned the closing of the eye He followed it with the closing of the ear, and when He mentioned the opening of the eye He followed it with the opening of the ear; and this likening is one of the divisions, namely the likening of an intelligible matter to a perceptible matter: He likened the blindness of insight and its deafness to the blindness of sight and the deafness of hearing, the former wandering in the darknesses of misguidance, just as the latter is bewildered in the roads. These are the benefits of the science of bayān.
His saying: {مَثَلاً}: a tamyīz (specification), transferred from the agent function; the origin is: "Are their likenesses equal?" (هل يَسْتوي مَثَلُهما), like His saying, the Exalted: {واشتعل الرأس شَيْباً} [Maryam: 4]. Ibn ʿAṭiyya, may Allah have mercy on him, allowed that it be a ḥāl, and there is remoteness in it in craft and meaning, because it is on the meaning of "min" and not on the meaning of "fī".

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِنَّي لَكُمْ}: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read «أني» with fatḥa on the hamza, and the rest with kasra. As for the fatḥa, it is on the implication of a preposition, that is: «بأني لكم». Al-Fārisī said: "In the reading with fatḥa there is a shift from the third person to the second." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: There is something to consider in this; it is only a quotation of his address to his people, and this is not really a shift from the third person to address; had the speech been «أن أَنْذِرْهم» or the like, that would be sound. Makkī also said this, I mean iltifāt (shift), for he said: "The origin is «بأني», the preposition and its noun being in the position of the second object, and the origin was «أنه», but it came in the manner of iltifāt." End. But this iltifāt is not the one mentioned by Abū ʿAlī, for that was from third person to second person and this is from third person to first person; and neither is needed, though Makkī's statement is nearer.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The preposition and its noun is attached to an omitted ḥāl, the meaning being: 'We sent him connected with this speech', which is His saying {إِنَّي لَكُمْ نَذِيرٌ مُّبِينٌ} with kasra; when the preposition was joined to it, it was given fatḥa, as it is given fatḥa in «كأنَّ», while the meaning is that of kasra in your saying «إن زيداً كالأسد»." As for the kasra, it is on the implication of saying, which is often implied and needs no evidence.

semin-durr:26-26.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: {أَن لاَّ تعبدوا}: like His saying {أَن لاَّ تعبدوا} at the beginning of the sūra; and we add here something else, namely that on the reading of those who put fatḥa on «أني» it admits of two aspects. One: that it be a badal (substitute) for His saying «أني لكم», that is: "We sent him with 'that you not worship'". The second: that it be explicative, the thing explained by it being either «أرسلنا» or «نذير». As for the reading of those who put kasra, it may be the maṣdar particle, governed by «أرسلنا», and it may be the explicative in its two states.
His saying: {أَلِيمٍ}: Ascribing pain to the day is figurative, because it occurs in it and not by it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "When the punishment is described by it, I say: it is a similar figure, because the one who is in pain, in reality, is the one punished; so its like is your saying «نهارك صائم» ('your day is fasting')." The Shaykh said: "This is on the basis that «أليم» is an adjective of intensity, meaning one whose pain is great; if «أليم» is in the sense of «مُؤْلم» (painful), then ascribing it to the day is figurative and to the punishment is literal."

semin-durr:116-116.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَلَوْلاَ كَانَ}: «لولا» is hortative (taḥḍīḍiyya), into which the sense of lamentation over them has entered, which is close to the figurative sense of the saying of the Exalted {ياحسرة عَلَى العباد} [Yā Sīn: 30]. What is related from al-Khalīl, that he said: "Every «لولا» in the Qur'an has the meaning of «هَلاَّ» except the one in al-Ṣāffāt: {فَلَوْلاَ أَنَّهُ [كَانَ مِنَ المسبحين]} [verse 143]," is not sound from him, because it occurs likewise outside al-Ṣāffāt: {لَّوْلاَ أَن تَدَارَكَهُ} [al-Qalam: 49], {وَلَوْلاَ أَن ثَبَّتْنَاكَ} [al-Fatḥ: 25], {وَلَوْلاَ رِجَالٌ} [al-Isrāʾ: 74].
«مِن القُرون»: it may be attached to «كان», because it is complete (tāmma) here, since the meaning is "why was there not found among the generations," or "there did not occur," and the like. It may also be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «أُولو بَقِيَّة», because had it come after it, it could have been an adjective of it. «مِنْ قبلكم» is a ḥāl from «القرون»; «يَنْهَوْن» is a ḥāl from «أولو بقية» because of its being specified by annexation, and it may be an adjective of «أُولوا بقية», which is better.
It is weak to take this «كان» as incomplete (nāqiṣa), for the meaning is remote from that; and on that supposition, «من القرون» must be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl, because the incomplete «كان» does not act according to most grammarians, and «يَنْهَوْن» would be in the position of accusative as the khabar of «كان».
The majority read «بَقِيَّة» with fatḥa on the bāʾ and shadda on the yāʾ, and it has two analyses. One: it is an adjective on the pattern faʿīla for intensiveness with the sense of the active participle, which is why the tāʾ entered it; what is meant by it then is the army of a thing and its choicest. It is called "baqiyya" for its army and choicest in their saying "so-and-so is the baqiyya of the people, the baqiyya of the noble," because a man keeps back the best and most excellent of what he brings out; and on this basis the verse of al-Ḥamāsa is taken:
2730 - إنْ تُذْنِبُوا ثم تَأْتِيني بقيَّتُكم ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(If you sin, then your remnant comes to me...)
And in the proverb: "In corners are hidden things, and among men are remnants."
Two: it is a maṣdar with the sense of al-baqwā. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It may be that al-baqiyya has the sense of al-baqwā, as al-taqiyya has the sense of al-taqwā, that is: 'why were there not among them people of sparing care for themselves and guarding them from the wrath and punishment of Allah?'"
A group read «بَقِيَة» with the yāʾ lightened, and it is an active participle from baqiya, like shajiya from shajiya, the implied form being: "possessors of a remaining group," that is, a surviving one. Abū Jaʿfar and Shayba read «بُقْية» with ḍamma on the first letter and sukūn on the ʿayn. «بَقْيَة» was also read, denoting a single occurrence of the maṣdar. «في الأرض» is attached to al-fasād, and a maṣdar with the article acts on explicit objects, so how much more on adverbials? It may be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «الفساد».
His saying: {إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً}: two analyses. One: it is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), which arises when the exhortation is taken in its true sense; when it is taken so, the exception must be disconnected lest the meaning be spoiled.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its meaning: 'but a few of those We saved from the generations were forbidden from corruption, and the rest were abandoners of forbidding.'" Then he said: "If you ask: is there a justification for this exception being connected, on which it can be taken? I say: if you make it connected, as the apparent speech has it, the meaning is spoiled, because it would be an exhortation to those of remaining virtue to forbid corruption, except for the few of those saved among them, as you say 'why did your people not read the Qur'an, except the righteous among them,' intending to except the righteous from those exhorted to read the Qur'an." I say: because the speech would end up with the saved not being exhorted to forbid corruption, which is a spoiled meaning.
Two: it is connected, in that the exhortation is interpreted as negation, so that is sound, except that it leads to the accusative in a non-affirmative context, although other than the accusative is preferable. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: in exhorting them to forbid corruption there is the sense of negating it from them, as if it were said 'there were not among the generations people of remaining virtue except a few,' it would be a connected exception with a sound meaning, and its accusative would be on the basic rule of exception, although the most eloquent is to put it in the nominative as a badal." I say: what supports the exhortation here having the sense of negation is the reading of Zayd ibn ʿAlī «إلا قليلٌ» in the nominative, observing the sense of negation and so using badal, the most eloquent, like His saying {مَّا فَعَلُوهُ إِلاَّ قَلِيلٌ مِّنْهُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 66]. Al-Farrāʾ said: "The meaning: 'so there was not,' because in the interrogative there is a kind of denial"; he called the exhortation an interrogative. It is reported from al-Akhfash that he held the connected exception to be necessary, as if he observed the negation.
«مِن» in «مِمَّنْ أَنْجَيْنا» is partitive (tabʿīḍ). Al-Zamakhsharī refused that it be partitive; rather it is explicative (bayān), saying: "Its due is to be explicative, not partitive, because salvation belonged only to those who forbade, by the proof of His saying, the Mighty and Majestic {أَنجَيْنَا الذين يَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ السواء وَأَخَذْنَا الذين ظَلَمُواْ بِعَذَابٍ بَئِيسٍ} [al-Aʿrāf: 165]." I say: on the first view it is attached to an omitted element as an adjective of «قليلاً»; on the second it is attached to an omitted element by way of explanation, that is, "I mean."
His saying: {واتبع}: the majority read «أتَّبع» with hamzat al-waṣl, a doubled tāʾ and a bāʾ, both with fatḥa, an active past verb, and it has two analyses. One: it is conjoined to an implied element. Two: the wāw is circumstantial, not conjunctive. This becomes clear by al-Zamakhsharī's statement: "If you ask: to what is His saying {واتبع الذين ظَلَمُواْ} conjoined? I say: if its meaning is 'and they followed the desires,' it is conjoined to an implied element, because the meaning is: 'except a few of those We saved from among them, who were forbidden corruption, and those who did wrong followed their desires'; so it is a conjunction on «نُهوا». If its meaning is 'and they followed the requital of the luxury,' the wāw is circumstantial, as if it were said: 'We saved the few, while those who did wrong had followed their requital.'"
I say: so he allowed two analyses for «ما أُتْرفوا». One: it is an object without omission of a muḍāf, «ما» applying to the desires and to the blessings on account of which they became insolent. Two: it is with an omitted muḍāf, that is, "the requital of what they were given luxury in"; and he built on these two analyses the statement about «واتَّبع», as you know.
Al-itrāf is ifʿāl from al-taraf, which is comfort; one says "a mutraf boy," that is, one soft of body, and «أُتْرفوا» means they were given comfort. It was also said: al-turfa is expansion in comfort.
Abū ʿAmr, in the transmission of al-Juʿfī, and Jaʿfar read «وأُتبع» with ḍamma on the hamzat al-qaṭʿ, sukūn on the tāʾ and kasra on the bāʾ, passive; an omitted muḍāf is then necessary, that is, "they were made to follow the requital of what they were given luxury in." «ما» may mean "that which," which is apparent because the pronoun in «فيه» returns to it, and it may be a maṣdar particle, that is, "the requital of their luxury."
His saying: {وَكَانُواْ مُجْرِمِينَ}: three analyses. One: it is conjoined to «أُتْرِفُوا» if we make «ما» a maṣdar particle, that is, "they followed their luxury and their being criminals." Two: it is conjoined to «اتَّبع», that is, "they followed their desires and were criminals by that," because a follower of desires is submerged in sins. Three: it is parenthetical, a judgment upon them that they are a criminal people; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned that. The Shaykh said: "This is not called parenthetical in the technical usage of grammar, because it is the end of a verse, so it is not between two things of which one needs the other."
[Translator's note: the source has stray slashes ("وقرأ فرقةٌ/" and "لأنَّ/ تابع") that are page-break marks; they are not translated. The source spells al-Zamakhsharī's name once as «الزمشخري».]

semin-durr:117-117.t: His saying, the Exalted: {لِيُهْلِكَ}: here are the two well-known analyses: the redundancy of the lām in the khabar of «كان» as an indication of emphasis, which is the view of the Kufans, or its being attached to the omitted khabar of «كان», which is the doctrine of the Basrans. «بظلمٍ» is attached to «يُهْلك», the bāʾ being causal. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed that it be a ḥāl from the agent of «ليُهْلِكَ». His saying «وأهلُها مُصْلحون» is a circumstantial sentence.

semin-durr:119-119.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِلاَّ مَن رَّحِمَ}: Its apparent sense is that it is connected, an exception from the agent of «يَزالون» or from the pronoun in «مختلفين». Al-Ḥūfī allowed it to be a disconnected exception, that is, "but those on whom He had mercy did not differ," and there is no necessity calling for that. As for «لذلك», what it points to has many views, the most apparent being that it is the disagreement indicated by «مختلفين», like his saying:
2731 - إذا نُهي السَّفيهُ جرى إليه ... وخالفَ، والسَّفيهُ إلى خلافِ
(When the fool is forbidden, he runs to it and opposes, and the fool is inclined to opposition.)
The pronoun in «إليه» returns to foolishness (safah), indicated by the word «السَّفيه»; and an omitted muḍāf is necessary on this view, that is, "and for the fruit of disagreement He created them." The lām in reality is the lām of consequence (ṣayrūra), that is, He created them so that most of them would end up in disagreement. It was also said: what is meant by it is the mercy indicated by «رحم», and it was made masculine in view of its being good. It was also said: what is meant is the two together, and Ibn ʿAbbās leaned to this, like His saying {عَوَانٌ بَيْنَ ذلك} [al-Baqara: 68]. It was also said: it points to what follows it, His saying «وتَمَّت كلَّمة ربك», so there is a fronting and delaying in the speech, which is a weaker view, because the basic rule is the absence of that. His saying «أجمعين» is emphasis, and most often it is preceded by «كل», but here it came without it.
Al-Jinna and al-jinn: it was said that they are one, the tāʾ in it being for intensiveness. It was also said that al-jinna is the plural of jinn, which is strange; it would then be like kamʾ for the plural and kamʾa for the singular.
[Translator's note: the source prints «وتَمَّت كلَّمة ربك» without its opening quotation mark; translated as the verse words.]

semin-durr:120-120.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَكُلاًّ نَّقُصُّ}: in its accusative there are several analyses. One: it is a direct object and the muḍāf ilayhi is omitted, with tanwīn as a substitute for it, the implied form being "and every report We relate to you." «مِنْ أنباء» is an explanation of it or an adjective if the muḍāf ilayhi is supplied as indefinite. His saying «ما نُثَبِّتُ» may be a badal from «كلاً», or the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is, "it is that by which We make firm," or accusative by an implied "I mean."
Two: it is accusative as a maṣdar, that is, "every relating We relate," «مِنْ أنباء» being an adjective or explanation, and «ما نُثَبِّت» being the object of «نَقُصُّ».
Three: as before, except that «ما» is made redundant (ṣila), the implied form being: "We relate every one of the reports of the messengers, by which We make your heart firm." So the Shaykh parsed it, and said: it is like it in His saying {قَلِيلاً مَّا تَذَكَّرُونَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 3].
Four: «كلاً» is accusative as ḥāl from «ما نُثَبِّت», with the sense of "altogether." It was also said: rather it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «به». It was also said: rather it is a ḥāl from «أنباء». These last two analyses are permitted only according to al-Akhfash, who allows the ḥāl of a noun governed by a preposition to precede it, like the saying of the Exalted {والسماوات مَطْوِيَّاتٍ بِيَمِينِهِ} [al-Zumar: 67] in the reading of one who put «مَطْويات» in the accusative, and the saying of another:
2732 - رَهْطُ ابنِ كُوْزٍ مُحْقبي أَدْراعهم ... فيهم ورَهْطُ ربيعةَ بنِ حُذار
(The clan of Ibn Kūz, carrying their coats of mail behind them among them, and the clan of Rabīʿa ibn Ḥudhār.)
The i'rab of the rest of the sūra is clear from what has preceded.

semin-durr:123-123.t: Nāfiʿ and Ḥafṣ read «يُرجع» passive, and the others active. Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ read «تَعْملون» in the second person, because «اعملوا» precedes it, and the others read in the third person, returning to His saying {لِّلَّذِينَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ}. This disagreement also occurs at the end of al-Naml.

semin-durr:27-27.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَا نَرَاكَ}: It may be of the heart (qalbiyya, "we think") or of the eye (baṣariyya, "we see"). On the first, the clause of His saying «اتَّبعك» is in the position of accusative as a second object; on the second, it is in the position of accusative as ḥāl, with «قد» implied according to those who stipulate that.
Al-arādhil: there are two aspects. One: that it is a plural of a plural; the second: only a plural. Those who say the first differed: it was said that it is a plural of «أَرْذُل», and «أَرْذُل» is a plural of «رَذْل», like kalb, aklub and akālib. It was said: rather it is a plural of «أَرْذال», and «أَرْذال» is also a plural of «رَذْل». Those who say that it is not a plural of a plural, but only a plural, said: it is a plural of «أَرْذُل», and it is permissible that it be a plural of «أَرْذُل» only because it is treated like nouns, in that what it qualifies has been abandoned, like al-abṭaḥ and al-abraq. Some of them said: it is the plural of the comparative «أَرْذَل», and it came as a plural as {أَكَابِرَ مُجَرِمِيهَا} [al-Anʿām: 123] and {أحاسِنُكم أخلاقاً} came. One says: a man is radhl and rudhāl, like rakhl and rukhāl, meaning one who is turned away from because of his inferiority.
His saying: {بَادِيَ الرأي}: Abū ʿAmr, of the seven, and ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī read «بادِئَ» with hamza, and the rest with a clear yāʾ in place of the hamza. As for the hamza, its meaning is: "the first of opinion", that is, the first opinion, in the sense that it does not proceed from reflection and consideration, but from the first impression. As for the one who did not use the hamza, it may be that its origin is as already given, and it may be from badā yabdū, that is, "appeared", the meaning being: the outward of opinion, not its inward, that is: had it been considered, its inward would be known; and in meaning it is like the first.
Regarding its accusative on both readings there are seven aspects. One: that it is accusative as an adverb, and regarding its governor on this there are three aspects. One: «نراك», that is: "we do not see you in the first of our opinion", on the reading of Abū ʿAmr, or "in what appears to us of opinion" on the reading of the rest. The second of the three aspects: that it is accusative by «اتَّبعك», that is: "we do not see that those who followed you did so in the first of their opinion, or the outward of their opinion", and this admits two meanings. One: that they mean "they followed you in the outward of their affair, while their inwards are not with you". The second: that they followed you at first glance and with the apparent opinion without deliberation, and had they deliberated, they would not have followed you. The third of the three aspects: that the governor of it is «أراذِلُنا» and the meaning: "our lowly ones, at first glance of theirs, or by the outward opinion, we know that", that is, their lowliness is exposed and apparent because they are people of base trades.
Then the view that «باديَ» is an adverb requires an excuse, for it is an active participle and is not an adverb in origin. Makkī said: "It is permissible for fāʿil to be an adverb only as it is permissible for faʿīl, such as qarīb and malīʾ, and fāʿil and faʿīl alternate, like rāḥim and raḥīm, ʿālim and ʿalīm; and it is good in fāʿil because it is annexed to «الرأي», and a maṣdar is annexed to «الرأي», and the maṣdar with it is accusative as an adverb, such as «أما جَهْدَ رأيٍ فإنك منطلقٌ», that is, «في جَهْد»."
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its accusative is as an adverb; its origin is: 'at the time of the occurrence of the first of their affair', or 'at the time of the occurrence of the outward of their opinion', so that was dropped and the annexed one stood in its place."
The second of the seven aspects: that it be accusative as a direct object, with the preposition dropped with it, like {واختار موسى قَوْمَهُ} [al-Aʿrāf: 155]; so said Makkī. There is something to consider in it, in that there is no verb here fit to be transitive to two objects, to the second of which by dropping the preposition.
The third of the seven: that it be accusative as a maṣdar, and the coming of the maṣdar on fāʿil is also not analogical; and the governor in this maṣdar is like the governor in the adverb, as already given, and it is of the chapter in which the maṣdar comes from the meaning of the verb and not its wording, its implied form being: "a seeing of a beginning or appearance", or "a following of a beginning or appearance", or "a lowliness of beginning or appearance".
The fourth of the seven: that it be an adjective of «بشر», that is: "we see you only as a human like us, apparent in opinion", that is, its outward, or "beginning in it"; there is remoteness in it because of the separation between the adjective and what it qualifies by the conjoined clause. The fifth: that it be a ḥāl from the object of «اتَّبَعَكَ», that is: "and you are exposed in opinion, apparent, with no strength in it and no firmness in you". The sixth: that it be a vocative, Nūḥ, peace be upon him, being meant, as if they said: "O apparent of opinion", that is, what is in your soul is apparent to everyone; they said that by way of mockery of him and belittling him. The seventh: that its governor is implied, its implied form being: "Do you say that, apparent in opinion?"; Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned it, and the basic principle is non-implication when it can be dispensed with. On these last four aspects it is an active participle without interpretation, unlike the preceding aspects, in which it is an adverb or maṣdar.
Know that if you make «باديَ» accusative as adverb or maṣdar by what precedes «إلا», you need an answer to a difficulty, namely that what follows «إلا» cannot be governed by what precedes it, unless it is the one excepted from, like «ما قام إلا زيداً القوم»; or the excepted, like «قام القومُ إلا زيداً»; or a follower of the one excepted from, like «ما جاءني أحدُ إلا زيدٌ أخيرٌ من عمرو»; and «بادي الرأي» is none of these. Makkī said: "If you said in speech «ما أعطيت [أحداً] إلا زيداً درهماً» and so put two nouns as objects after «إلا», it would not be permissible, because the verb does not reach by «إلا» to two objects; it reaches only one noun, like the other particles. Do you not see that if you said «مررت بزيدٍ عمروٍ» so that you made the verb reach both by a single particle, it would not be permissible? And for that reason, if you said «استوى الماءُ والخشبة الحائط», putting two nouns in the accusative with the wāw of "with", it would not be permissible, unless you brought in all of that the wāw of conjunction, in which case the verb's reaching them is permissible."
The answer they gave is that adverbs are given latitude not given to others. This is the sum of what is said on this question, in brief.
And «الرأي» may be from seeing with the eye, or from thought and consideration. And His saying {بَيِّنَةٍ مِّن ربي}: «مِن ربي» is an adjective of «بَيِّنة», that is: "a proof of the proofs of my Lord".

semin-durr:28-28.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {رَحْمَةً مِّنْ عِندِهِ}: It is also permissible for the preposition and its noun to be an adjective of «رحمة» and to be attached to «آتاني».
His saying: {فَعُمِّيَتْ}: The two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) and Ḥafṣ read it with ḍamma on the ʿayn and a doubled mīm, and the rest with fatḥa and a light mīm. As for the first reading, its origin is: "Allah made it obscure to you" (عَمَّاها اللَّهُ عليكم), that is, made it unclear as a punishment for you; then the verb was made passive, so its agent was dropped because it is known, being Allah the Exalted, and the object, which is the pronoun of the mercy, was put in its place. This is indicated by the reading of Ubayy with this origin: «فعماها اللَّهُ عليكم», and it was also reported from him, and from al-Ḥasan, ʿAlī and al-Sulamī: «فعماها» with no verbal agent mentioned; and it was reported from al-Aʿmash and Ibn Wathāb: «وعُمِّيَتْ» with wāw and not fāʾ.
As for the second reading, the verb is ascribed to it figuratively. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what is its reality? I say: its reality is that the proof, as it is made seeing and giving sight, is made blind; for the blind one is neither guided nor guides another; so the meaning of «فَعَمِيَتْ عليكم البَيِّنَةُ» is: it did not guide you, as when the guide of a people in the desert becomes blind to them, they remain without a guide."
It was said: this is of the chapter of inversion (qalb), and its origin is «فَعَمِيْتُم أنتم عنها», as you say: "I put the cap on my head" and "I put the ring on my finger", which is frequent; the verification of the disagreement about it has already been given, and they cited on it:
2654 - ترى الثورَ فيها مُدْخِلَ الظلِّ رأسَه ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . (You see the bull in it, putting its head into the shade …)
Abū ʿAlī said: "This is among what is inverted, since there is no ambiguity, and in the Qurʾān {فَلاَ تَحْسَبَنَّ الله مُخْلِفَ وَعْدِهِ رُسُلَهُ} [Ibrāhīm: 47]"; some of them explain the verse as latitude in the adverb. As for the verse of Ibrāhīm, akhlafa is transitive to two, so you are free to annex to whichever of them you wish, and it is not of the chapter of inversion. Some of them have rejected this verse being of the chapter of the inverted, because had it been so, it would be made transitive by «عن» and not «على»; do you not see that you say «عَمِيْتُ عن كذا» and not «على كذا»?
There was disagreement about the pronoun in «عُمِّيَتْ»: does it refer back to the proof (bayyina), so that His saying «وآتاني رحمة» is a parenthetical clause between the two conjoined elements, since the proper form would be {على بَيِّنَةٍ مِّن ربي. . . فَعُمِّيَتْ}? If it is said that it refers back to the mercy, then something has been omitted from the first, as the second indicates it, the origin being: «على بينة من ربي فَعُمِّيَتْ». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«وآتاني رحمة» by giving the proof, on the basis that the proof is itself the mercy. It may be that by the proof the miracle is meant, and by the mercy prophethood. If you say: His saying «فعُمِّيَتْ» is clear on the first aspect, so what is its aspect on the second, when the proper form would be «فَعَمِيَتَا» (dual)? I say: the aspect is to imply: «فعُمِّيَتْ بعد البينة», or that he dropped it to confine himself to mentioning it once."
End.
The discussion on this «أرأيتم» has already been given in al-Anʿām, and its summary here is that «أَرَأَيْتُم» requires the proof as accusative, and the verb of the condition requires it as genitive with «على», so the second was given effect and a pronoun implied in the first, the implied form being: "Do you see the proof from my Lord, if I am on it, shall we compel you to it?"; so the first object was dropped, the interrogative clause being in the position of the second, and the apodosis of the condition is omitted as indicated.
His saying: {أَنُلْزِمُكُمُوهَا}: Here he brought the two pronouns attached, putting the pronoun of address first because it is more specific; had the third person been brought first, the pronoun would necessarily have been detached. Some have permitted the attachment, and ʿUthmān cited «أراهُمُني الباطل شيطاناً». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is permissible that the second be detached, as in «أَنُلْزِمكم إياها», and the like: {فَسَيَكْفِيكَهُمُ الله} [al-Baqara: 137], and «فسيكفيك إياهم» is permissible." This which al-Zamakhsharī said is the apparent sense of the statement of Sībawayh, although some have forbidden it.
The lengthening of the mīm in the like of this construction is obligatory, and its sukūn is weak, and on it is «أراهُمني الباطل». Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It was read with sukūn on the mīm to avoid the succession of vowels." His saying may mean the sukūn of the mīm of the plural, because he mentioned that after saying: "the wāw entered here as a completion for the mīm, which is the origin in the mīm of the plural, and it was read with sukūn on the mīm." End. This, if established as a reading, is a school of Yūnus, who permits «الدرهمَ أعطيتكمْه», while others refuse it. It may also mean the sukūn of the mīm of the verb, which is indicated by what al-Zajjāj said: "The Basran grammarians agreed that it is not permissible to put sukūn on a vowel of i'rab except in the necessity of poetry; as for what was reported from Abū ʿAmr, the readers did not record it accurately from him; Sībawayh reported from him that he lightened the vowel and pronounced it hurriedly (ikhtilās), and this is the truth; sukūn is permissible only in poetry, such as the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
2655 - فاليَومَ أشرَبْ غير مُسْتَحْقِبٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . (Today I drink, not burdened with sin …)"
So also said al-Zamakhsharī: "It is reported from Abū ʿAmr that he put sukūn on the mīm, and the aspect of it is that the vowel was only a light, hurried one, which the transmitter thought to be sukūn; and plain sukūn is a solecism according to al-Khalīl, Sībawayh and the experts of the Basrans, because the vowel of i'rab may not be dropped except in the necessity of poetry."
I say: al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ reported «أَنُلْزِمْكموها» with sukūn on this mīm, and the discussion of that has already been given at length in Sūrat al-Baqara, I mean putting sukūn on the vowel of i'rab, so how can they make it a solecism?
And «ألزم» is transitive to two, the first the pronoun of address and the second the pronoun of the absent. And {وَأَنتُمْ لَهَا كَارِهُونَ} is a circumstantial clause, which may be for the agent or for one of the two objects. He put the preposition and its noun first on account of the verse-endings. There are irregular readings in the verse that differ from the codex, and I pass over them for that reason.

semin-durr:29-29.t:
The pronoun in «عليه» may refer back to the warning understood from «نذير», or to the religion which is the creed, or to the conveying. «بطاردٍ الذين» was read with tanwīn on «طاردٍ». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "on the original", meaning that the original of the active participle in the sense of present and future is to act (govern), which is the apparent sense of Sībawayh's statement. The Shaykh said: "It could be said: the original is annexation, not governing, because two resemblances have befallen it: one, its resemblance to the imperfect, which is a resemblance to something not of its kind; the other, its resemblance to nouns when annexation is in it, so attaching it to its own kind is more fitting."
And His saying {إِنَّهُمْ مُّلاَقُو} is resumptive, giving the reason. And His saying «تَجْهلون» is an adjective that is indispensable, since bringing this qualified word without its adjective gives no benefit, and he brought it as a verb to indicate renewal at every time.
